A business that bills only for junior human seats is short the exact trend driving its market; pod pricing lets Anvi capture value as AI tooling raises per-engineer output instead of losing revenue as seat counts fall.

recommendations.action: Do not enter the annotation, RLHF or data-labelling segment as a revenue line, and remove annotation from the marketed skill list; keep RLHF and LLM evaluation framed only as capabilities an embedded engineer brings to a client's own product team.
recommendations.why: Mercor reached ~$2bn annualised gross revenue by June 2026 at a $10bn valuation, micro1 went from ~$7m to $500m+ annualised at a reported ~$4bn valuation, and Scale AI did $870m in 2024 — all with capital and AI-lab relationships Anvi cannot match, against India's ~200,000 existing annotators. It is the single most contested and most capital-intensive adjacent market on Anvi's current page.

unverified: Anvi Innovate's own bench size, cohort throughput, placement count, client count, pricing and founder track record — nothing is published on the site and nothing was found elsewhere, so no competitive comparison on scale or proof is possible.

Actual bill rates, markups or HTD programme prices charged by Quess, TeamLease Digital, NLB Services, Alp Consulting, upGrad Rekrut, Andela or Revature. No vendor publishes pricing and no filing discloses per-seat economics; the only figures available (15-35% markup on salary, 8-20% of CTC plus 25-30% statutory, 12-20% margin for IT staffing) come from staffing-vendor blogs and should not be treated as benchmarks.

Revenue, headcount and AI-practice scale for NLB Services, Xpheno, Careernet, Alp Consulting and upGrad Rekrut. LinkedIn employee bands were the only data located; no filings or audited figures were found. upGrad Rekrut's claimed "10M upskilled talent pool" is an unverified marketing figure.

Revature's current revenue, ownership and whether it has any India delivery or recruitment operation. Only an employee-count estimate (1,343, May 2026, Tracxn) and historical model details (10-12 week paid training, two-year commitment, $50-65k salaries) were found, the latter from 2017-era press and Glassdoor reviews.
iMerit's revenue. Sources conflict irreconcilably (~$33m with $24.3m raised versus $1.1bn); neither was traced to a filing.

Cognition/Devin's official current pricing. The pricing page returned 404 at cognition.ai and cognition.com, so all tier and ACU figures come from third-party aggregator blogs and may be stale or wrong.

The claim that AI coding assistants reduce junior developer need by 30-50%, and the figures "junior dev hiring down 35% from 2023" and "new-grad hiring down 50-65% since 2019" (attributed to SignalFire). These were found only in secondary summaries; the underlying SignalFire State of Talent report and the LeadDev survey were not read directly.

Whether any named competitor offers a contractual productivity or ramp SLA. Advertised 7-business-day replacement SLAs with pro-rata exit were found only on an aggregator comparison page, not on a named vendor's own terms, so the "unclaimed SLA" conclusion rests on the absence of such terms on Quess, TeamLease, Revature and Andela pages rather than on confirmed absence across the market.

Hyderabad versus Bengaluru AI engineer salary bands (₹18-28 LPA vs ₹25-40 LPA mid-level) and the ₹60 lakh figure for an 8+ year GenAI engineer. These come from recruitment-vendor blogs and a 1 Finance study reported second-hand; no primary salary survey was accessed.

The PwC-FICCI GCC survey's sample size, methodology and exact publication date — pwc.in returned 403, so all figures (72%, 62%, 27%, 8.69 months) are from CRN Asia's summary. Likewise the EY GCC Pulse Survey figures (81%, 71%, 66%) were not read in the original.

Reconciliation of India's AI/ML talent pool size. Sources quote 506k+ (Zinnov-NASSCOM 2026), ~250,000 and 2.35m "AI professionals" with no shared definition; the true pool of deployable applied-AI engineers is unknown.

Quess Corp's IT staffing segment revenue and margin specifically (as distinct from the ₹15,305 crore consolidated FY26 figure), and whether its HTD business is material. The post-demerger segment disclosure was not located.

The Business Standard articles on GCC hiring versus IT services and on GCC AI reskilling returned 403 and could not be read directly; their figures are reported here only where a second source carried them.

modules.domain: Pricing, margins and unit economics of Indian tech staffing

findings.claim: India's largest listed professional/IT staffing book bills roughly Rs 1.10 lakh per deployed head per month on average, not the premium rates AI marketing implies.
findings.detail: Quess Corp's Professional Staffing segment (IT Services, ITES, CRT, BFSI; GCCs are 67% of revenue) reported FY26 revenue of Rs 930 crore on a closing headcount of 7,066. That is Rs 13.16 lakh per deployed head per year, i.e. ~Rs 1,09,700 per head per month across a mixed-seniority book. An entry-level bench will sit well below this average.
findings.source: Quess Corp Limited, Investor Presentation Q4 FY26

findings.claim: Segment operating profit in that same book is only about Rs 13,100 per deployed head per month, or 11.9% of billing - and that is after a decade of scale, brand and GCC relationships.
findings.detail: Quess Professional Staffing FY26 operational EBITDA was Rs 111 crore on Rs 930 crore revenue (11.9%), i.e. ~Rs 13,090 per deployed head per month on 7,066 heads. Q4 FY26 margin was 12.7%; management guided 11-12% medium term. This is segment operational EBITDA before corporate/IDC allocation, so true company-level margin is lower.
findings.source: Quess Corp Limited, Investor Presentation Q4 FY26
findings.asOf: FY2026 and Q4 FY2026; published May 2026

findings.claim: The second-largest listed player runs the same business at roughly half that: Rs 67,900 revenue and Rs 4,633 EBITDA per deployed head per month.
findings.detail: TeamLease Specialised Staffing Services FY24: revenue Rs 589 crore, EBITDA Rs 40.2 crore (6.8% margin), closing headcount 7,230. Per head per month that is Rs 67,890 revenue and Rs 4,633 EBITDA. FY23 margin was 7.7%. So the realistic India IT-staffing operating-margin band is roughly 7-12%, with per-head monthly contribution of Rs 4,600-13,100.
findings.source: TeamLease Services Limited, Investor Presentation Q4 FY24
findings.asOf: FY2024 and Q4 FY2024; published May 2024
findings.contradicts: Widely-cited staffing blogs quote 35-65% markups and 25-28% gross margins for 'IT staffing'. Those are US figures. Indian listed-company disclosure points to roughly 7-16%, so US markup benchmarks must not be used to build an Indian plan.

findings.claim: Quess management's own cross-check puts India IT-staffing gross margin per head at about 17.5x general-staffing gross margin per head - roughly Rs 12,000 per month.
findings.detail: On the Q4 FY23 call Lohit Bhatia said one head of gross margin in the US business equals about 20 heads in India IT staffing and about 350 heads in India general staffing. With general-staffing gross margin PAPM at Rs 670-700, that implies India IT staffing gross margin of ~Rs 11,700-12,250 per deployed head per month - independently consistent with the Rs 13,090 derived from the FY26 segment accounts.
findings.source: Quess Corp Limited, Q4FY23 & FY23 Earnings Conference Call transcript

findings.claim: General staffing yields only Rs 670-700 gross margin per associate per month, which is why a sub-scale firm has no viable path outside skilled/IT staffing.
findings.detail: Quess reports general-staffing PAPM (per associate per month gross margin) stable at Rs 670-700 across FY23-FY27 calls, rising to Rs 800-1,100 only in manufacturing. Segment EBITDA margin is 1.4-1.5%. TeamLease's consolidated operating margin was 1.2-1.3% in FY25 because 92-94% of revenue is general staffing.
findings.source: Quess Corp Q4FY23 call transcript; Quess Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY26 call summaries; ICRA rating rationale on TeamLease Services
findings.asOf: Q4 FY23 (May 2023) through Q1 FY27 (call 30 July 2026); ICRA report 30 January 2026

findings.claim: Indian IT staffing runs on 'pay-and-collect': the staffing firm pays salaries first and collects from the client later. General staffing's cash-positive 'collect-and-pay' model is not available in this segment.
findings.detail: Frost & Sullivan's market assessment prepared for FirstMeridian's IPO states collect-and-pay (bill, collect, then pay staff) is used 'predominantly in General Staffing only', while pay-and-collect is 'the prevalent model in IT Staffing and Professional Staffing'. Quess confirms the contrast: 76% of its general staffing is collect-and-pay, producing general-staffing AR DSO of 15 days (28 days including unbilled) and consolidated DSO of 24 days in FY26. None of that applies to a pure IT-staffing book.
findings.source: Frost & Sullivan, 'Assessment of Staffing Solutions Market in India', submitted to FirstMeridian (IPO support document); Quess Corp Q4 FY26 Investor Presentation
findings.asOf: Frost & Sullivan report January 2023; Quess DSO data FY2026

findings.claim: Rate-card billing is the convention in Indian IT staffing, but fixed mark-ups are a documented margin trap - the market leader is actively migrating clients to variable mark-up.
findings.detail: Frost & Sullivan lists three billing conventions: fixed fee per head per month (general staffing), rate card / bill rate per hour (the common method in IT and professional staffing), and percentage of the employee's total cost. ICRA's rationales on TeamLease in both November 2024 and January 2026 say margins are expected to improve only through 'the gradual transition of contracts to variable markup, especially with new clients' - i.e. fixed rupee mark-ups get eaten by annual salary hikes.
findings.source: Frost & Sullivan report for FirstMeridian; ICRA rating rationales on TeamLease Digital Pvt Ltd and TeamLease Services Ltd
findings.asOf: Frost & Sullivan January 2023; ICRA 19 November 2024 and 30 January 2026

findings.claim: Indian IT staffing is extremely fragmented with low entry barriers - the top seven named players held just 16.6% share - so pricing is set by the market, not by a differentiation story.
findings.detail: Frost & Sullivan put the India IT Staffing Solutions segment at INR 260 billion in FY2022, forecast to reach INR 546 billion by FY2026 (20.4% CAGR). Market share FY2022: Quess 4.6%, TeamLease 1.7%, FirstMeridian 0.9%, Adecco 1.5%, Randstad 1.7%, ManpowerGroup 2.1%, Genius 4.0%, 'Others' 83.4%. The report attributes this to 'high growth... and low entry barriers'.
findings.source: Frost & Sullivan, 'Assessment of Staffing Solutions Market in India', for FirstMeridian
findings.asOf: FY2022 actuals, FY2026 forecast; report January 2023

findings.claim: IT flexi staffing is the fastest-growing staffing segment in India (+12.3% YoY) even while the overall flexi market slowed to its weakest first quarter since 2020.
findings.detail: Indian Staffing Federation data for Q1 FY26: total flexi staffing grew 6.1% YoY and 1.5% QoQ; IT staffing grew 12.3% YoY and 5.5% QoQ; general staffing 5.8% YoY. The formal contract workforce stood at 1.83 million as of June 2025, with 91,500 net new positions over 12 months. FY25 had grown 9.7% with 1.39 lakh additions on a base of 1.8 million at March 2025.
findings.source: Indian Staffing Federation, reported by Outlook Business and The Hans India
findings.asOf: Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended June 2025); published 7 October 2025

findings.claim: The entry-level AI pay band that a freshly-trained graduate actually maps to is Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh a year, not the Rs 11-13 lakh commanded by proven GenAI engineers.
findings.detail: TeamLease Digital's Digital Skills & Salary Primer splits roles into AI-Core (build and own intelligent systems), AI-Adjacent (data, cloud, security) and AI-Support (monitoring, validation, first-line resolution). Entry-level AI-Core in GCCs is Rs 13.2 lakh; a GenAI Developer at 0-2 years is Rs 11.2 lakh; entry-level AI-Support is Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh. A bootcamp-trained fresher with no production track record prices into the AI-Support band, which implies a bill rate of roughly Rs 55,000-70,000 per month, not Rs 1.2 lakh+.
findings.source: TeamLease Digital, 'Digital Skills & Salary Primer FY2026-27', reported by CIOL and Outlook Business
findings.asOf: FY2026-27 primer, published 29 September 2026; earlier edition reported 28-29 August 2025

findings.claim: There is genuine unmet demand - but the market leader's own diagnosis is that unfilled roles fail on salary expectations, location and skills, which is a different problem from supply of trained freshers.
findings.detail: TeamLease reports it can fill only about 30% of client openings, citing mismatches on salary expectations, location preferences and required skills. Separately it estimates a 53% talent supply gap in GenAI and 55-60% in cloud, and roughly one qualified engineer per ten open GenAI roles. Reconciling those: clients are short of proven mid-level people at an acceptable price, which does not automatically convert into willingness to pay for unproven juniors.
findings.source: Reuters via Yahoo Finance; TeamLease Digital reports via SMEStreet and Deccan Herald
findings.contradicts: The '53% GenAI talent gap' headline and the '30% fill rate due to salary and location mismatch' explanation point in different directions: the gap is not purely a training-supply gap.

findings.claim: Skilled/IT staffing needs roughly one internal employee per 22 deployed contractors - sixteen times the overhead ratio of general staffing. This, not the mark-up, is what kills small operators.
findings.detail: TeamLease's Q4 FY24 core-headcount breakdown shows 320 core employees supporting 7,230 Specialised Staffing associates (1:22.6), while Staffing and Degree Apprenticeship ran 829 core employees for 311,800 associates (FTE productivity 371:1). Quess reported a general-staffing associate-to-core-FTE ratio of 270:1 in Q4 FY26 and 1:500+ in FY23.
findings.source: TeamLease Services Limited, Investor Presentation Q4 FY24; Quess Corp Investor Presentation Q4 FY26

findings.claim: A well-capitalised incumbent entering IT staffing in a new market burned Rs 11 crore in one year and set 'a few hundred deployed resources' as its medium-term goal before scale economics worked.
findings.detail: On the Q4 FY23 call Quess disclosed Rs 11 crore of full-year investment in its North America professional/IT staffing build-out (Rs 3 crore in Q4 alone), with EBITDA breakeven as the immediate-year goal and 'steadily go beyond a few hundred deployed resources' as the medium-term goal. For a bootstrapped operator the implication is that breakeven in IT staffing is a tens-to-low-hundreds-of-heads problem, not a ten-heads problem.
findings.source: Quess Corp Limited, Q4FY23 & FY23 Earnings Conference Call transcript

findings.claim: GST of 18% applies to the entire invoice value of contract staffing - salary plus mark-up - and is payable on invoice date, not on collection.
findings.detail: Contract staffing / manpower supply falls under SAC 998513 at 18% GST. The taxable value includes the service charge per deployed employee, the mark-up on salaries, administrative fees and reimbursable costs forming part of consideration. For a firm billing Rs 1 lakh per head where ~Rs 87,000 is pass-through salary cost, the GST liability is on the full Rs 1 lakh, creating a cash float of roughly 18% of gross billing for the period between invoice and collection. A body corporate charges forward; a proprietorship or partnership supplying a registered recipient triggers reverse charge.
findings.source: ClearTax and multiple GST practice guides on SAC 998513 / manpower supply

findings.claim: The four Labour Codes in force from 21 November 2025 raise cost-to-company for exactly this business model: fixed-term employees now earn gratuity after one year, and the 50% wage rule widens the PF/gratuity/bonus base.
findings.detail: Under the Social Security Code read with the IR Code, fixed-term employees get parity in wages and benefits, proportionate statutory benefits, and 'gratuity benefits if they render service for at least 1 year under the contract' (previously five years). Separately, if excluded allowance components exceed 50% of total remuneration, the excess is deemed wages and added back for PF, gratuity, bonus, leave encashment and notice pay. Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas states employers 'will have to assess the cost impact consequent to engagement of fixed term employees'. On top of base statutory load - employer EPF ~13% including EDLI and admin, ESIC 3.25% up to Rs 21,000 wages, gratuity ~4.81%, statutory bonus minimum 8.33% - this is a direct, structural margin event for a contract-staffing P&L priced on fixed mark-ups.
findings.source: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, 'A Guide to The New Labour Codes: What you need to know'

findings.claim: The OSH Code introduces a core-activity prohibition on contract labour plus contractor licensing - a procurement and legal objection this business will face, with a specific carve-out it must be able to point to.
findings.detail: The OSH Code sets a unified threshold of 50 or more contract labour for applicability, allows manpower-supplying contractors to obtain a work-specific licence or a national licence for multi-state work, and newly prohibits principal employers from engaging contract labour in the establishment's core activities (previously restricted only in a few states such as Telangana and Andhra Pradesh). Crucially, persons 'regularly employed by, and are paid wages and provided benefits by, the contractor' are expressly excluded from the definition of 'contract labour'. The Code also makes welfare obligations the principal employer's primary responsibility and attaches liability to the principal employer where the contractor is unlicensed - which is why client legal teams will interrogate payroll and licence status.
findings.source: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, 'A Guide to The New Labour Codes'

findings.claim: Section 80JJAA is a real, proven cash subsidy for staffing firms employing people at or below Rs 25,000 a month - TeamLease received a ~Rs 115 crore refund under it.
findings.detail: Section 80JJAA allows a deduction of 30% of additional employee cost for three consecutive assessment years, for new employees with emoluments not exceeding Rs 25,000 per month, employed at least 240 days in the year and participating in a recognised provident fund. It survives the concessional corporate tax regimes under sections 115BAA/115BAB. ICRA records that TeamLease received an income-tax refund of ~Rs 115 crore (including Rs 6.5 crore interest) for AY 2023-24 pertaining to 80JJAA, and had ~Rs 240 crore of 80JJAA-related refunds outstanding at 30 September 2024 - though the department has disallowed its FY2019 claim and reopened FY2017, so the claim is litigated.
findings.source: ICRA rating rationale, TeamLease Digital Private Limited; ClearTax / Tax2win on s.80JJAA
findings.asOf: ICRA report 19 November 2024; 80JJAA provisions as at AY 2025-26
findings.contradicts: 80JJAA is sometimes described as limited to manufacturing. The ICRA record of TeamLease's claims and refunds shows pure staffing businesses do claim it, but the Income Tax Department's disallowance of TeamLease's FY2019 claim shows it is contested.

findings.claim: Section 43B(h) gives a Udyam-registered micro or small supplier a hard legal lever on client payment terms: pay beyond 45 days and the client loses the tax deduction that year.
findings.detail: Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act denies the buyer a deduction for amounts payable to a micro or small enterprise unless paid within the time under section 15 of the MSMED Act - 15 days without a written agreement, or the agreed period capped at 45 days. The deduction then shifts to the year of actual payment. It applies only to suppliers registered as micro or small on the Udyam portal, not to medium enterprises. Commentary notes the provision migrates to section 37 under the Income-tax Act, 2025.
findings.source: ClearTax on Section 43B(h); taxupdate.in on its migration to s.37 of the Income-tax Act 2025
findings.asOf: Effective from AY 2024-25; migration commentary dated 2026

findings.claim: A minimum-service bond with liquidated damages is enforceable in India after the Supreme Court's May 2025 ruling - but the case upheld Rs 2 lakh against a salaried bank officer, not a recovery model against unemployed freshers.
findings.detail: In Vijaya Bank v. Prashant B. Narnaware (decided 14 May 2025) the Supreme Court upheld a clause requiring a selected candidate to serve three years or pay Rs 2 lakh in liquidated damages, holding it was not a restraint of trade under section 27 of the Contract Act and not against public policy, because it did not prevent the employee from resigning or taking other employment but gave the employer a mechanism to recover its investment. The facts matter: a public-sector bank, a promoted internal candidate, a recruitment notification disclosing the term upfront, and damages actually paid.
findings.source: Supreme Court of India via Indian Kanoon; analysis by Cyril Amarchand/Mondaq and Bar & Bench

findings.claim: The Employment Linked Incentive scheme pays an employer up to Rs 3,000 per month per additional employee for two years - a direct, time-limited subsidy to a hire-train-deploy P&L, but only for jobs created up to 31 July 2027.
findings.detail: The Cabinet approved the ELI Scheme on 1 July 2025 with an outlay of Rs 99,446 crore. Part B incentivises employers up to Rs 3,000 per month for two years for each additional employee with sustained employment of at least six months (extended to years 3 and 4 for manufacturing). Part A pays first-time EPFO-registered employees one month's EPF wage up to Rs 15,000 in two instalments (at 6 and 12 months, the second conditional on a financial literacy programme), for employees earning up to Rs 1 lakh. Benefits apply to jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027. At India IT-staffing gross margins of roughly Rs 5,000-13,000 per head per month, Rs 3,000 per month is a material fraction of contribution per head.
findings.source: Press Information Bureau / EPFO press release on Cabinet approval of the ELI Scheme
findings.asOf: Cabinet approval 1 July 2025; scheme window 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027

recommendations.action: Delete the AI-training-dataset statistic (USD 8.60bn by 2030) from the site. It is the data-annotation market and has nothing to do with talent supply. Replace it with the India IT staffing segment size and growth - INR 260bn in FY2022 forecast to INR 546bn by FY2026 at 20.4% CAGR (Frost & Sullivan) - plus ISF's IT flexi staffing growth of 12.3% YoY in Q1 FY26 against 6.1% for flexi staffing overall.
recommendations.why: Citing the annotation market signals to any buyer who checks that the team has not read its own market. The ISF and Frost & Sullivan numbers say the same encouraging thing and are defensible, and the ISF datapoint also shows IT staffing outperforming a slowing overall market.

recommendations.action: Build an internal price book before the first sales call, priced as a percentage of the deployed engineer's fully-loaded cost-to-company, never as a fixed rupee fee per head, with an explicit annual CTC-revision pass-through clause in the MSA. Set the target mark-up band from Indian evidence (roughly 12-18% on cost for entry-level, higher only for scarce lateral skills), not from US blog markups of 35-65%.
recommendations.why: Quess's FY26 professional staffing book earns ~11.9% segment operating margin and TeamLease's 6.8-7.7%; ICRA records that fixed mark-up contracts are precisely what has capped TeamLease's margins and that the fix is migrating clients to variable mark-up. A fixed rupee fee signed in year one gets eaten by the first salary revision and by the Labour Code wage-base expansion.

recommendations.action: Re-band the bench honestly on the website. Present the fresher cohort against TeamLease Digital's AI-Support band (Rs 4.8-5.4 LPA CTC, implying a bill rate of roughly Rs 55,000-70,000 per head per month) and reserve AI-Core / GenAI-engineer language for laterals with production track records. Price the nine tracks into two or three bands rather than nine equal-looking tracks.
recommendations.why: TeamLease Digital's own primer puts a GenAI Developer at 0-2 years at Rs 11.2 lakh and entry-level AI-Core in GCCs at Rs 13.2 lakh, while entry-level AI-Support is Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh. Marketing nine AI role tracks off a bootcamp bench invites buyers to price you at AI-Core and then discover AI-Support, which costs the account. Nine tracks at one unproven quality bar also reads as unfocused to a GCC buyer.

recommendations.action: Size and fund the working-capital gap before signing the first deployment, and model it explicitly: monthly payroll out, client cash in at 45-60 days, plus 18% GST on gross billing payable by the 20th of the following month. For 50 deployed heads at Rs 50,000 cost each this is roughly Rs 50-60 lakh of receivables plus a Rs 5-6 lakh monthly GST float. Then register on Udyam as a micro/small enterprise and put a 45-day payment term plus a Section 43B(h) reference into every MSA and invoice.
recommendations.why: Frost & Sullivan is explicit that IT and professional staffing run on pay-and-collect, unlike general staffing's cash-positive collect-and-pay - Quess's 24-day consolidated DSO is a general-staffing artefact and is not reachable here. Section 43B(h) makes a client's own tax deduction conditional on paying a Udyam-registered micro/small supplier within 45 days, which is the single strongest negotiating lever a small vendor has on payment terms with a large client.

recommendations.action: Impose a hard bench rule before any cohort starts: no training cohort begins without a stated number of signed or committed mandates, and a maximum bench window (for example 60 days) per trainee with a defined exit. Track cost-per-bench-month and months-of-margin-to-recover as a standing metric.
recommendations.why: At Rs 5,000-13,000 of gross margin per deployed head per month (TeamLease FY24 and Quess FY26 segment accounts), one month of an unbilled trainee at even Rs 25,000 fully-loaded consumes two to five months of a billed head's entire contribution. Bench days, not mark-up, are what decide whether this business survives - and the 'deploy in days from a pre-trained bench' promise structurally creates bench.

recommendations.action: Shift the recovery mechanism from the candidate to the client. Put a conversion/buyout fee in every contract-to-hire MSA, and keep candidate-side commitments to a cost-linked minimum-service agreement: hire onto payroll first, document actual training cost per head, set liquidated damages at no more than that documented cost, disclose the term in the offer letter before acceptance, and taper it to zero over the service period.
recommendations.why: Vijaya Bank v. Prashant B. Narnaware (SC, 14 May 2025) upholds minimum-service bonds with liquidated damages, but the facts that carried it were upfront disclosure in the recruitment notification and a salaried employee who could actually pay. Recovery against an unemployed fresher is practically worthless and reputationally expensive in a candidate-supply business, whereas a client-side conversion fee is collectable from a creditworthy counterparty.

recommendations.action: Engineer the statutory and incentive stack into the price model rather than treating it as back-office: keep trainee and early-deployment emoluments at or below Rs 25,000 per month across a 240-day window to qualify for Section 80JJAA (30% of additional employee cost, three years), register for ELI Part B (up to Rs 3,000 per month per additional employee for two years, for jobs created before 31 July 2027), and surface ELI Part A to candidates as a joining benefit. Quantify each as basis points of per-head margin in the plan.
recommendations.why: At Rs 5,000-13,000 gross margin per head per month, Rs 3,000 of ELI Part B is 25-50% of contribution per head, and 80JJAA is worth roughly 7.5% of the qualifying wage bill in cash tax at a 25% rate. ICRA records TeamLease receiving a ~Rs 115 crore 80JJAA refund, so this is real money in staffing - but the ELI window closes 31 July 2027, and the department has disallowed some of TeamLease's 80JJAA claims, so documentation discipline from day one is the condition of collecting.

recommendations.action: Staff and budget to a 1:20-to-1:25 core-to-deployed ratio and publish an internal break-even number. Working arithmetic: a three-person core team plus rent, tooling and compliance at roughly Rs 3.5-4 lakh per month fixed needs about 35-45 billed heads at Rs 10,000 gross margin per head per month to break even - and about 55-70 once a 20% unbilled bench is carried. Treat anything below 25 deployed heads as pre-revenue, not as a business.
recommendations.why: TeamLease ran 320 core employees for 7,230 specialised staffing associates (1:22.6) while its general staffing ran 1:371 - skilled staffing cannot be run on general-staffing overhead assumptions. Quess invested Rs 11 crore in one year entering IT staffing in a new market and set 'a few hundred deployed resources' as its medium-term goal, so a plan that assumes profitability at ten heads is not supported by any disclosed Indian comparable.

recommendations.action: Add a short compliance and contracting page aimed at client legal and procurement: state that deployed engineers are Anvi's own payroll employees with EPF, ESIC and gratuity, that Anvi holds (or has applied for) the relevant OSH Code contractor licence including a national licence if deploying across states, confirm GST registration and SAC 998513 invoicing, and state the position on the OSH Code core-activity prohibition.
recommendations.why: From 21 November 2025 the OSH Code prohibits principal employers from engaging contract labour in core activities and makes the principal employer primarily liable for welfare obligations and liable where the contractor is unlicensed - so a client deploying your engineers into its own engineering team has a live legal question. The Code's exclusion of persons 'regularly employed by, and paid wages and provided benefits by, the contractor' from 'contract labour' is the answer, but only if you can evidence own-payroll employment. Procurement will ask; having no answer on the site costs deals before the first call.

recommendations.action: Replace 'deploy in days, not months' with a measured, auditable metric and do not publish it until there are at least ten completed mandates: median calendar days from signed requirement to candidate joining, stated with the sample size. Instrument this from the first mandate.
recommendations.why: An unsubstantiated speed claim is the easiest thing for a GCC buyer to test and the easiest to lose the account over, and the site currently has no case studies, SLAs or placement numbers to back it. TeamLease's disclosure that it fills only ~30% of client openings - on salary, location and skill mismatch rather than speed - shows that fill rate and quality, not raw speed, are the metrics buyers actually negotiate on.

unverified: Published bill rates or rate cards for contract AI/ML and data engineers in India by experience band. No primary rate-card source was found. Every figure located is candidate CTC (TeamLease Digital's primer) or company-level revenue per deployed head (Quess, TeamLease segment accounts). Bill rates in this answer are derived from those two, not quoted.

Cost to train one person in an Indian hire-train-deploy programme. No provider (NIIT StackRoute, TalentSprint, Quess, mthree) discloses a per-trainee cost. All market their programmes as zero upfront cost to the hiring enterprise, which means the training cost is absorbed and recovered through billing - but the amount is undisclosed. A widely-repeated 'Rs 30,000 to Rs 1.5 lakh per hire' figure appears only in vendor blogs and is cost-per-hire, not cost-to-train.

Bench cost per month and average time to first deployment for Indian HTD providers. No disclosed benchmark found. The only adjacent datapoint is Frost & Sullivan's statement that 25-30% of an Indian IT services company's own employees sit on bench awaiting deployment, which is a client-side metric, not a staffing-bench metric.

Conversion and buyout fee conventions for contract-to-hire in India. The commonly quoted 8.33% of annual CTC (one month's salary) rising to 12.5-16.67% for senior roles, and 3-6 month pre-conversion periods, appear only in recruitment-agency marketing blogs. No industry body, filing or survey was found. Treat as folklore until tested in negotiation.

Typical contractual payment terms and DSO specifically for Indian IT/professional staffing. Quess discloses consolidated DSO (24 days FY26) and general staffing AR DSO (15 days, 28 including unbilled revenue), but both are dominated by the collect-and-pay general staffing book. No company discloses professional or IT staffing DSO separately. The structural point (pay-and-collect) is verified; the number of days is not.

Lock-in period enforceability in practice against freshers. Vijaya Bank v. Prashant B. Narnaware establishes that minimum-service bonds are not void under section 27, but no data was found on quantum actually awarded against junior employees, on how courts apply section 74 (reasonable compensation rather than the stipulated sum) to training bonds, or on recovery rates. Assume low practical recoverability.

The revised MSME classification turnover and investment limits applicable from 1 April 2025, which determine for how long Anvi qualifies as micro or small and can therefore rely on Section 43B(h). This needs confirmation from the MSME Ministry notification before the clause is relied on in an MSA.

Whether Section 80JJAA and Section 43B(h) survive in the Income-tax Act, 2025 (effective 1 April 2026) and under what section numbers. One commentary says 43B(h) migrates to section 37. This must be confirmed with a chartered accountant before either is built into the financial model.

Statutory employer cost loading as a precise percentage. The components are individually sourced (employer EPF ~13% including EDLI and administrative charges, ESIC 3.25% up to Rs 21,000 wages, gratuity accrual ~4.81%, statutory bonus minimum 8.33%), but the aggregate '10-20% over gross salary' comes from employer-of-record vendor guides, not a government source. The Labour Code 50% wage rule changes the base these are applied to, and the net effect on a specific salary structure needs to be computed, not assumed.

The claim that Quess's India professional staffing gross margin per associate per month is about Rs 14,300. This appears in an earnings-call summary but could not be confirmed in a primary transcript. The figure is directionally consistent with the Rs 13,090 per head per month derived from Quess's FY26 segment accounts, but it is reported here only as a cross-check, not as a verified disclosure.

NASSCOM primary data on FY2026 net hiring, entry-level intake and AI talent demand. The web search budget for this session was exhausted before NASSCOM's Strategic Review could be retrieved, so demand-side sizing here rests on Indian Staffing Federation and TeamLease Digital data only.

modules.domain: How enterprises and GCCs actually buy contract tech talent

findings.claim: At large Indian enterprises, buying contract IT talent is a two-stage process: you must first win empanelment through an open EOI, after which actual work is awarded only in closed tenders among the already-empanelled pool.
findings.detail: SBI's RFP for procurement of IT-Human Resources states on its cover: "This is a closed RFP and participation in this RFP is by invitation only." Eligibility criterion 1 is simply "The Bidder should be the Empaneled Bidder under the Category III pursuant to the EOI", evidenced by "Copy of the Empanelment Letter issued by the Bank". A non-empanelled vendor cannot bid at all, regardless of capability or price.
findings.source: State Bank of India (RFP dated 01.11.2025, for contract 1 Jan 2026 – 31 Dec 2027)
findings.asOf: RFP issued 1 November 2025; contract period 1 Jan 2026 – 31 Dec 2027

findings.claim: Once inside the empanelled pool, IT staffing work is awarded by online reverse auction to the lowest bidder (L1) — not on speed, quality or bench readiness.
findings.detail: The same SBI RFP schedules a "Reverse Auction" as a listed event, and states "The Bidder will be selected as L1 on the basis of net total of the price evaluation as quoted in the Reverse Auction" and "Among all qualified bids, the lowest bid (as quoted in reverse auction) will be termed as L1." Shortlisted bidders must agree to participate. Speed-to-deploy is not a scored commercial variable at this stage.
findings.source: State Bank of India (closed RFP / limited tender enquiry for IT-Human Resources)
findings.contradicts: Anvi's headline differentiator "deploy in days, not months" is not a variable that this award mechanism prices; it only matters after price selection.

findings.claim: Empanelment is a long-lived licence, awarded in windows that open only every 2–5 years — miss the window and there is no route in.
findings.detail: IDBI: "The empanelment of the selected vendors is for five years from date of signing of LOI", extendable by one further year, with yearly performance review and possible de-empanelment. Union Bank of India's ITCSSP empanelment runs 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2027 (two years). PNB Cards & Services: "The Empanelment will be for 03 (Three) Years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2028-29." A vendor that is not ready when the EOI is published waits years.
findings.source: IDBI Bank (RFP ref IDBI-Bank/ITD/VMG/RFP/22-23/21); Union Bank of India (RFP No. UBI/ITCSSP/NOVEMBER/2024); PNB Cards & Services Ltd (PNBCSL/RFE/HR/2025/07)
findings.asOf: IDBI 29-Jun-2022; UBI Nov 2024 for FY2025-27; PNBCSL 2 December 2025 for FY2026-29

findings.claim: After empanelment, rates are discovered once and then competed down: the standard models are lowest-price bid, maximum discount on an already-discovered person-day rate, or nomination.
findings.detail: IDBI defines three engagement models for empanelled vendors: (a) Price Model — "The vendor quoting the lowest prices shall be selected"; (b) Person-Days Model — "For given N person-days or person-months, resource cost will be arrived based on the discovered prices through this RFP, say the cost is Y. Vendors will be asked to quote the discount percentage on Y... The vendor quoting the maximum discount on Y shall be selected"; (c) Nomination Model for urgent work. Rate cards are therefore set at empanelment and eroded thereafter.
findings.source: IDBI Bank, RFP for Empanelment of IT Service Providers

findings.claim: The technical scoring matrices structurally penalise a vendor with no completed purchase orders: roughly 43% of marks are allocated to counts of past assignments, before capability is assessed at all.
findings.detail: Union Bank of India's 150-mark technical matrix allocates: 25 marks for number of BFSI assignments in India (1 mark per PO), 20 marks for BFSI assignments globally (2 marks per PO), 20 marks for special security-incident assignments, 20 marks for three-year average turnover banded from ₹8–50 cr (5 marks) up to >₹500 cr (20 marks), 15 marks for counts of certified L1/L2/L3 resources, 10 marks for years of experience, 10 for certifications, 10 for technical credentials, 20 for presentation. A new vendor forfeits ~65 of 150 marks on past-PO counts alone and scores the minimum turnover band. Shortlisting thresholds are "Premium – Technical Score 75% and above; Non-Premium – above 50% and below 75%".
findings.source: Union Bank of India, RFP No. UBI/ITCSSP/NOVEMBER/2024

findings.claim: Manpower-supply empanelment at a bank subsidiary now requires ₹25 crore turnover, ₹1 crore average PAT, three years in the business and 1,000 people already placed — gates a pre-revenue vendor cannot clear.
findings.detail: PNB Cards & Services Ltd eligibility criteria: in the manpower-services business for banks/FIs/insurers/PSUs/MNCs/large corporates "for at least 3 years"; "An annual gross turnover of at least Rs.25 crores in any of one year within last 3 years"; "average net profit after tax of at least Rs. 1.00 crore for the last 03 audited financial years viz. 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25"; "should have supplied manpower of minimum no. of 1,000" to banks/FIs/insurers/PSUs; multi-state GST registrations as proof of multi-state presence; "a certified copy of License from Labour Commissioner to employ Contract Labour under Contract Labour Act"; no blacklisting by any PSB, RBI or IBA. Canvassing about shortlisting status "will amount to disqualification".
findings.source: PNB Cards & Services Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of Punjab National Bank), RFP PNBCSL/RFE/HR/2025/07
findings.asOf: RFP issued 2 December 2025; bids due 2 January 2026

findings.claim: IT-services empanelment gates are lower than manpower-supply gates but still require ~₹10 crore average turnover, three years of positive net worth and 12 certified full-time staff held for three years.
findings.detail: IDBI's eligibility compliance sheet requires: "annual average turnover of Rs.10 crore (Rs.5 crore for MSE) towards Information Technology Service in the past three financial year"; "positive Net Worth in the past three financial years"; in the ITSP business "for a minimum period of 3 (three) years"; "a pool of full time minimum 12 professionals possessing any of the certification given in CERTIFICATIONS employed with them for the last 3 years" (multiple certificates counted once); and no blacklisting by Govt bodies/PSB/PSU "during the last five years" with a self-declaration of no pending vigilance, court, inquiry or investigation matters.
findings.source: IDBI Bank, RFP for Empanelment of IT Service Providers, Annexure-17

findings.claim: Some empanelments impose a hard 10-year-existence gate plus three consecutive years of EBITDA profit and a minimum permanent headcount — an absolute bar, not a scoring penalty.
findings.detail: Union Bank of India pre-qualification: bidder "should be in existence for last 10 years as on 30.09.2024"; "minimum annual turnover of Rs.8 Crores during the last three financial years... It should be individual company turnover and not that of any group of companies"; "should be in operating-profit (EBITDA) during last three financial years"; "minimum 30 permanent employees as on 30.09.2024" of which 5 must hold CISA/CISM/CISSP; presence in both Mumbai and Hyderabad; EMD ₹4,00,000. Scope is IT/cyber-security services and consulting rather than pure staffing, but the shape of the gate is representative of BFSI empanelment.
findings.source: Union Bank of India, RFP No. UBI/ITCSSP/NOVEMBER/2024, Annexure-C
findings.asOf: Criteria as on 30 September 2024; RFP November 2024

findings.claim: MSME and DPIIT-startup registration is the one documented concession that materially lowers these barriers — it halves turnover thresholds and waives earnest money.
findings.detail: IDBI sets the turnover gate at "Rs.10 crore (Rs.5 crore for MSE)" and references the Public Procurement Policy for Micro & Small Enterprises Order 2012 (Gazette notification 23.03.2012, amended S.O. 5670(E) dated 9 November 2018), with NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme certificate plus Udyam/Udyog Aadhaar as proof; traders are not eligible. Union Bank: "In case of bidders registered with NSIC/Udyog Aadhaar as MSME or a Start-up Company, they are eligible for waiver of EMD" — startups via a DPIIT Certificate of Recognition, plus a CA-signed declaration. The MSE must still meet all other criteria.
findings.source: IDBI Bank RFP Annexure-17; Union Bank of India RFP clause 12.2.2
findings.asOf: UBI November 2024; IDBI 29 June 2022; policy order 23.03.2012 as amended 09.11.2018

findings.claim: Enterprise requisitions for technology contractors set a relevant-and-current experience floor of around 4+ years, with documentary proof of duties — which excludes freshers from the requisition line items entirely.
findings.detail: SBI's Appendix-E role specification requires "4 + Years Relevant and Current Experience", a BTech/BE in Computer Science (or PGDM/MBA plus BE/BTech/MCA/BCA/BSc in CS/IT), "mandatory IT working Background on IT Projects" and 4+ years in Banking/Financial Institutions/Corporate, with the footnote: "The previous experience letter should explicitly mention the nature of duties performed by the resource." Training to upskill deployed resources is the vendor's cost: "the same shall be taken up by the Service Provider and no cost shall be borne by the Bank".
findings.source: State Bank of India, closed RFP for IT-Human Resources, Appendix-E
findings.contradicts: Anvi's core supply is trained fresh graduates and career-switchers; the requisition text here makes prior paid project experience documentary and non-waivable.

findings.claim: The client, not the vendor, controls selection and the replacement economics; substitution terms are punitive and make a thin bench a financial liability.
findings.detail: SBI terms: the bank interviews every resource and "the decision of Bank to onboard the resource will be final and binding on the Service Provider"; unsuitable CVs must be replaced within 3 working days with at least as many additional CVs, else the PO can be cancelled; shortlisted resources must report within 15 days; if unsatisfactory within 15 days of joining the bank may demand replacement and "no payment shall be made for the period"; no substitution in the first 3 months; on attrition, 45 days' notice plus "CVs of a minimum 200%... of total number of resource(s) to be substituted", maximum 2 substitutions per role, one month of knowledge transfer and "The Bank will not make payment for the substitution resource during transition and knowledge transfer period." Absence without approval is penalised at twice the hourly rate.
findings.source: State Bank of India, closed RFP for IT-Human Resources, Appendix-I "Other Terms and Penalties"

findings.claim: Background verification and police verification are contractual deliverables with 7-day and 90-day clocks, and subcontracting is prohibited.
findings.detail: SBI: "Service Provider will submit BGC (Background Check) as per the prescribed format of the Bank and PVR (Police Verification Report) applied for copy within 7 (seven) days of boarding of resources. Police Verification Report duly issued by Police authorities shall be submitted within 90 (ninety) days of onboarding"; biometrics captured at onboarding for attendance. Separately: "As per the scope of this RFP, sub-contracting is not permitted." UBI and GIL similarly bar consortium bids ("Any kind of consortium will not be allowed").
findings.source: State Bank of India closed RFP; Gujarat Informatics Ltd RFP (consortium bar)
findings.asOf: SBI 1 November 2025; GIL tender P&A-201718/04 dated 2017

findings.claim: The cash-flow structure is pay-first, bill-later: the staffing vendor must fund payroll before the client pays, and payment is conditional on proof of statutory remittances.
findings.detail: Gujarat Informatics Ltd: "Payment shall be made within 20 days of the submission of the bill" but only on submission of "challans for having made payments of the statutory deductions like P.F. Professional Tax, ESIC contribution" for the previous month — "If such copies have not been submitted, then the reimbursement/ payment of bill will not be" made; and "the agency will have to make payment to the manpower provided within 7 days from the end of the month irrespective of the pending payment from GIL." SBI pays "not exceeding 30 (thirty) days" after invoice receipt, monthly in arrears. Quess reports General Staffing DSO of 28 days with AR stable at 15 days at Q1 FY27.
findings.source: Gujarat Informatics Ltd (RFP for Empanelment of Agencies for Providing Outsourced Manpower); State Bank of India; Quess Corp Q1 FY27 investor presentation
findings.asOf: GIL tender P&A-201718/04, 2017; SBI 1 Nov 2025; Quess quarter ended June 2026
findings.contradicts: The GIL document is from 2017, so the 20-day term should not be read as current market practice; the structural point (vendor funds payroll first, payment gated on statutory challans) is corroborated by the SBI 30-day arrears term and Quess's 28-day DSO.

findings.claim: Insurance cover is an onboarding requirement with a defined floor, not a nice-to-have, and must be evidenced on demand.
findings.detail: IDBI clause 45 requires the bidder to "take out and maintain at their own cost" and, on request, "provide evidence... showing that such insurance has been taken out and maintained": third-party motor vehicle liability under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988; third-party liability "with a sufficient coverage for the period of the Contract"; "Professional liability insurance, with a minimum coverage equal to estimated remuneration and reimbursable"; and "Employer's liability and workers' compensation insurance in respect of the personnel of the Bidder", plus life/health/accident/travel cover as appropriate.
findings.source: IDBI Bank, RFP for Empanelment of IT Service Providers, clause 45

findings.claim: GCCs are overwhelmingly the buyer of Indian IT contract staffing: at India's largest staffing firm, GCCs account for 71% of professional-staffing headcount and 68% of segment revenue.
findings.detail: Quess Corp Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) Professional Staffing: "GCC contributing 71% of headcount with 68% of revenue contribution"; segment headcount 7,129 (+7% YoY), revenue ₹252 cr, EBITDA ₹28 cr (11.0% margin, down from 12.8% in Q4 FY26); "Added 36 contracts during the quarter"; "Open mandates at 1,100+ primarily in niche and high value roles". Client concentration in Q1 FY27 was Top 10% of clients = 40% of revenue, next 40% = 50%, others 10%.
findings.source: Quess Corp Limited, Investor Presentation Q1 FY27

findings.claim: The scale needed to serve that GCC demand is a 450-recruiter, 300-client, 80-city delivery engine, and the unit economics are ~₹1.18 lakh average monthly billing per deployed associate on ~22% gross margin.
findings.detail: Quess IT Staffing & Solutions: "delivering skilled IT talent and managed technology solutions to 300+ enterprises across 80+ cities", ~7,000 associates deployed, "450+ Specialist IT recruiters", 800+ technology skill domains, "30K+ Monthly talent outreach". Professional Staffing revenue of ₹252 cr over 7,129 associates implies ~₹3.53 lakh per associate per quarter, i.e. ~₹1.18 lakh per associate per month. Quess states "Gross margin to EBITDA margin conversion remains above 50%" on an 11.0% EBITDA margin, implying segment gross margin around 20–22%. Group EBITDA margin was 2.02% in Q1 FY27.
findings.source: Quess Corp Limited, Investor Presentation Q1 FY27 (segment pages and company profile slides)

findings.claim: The IT staffing segment is the slowest-growing part of a flat Indian staffing market — it grew 2% quarter-on-quarter against 2.6% for general staffing.
findings.detail: Indian Staffing Federation research page, Q1 2026-27: overall staffing industry grew 7.5% year-over-year; ISF members represent a formal flexi workforce of 1.95 million; 1.14 lakh new formal flexi jobs added over 12 months; quarter-over-quarter growth 2.6% in General Staffing and 2% in IT Staffing. ISF's own forward projection is for the flexi workforce to reach ~9.16 million by FY27 from 7.2 million in FY25.
findings.source: Indian Staffing Federation (industry body), Research page / Flexi Staffing Employment Trends Report Q1 2026-27
findings.asOf: Q1 FY2026-27 (quarter to June 2026), page read 7 October 2026

findings.claim: Hyderabad is the right city for this business: it reportedly accounts for 40% of all new GCC setups in India, against India hosting 1,700 of the world's 3,200 GCCs.
findings.detail: NASSCOM-hosted article: "1700 out of 3200 centres globally" are in India and "60% of them lead product development or deep analytics mandates"; "Hyderabad now accounts for 40% of all new GCC setups in India", with Tier-2 cities clocking 21% YoY hiring growth; India has "over 120,000 AI / ML professionals and over 185 dedicated AI/ML COEs"; GCCs projected to contribute 2% of India's GDP and 2.8 million jobs by 2030; GCCs leased a record volume of office space in early 2026.
findings.source: nasscom.in Voices — Aditi Jha, Executive Director & Country Head, Legal & Government Affairs, LinkedIn India (community contribution with NASSCOM disclaimer)

findings.claim: The dominant competitor to a train-and-deploy vendor is the GCC's own internal reskilling programme, which is reported as 2.5x cheaper than external hiring.
findings.detail: Same NASSCOM-hosted source: "78% of GCCs are already reskilling internal teams for GenAI adoption. Upskilling a current employee costs 2.5 times less than hiring externally. And employees with high internal mobility stay 60% longer." It concludes that the constraint is no longer hard AI skills — "LinkedIn Economic Graph data reveals that between 2019 and 2025, the country's AI talent concentration has grown by 120%, with AI literacy at 4.7x the global average" — but the applied/human-skills layer, with "6% or fewer employees in India's GCC workforce" holding those capabilities.
findings.source: nasscom.in Voices — Aditi Jha, LinkedIn India (community contribution; LinkedIn Economic Graph and WEF cited within)
findings.contradicts: This cuts against the premise that GCCs must buy externally-trained AI talent. It also suggests a scarcity claim built on 'hard AI skills' is weaker than one built on applied/judgement capability.

findings.claim: The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025 with central rules notified in May 2026, so compliance evidence demanded at vendor onboarding is in flux — and the cost impact is already material at scale.
findings.detail: Law-firm analysis: "The Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, with central rules notified in May 2026, while State-level implementation continues in a phased manner." Quess Corp's Q1 FY27 General Staffing commentary records a "One time increase in revenue of 176 crs due to labor code impact", confirming a real and quantified cost/billing effect on staffing vendors in the quarter.
findings.source: Paritosh Chauhan and Shylla Sawhney, Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan, published via Mondaq, 3 September 2026; Quess Corp Investor Presentation Q1 FY27
findings.asOf: Codes in force 21 November 2025; central rules May 2026; Quess quarter ended June 2026

findings.claim: GCC legal and HR gate staffing vendors on co-employment risk: the contract must carry labour-law compliance obligations, indemnities, audit rights and access controls, and deployed staff must be visibly separate from GCC employees.
findings.detail: Law-firm guidance for GCCs in India states that vendor contracts should "contain labour-law compliance obligations, indemnities, audit rights and access-control obligations", and that the GCC must "maintain a clear distinction between vendor employees and GCC employees in reporting lines, email domains, system access and HR processes". It flags that where "the GCC supervises day-to-day work, controls attendance, assigns tasks directly" and integrates vendor staff into internal teams, authorities may treat the arrangement as disguised employment rather than genuine outsourcing. IP does not transfer by default: "payment for work does not automatically mean ownership of IP", so written assignment from contractor personnel is required.
findings.source: Paritosh Chauhan and Shylla Sawhney, Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan, via Mondaq

findings.claim: The buying centre differs by what is being bought — HR owns off-roll manpower, IT vendor-management owns IT services, the CISO owns security — so there is no single door into an enterprise.
findings.detail: PNB Cards & Services names the "Chief People Officer" as Empanelment/RFP Coordinator for off-roll manpower supply (hr@pnbcsl.co.in; cpo@pnbcsl.co.in). IDBI's IT-service-provider empanelment carries the reference IDBI-Bank/ITD/VMG/RFP/22-23/21, i.e. IT Department / Vendor Management Group. Union Bank's ITCSSP empanelment is issued from the "CISO OFFICE... Hyderabad". SBI's IT-HR RFP routes through its IT procurement process with a mandatory interview by the business unit.
findings.source: PNBCSL RFP PNBCSL/RFE/HR/2025/07; IDBI RFP ref IDBI-Bank/ITD/VMG/RFP/22-23/21; Union Bank of India RFP UBI/ITCSSP/NOVEMBER/2024
findings.asOf: PNBCSL 2 December 2025; IDBI 29 June 2022; UBI November 2024

findings.claim: Verifiable RFP-to-revenue windows at large Indian buyers run roughly 2 to 5 months from RFP publication to contract start, on top of a wait of up to several years for the window to open.
findings.detail: PNBCSL: RFP issued 2 December 2025, bids due 2 January 2026, bid validity 90 days, empanelment effective FY2026-27. Union Bank: RFP dated November 2024 (criteria as on 30.09.2024), empanelment effective 01.04.2025. SBI: closed RFP dated 1 November 2025 for a contract commencing 1 January 2026, with resources required to report within 15 days of communication. These are the documented clocks for an already-qualified bidder; a vendor that must first become empanelled adds the full EOI cycle plus the gap to the next window.
findings.source: PNB Cards & Services; Union Bank of India; State Bank of India tender documents

findings.claim: The Government e-Marketplace is a genuinely lower-barrier channel that produces the dated purchase orders enterprise scoring matrices reward.
findings.detail: GeM lists dedicated service categories including "Manpower Outsourcing Services - Minimum wage", "Manpower Outsourcing Services - Fixed Remuneration" and "Security Manpower Service (Version 2.0)", among 350 service categories and 10,671 product categories, with cumulative order value shown as ₹21,31,529 crore. Sellers self-register at mkp.gem.gov.in. Because empanelment scoring at banks awards 1–2 marks per past purchase order, GeM orders convert directly into future eligibility points.
findings.source: Government e-Marketplace (GeM), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

findings.claim: The NASSCOM/NSDL National Skills Registry is the industry's shared background-verification spine but is narrower than often assumed — only 337 subscriber companies.
findings.detail: The NSR portal, backed by NASSCOM and operated with NSDL, reports 37,22,697 web registrations, 25,86,677 IT Professional Identification Numbers generated, 337 subscriber companies joined, and 25 empanelled background checkers. It maintains a "List of Empanelled Background Checkers" used for employment screening. No as-of date is printed on the page.
findings.source: National Skills Registry (NASSCOM / NSDL)
findings.asOf: Figures as displayed 7 October 2026; no publication date on page

findings.claim: The share of GCC roles filled on contract is reported to be rising from about 1 in 5 to 1 in 4, heading toward 1 in 3 by FY27 — but the sourcing chain for this number is weak.
findings.detail: A staffing-software vendor's resource page states that "1 in 5 GCC roles in India was contractual" two years ago, is "now 1 in 4", and is projected "closer to 1 in 3" by FY27, citing Staffing Industry and Quess Corp's Q4 FY26 GCC Trends Report; it separately cites "Flexible staffing in GCCs rose to 25% in Q4 FY26, up from 22% in 2025" to a third-party blog, and C2H claims (15–20% higher retention, 40–50% faster onboarding) to the Quess report. None of these primary reports were obtainable directly.
findings.source: Ceipal (staffing software vendor resource page), citing Quess Corp Q4 FY26 GCC Trends Report and others
findings.asOf: Claims refer to Q4 FY26 and FY27 projection; page read 7 October 2026
findings.contradicts: The two figures quoted on the same page for the same period differ (1 in 4 vs 25% up from 22%), and both reach the reader through a vendor page rather than the underlying report. Treat the direction as credible and the level as unverified.

recommendations.action: Before approaching any enterprise buyer, complete three registrations that are the only documented concessions in these procurement rules: Udyam registration, NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme, and DPIIT Startup Recognition. Put the certificate numbers on the website footer and in the vendor pack.
recommendations.why: IDBI sets the turnover gate at ₹10 crore but ₹5 crore for an MSE, and Union Bank waives the ₹4 lakh EMD for NSIC/Udyog Aadhaar MSMEs and DPIIT-recognised startups (with a CA-signed declaration). These are the only mechanisms found that move a hard eligibility number for a small vendor.

recommendations.action: Drop direct PSU-bank and large-enterprise empanelment from the year-one plan and state internally that it is a year-three goal. Instead target (a) Hyderabad mid-market and new-entrant GCCs that have not yet built a vendor panel, and (b) Tier-1 IT services firms and already-empanelled staffing vendors, selling them trained candidate supply onto their payroll — not sub-deployment.
recommendations.why: PNBCSL requires ₹25 crore turnover, ₹1 crore average PAT and 1,000 people already placed; Union Bank requires 10 years of existence and 30 permanent employees. Anvi cannot clear these. And SBI's contract states "sub-contracting is not permitted", so positioning as a sub-supplier under someone else's PSU contract is not available either — the supply must be onto the partner's own payroll.

recommendations.action: Assemble a single downloadable "Vendor Onboarding Pack" PDF and publish it behind an email gate on the site: CIN, registered address, PAN, GSTIN (one per state of deployment), EPFO and ESIC codes with the latest ECR challans, Contract Labour (R&A) contractor licence, three years of audited financials plus a CA net-worth certificate, non-blacklisting affidavit, authorised-signatory board resolution, and certificates for professional indemnity, employer's liability / workmen's compensation and cyber liability. Name the legal entity on every page.
recommendations.why: Every document in that list is a named line item in the RFPs reviewed — PNBCSL demands the Labour Commissioner CLRA licence and multi-state GST certificates; IDBI clause 45 requires professional liability cover "equal to estimated remuneration" plus employer's liability and workers' compensation, evidenced on request. The site today shows no legal entity, CIN, registered address or certification at all, so a procurement reader cannot even start a vendor record.

recommendations.action: Replace "deploy in days, not months" as the hero claim with the three things procurement actually scores, published as hard numbers even when small: cumulative purchase orders / assignments completed (with client type and dates), count of full-time certified employees on roll, and years of operation. Add three named, contactable client references with project start and end dates.
recommendations.why: Union Bank's 150-mark matrix gives roughly 65 marks to counts of past assignments at 1–2 marks per purchase order, 20 to turnover band, 15 to certified-resource counts and 10 to years of experience — and SBI requires "At least 3 client references" with start and end dates. Speed-to-deploy appears nowhere in that matrix, and the award itself is a reverse auction.

recommendations.action: Split the nine role tracks into two commercial products: (1) Hire-Train-Deploy sold to the client's own capability/academy programme, where no experience floor applies and the client is buying a trained cohort; and (2) experienced contract staffing for requisitions, where Anvi must place 4+ year profiles. Stop implying that a fresher bench satisfies a standing requisition.
recommendations.why: SBI's Appendix-E requires "4 + Years Relevant and Current Experience" with an experience letter that "should explicitly mention the nature of duties performed". A fresher bench cannot be submitted against such a requisition at any price, so the two offers need different buyers, different collateral and different proof.

recommendations.action: Model the cash cycle and secure a committed payroll facility of roughly 60–75 days of fully-loaded cost per deployed cohort before signing the first contract; state the funding source in the vendor pack. Build the monthly compliance-evidence pack (PF/ESIC/PT challans, salary register, salary slips) into the invoicing workflow from day one.
recommendations.why: The GIL terms require the agency to pay deployed staff "within 7 days from the end of the month irrespective of the pending payment", with the client's own payment gated on production of PF/PT/ESIC challans; SBI pays within 30 days monthly in arrears; and Quess — at 469k headcount — runs 28-day DSO. A vendor that cannot fund one to two payroll cycles unaided will breach before it is paid.

recommendations.action: Price the service for an 18–22% gross margin and publish a per-track rate band with the statutory loading itemised separately from the service margin. Rehearse a reverse-auction floor price per track and write it down before the first negotiation.
recommendations.why: Quess's professional staffing segment runs 11.0% EBITDA with "gross margin to EBITDA margin conversion remains above 50%" (implying ~20–22% gross margin) and average billing of about ₹1.18 lakh per associate per month; SBI awards IT-HR work at L1 in an online reverse auction. Entering those rooms without a pre-agreed floor is how small vendors win unprofitable work.

recommendations.action: Register as a GeM service provider under "Manpower Outsourcing Services" and bid for small, dated orders in the first two quarters, explicitly to manufacture a verifiable purchase-order history.
recommendations.why: Empanelment scoring at banks awards 1–2 marks per past purchase order and demands "Work Order/Client Letter/Job Completion certificate" as proof. GeM accepts self-registration and lists these exact service categories, making it the cheapest documented route from zero POs to a scoreable track record.

recommendations.action: Remove the Grand View Research "USD 8.60 billion by 2030" statistic from the site and replace it with talent-market numbers a GCC or procurement reader recognises: Quess's disclosure that GCCs are 71% of its professional-staffing headcount and 68% of segment revenue; ISF's Q1 FY2026-27 IT staffing growth of 2% QoQ against 7.5% YoY overall; and Hyderabad's reported 40% share of new GCC setups.
recommendations.why: The cited figure is the AI training-dataset (data-annotation) market, not the talent market. A procurement or GCC reader who knows the sector will treat the mismatch as evidence the vendor does not understand what it is selling, which discredits the rest of the page — including the credible PwC and Naukri figures already on it.

recommendations.action: Publish a two-page "Compliance and Engagement Model" note covering principal-employer obligations under the Contract Labour (R&A) Act, the scope of Anvi's contractor licence, separation of reporting lines / email domains / system access, audit rights, IP assignment executed with every deployed engineer, indemnity position, and insurance limits. Have counsel confirm it against the Labour Codes as the state rules land.
recommendations.why: Law-firm guidance for India GCCs states vendor contracts must carry "labour-law compliance obligations, indemnities, audit rights and access-control obligations" and that the GCC must keep vendor staff distinct in "reporting lines, email domains, system access and HR processes", with IP requiring written assignment. The Codes came into force on 21 November 2025 with central rules in May 2026 and phased state rollout, so this is live diligence territory — and Quess booked a one-time ₹176 crore revenue effect from the Codes in the June 2026 quarter.

unverified: Which MSP and VMS platforms Indian GCCs actually run (SAP Fieldglass, Beeline, Magnit, Allegis Global Solutions, Randstad Sourceright etc.), what share of GCC contingent spend flows through an MSP/VMS rather than direct vendor panels, and whether tier-2 supplier slots on those programmes are open to new vendors. No primary source obtained; web search budget was exhausted before this could be researched. This is the single largest gap in this domain and should be re-run.

Named decision-maker and influencer titles at private GCCs (contingent workforce programme manager, category sourcing manager, TA lead, engineering hiring manager, InfoSec, legal) and the actual approval chain. Only PSU proxies were verifiable: PNBCSL routes manpower empanelment through the Chief People Officer, IDBI through ITD/Vendor Management Group, Union Bank through the CISO Office.

Realistic sales-cycle length in months for a new vendor at a private-sector GCC. Only PSU RFP-to-contract windows could be dated (roughly 2–5 months for an already-qualified bidder), which is a proxy, not a measurement of a new vendor's first-revenue timeline.

The GST rate and SAC code applicable to manpower supply / staffing services (commonly stated as 18% under SAC 9985). The CBIC rate page now redirects to a separate portal and the notification could not be confirmed.

Telangana-specific requirements: state Contract Labour (R&A) Rules thresholds and fees, Shops & Establishments registration, Telangana labour department licence processing time, and whether the Labour Codes' state rules are notified in Telangana as of October 2026.
The claim that average Indian staffing agency margins fell from about 15% in FY19 to about 10% in FY25 — seen only in vendor/SEO content, with no primary or company-filing corroboration.

The level (not direction) of contingent penetration in GCC roles. Figures of "1 in 4 GCC roles contractual", "25% in Q4 FY26 up from 22%" and "1 in 3 by FY27" all reach the reader through a software vendor's page citing Quess Corp's Q4 FY26 GCC Trends Report; the underlying report was not obtainable and two of the figures are internally inconsistent.

The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules notification date and compliance timeline, and the specific data-processor obligations a staffing vendor takes on when handling candidate data for a GCC. The MeitY data-protection page returned HTTP 403.

Typical rupee limits GCCs demand for professional indemnity, cyber liability and employer's liability cover from staffing vendors. Only IDBI's formula was verifiable (professional liability "equal to estimated remuneration and reimbursable"), not market-standard sums insured.

Whether specific large Hyderabad GCCs currently have open vendor-registration portals, their published prequalification thresholds, and whether any run a dedicated small/diverse-supplier track. Not researched.

The ISF Q1 FY2026-27 figures were read from the Indian Staffing Federation's research landing page summary rather than the underlying report PDF, so the exact definitions behind "7.5% YoY" and "2% QoQ IT staffing" are unconfirmed.

Whether Anvi Innovate is currently registered as a private limited company, has GST/EPFO/ESIC registrations or a CLRA contractor licence. The website shows no CIN, registered address or legal entity name beyond the trading name, so none of the eligibility gaps above could be assessed against its actual filings.

modules.domain: Buyer objections, trust signals and risk reversal

findings.claim: Mainstream enterprise/government IT staffing rate cards have no zero-experience band at all — the lowest 'Junior' tier already assumes 12–36 months of experience.
findings.detail: North Carolina's statewide IT Supplemental Staffing solicitation (IFB ITS-009440) defines four skill levels: Junior = 12–36 months, Mid = 36–60, Senior = 60–84, Expert = 84+ months, and rate cards (e.g. Junior Developer/Programmer $48.29–$51.68/hr) are priced against those bands. A fresher with zero months does not map to any category a buyer's procurement system can raise a task order against.
findings.source: North Carolina Statewide IT Procurement Office (IFB ITS-009440), document read directly
findings.asOf: Contract and skill-level table as published (open enrolment cycle beginning 1 Sep 2016, contract in force since); retrieved Oct 2026

findings.claim: The remedy buyers actually write into staffing contracts is unilateral removal plus free replacement — not a refund, not a guarantee window.
findings.detail: NC IFB reserves the Agency's right to 'refuse access to or require replacement of any such personnel for cause, including, but not limited to, technical or training qualifications, quality of work'; Attachment G para 5(b)–(c) says the State 'reserves the right to disapprove the continuing assignment of Vendor personnel' and that the vendor 'will provide suitable personnel at no additional cost to the State.' Guarantees framed as refunds answer a question buyers are not asking.
findings.source: North Carolina Statewide IT Procurement Office (IFB ITS-009440), §5.2 and Attachment G

findings.claim: Indian public-sector manpower contracts hardcode a 2-day replacement SLA and per-day financial penalties; this is the baseline commercial risk reversal an Indian buyer already assumes.
findings.detail: The GeM Manpower Outsourcing Services SLA sets: non-deployment by the joining date = 1% per day of total value for up to 15 days (2%/day at second instance), then cancellation with 10% cancellation charges; absence >2 days = substitute within 2 days, failing which 1%/day (3%/day at second instance); poor performance = 'immediately replace'; theft/misconduct = replacement within 2 days; and termination if cumulative penalties reach 10% of contract value or any SLA is breached more than 3 times.
findings.source: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) Manpower Outsourcing Services SLA, as published by Dept. of Finance, Govt. of Puducherry
findings.asOf: GeM standard service SLA document, retrieved Oct 2026

findings.claim: Indian buyers expect a documented per-candidate compliance dossier, and certifying a candidate's qualifications falsely is a contractual breach with legal consequences.
findings.detail: The GeM SLA requires the provider to certify each resource's biodata, qualifications and experience with documentary proof — 'In case any of such document is found to be false at any stage, it would be deemed to be a breach of terms of contract' — plus police verification certificate, Aadhaar copy, identity and residence proof at deployment, and a photo ID card within 8 days of joining. It also requires the provider to pre-assess candidates on 'educational qualification, work experience, skill assessment, pre-interviewing, short-listing'.
findings.source: GeM Manpower Outsourcing Services SLA §4.3, §5

findings.claim: Statutory-compliance evidence is a hard payment condition in Indian manpower contracts, not a trust nicety.
findings.detail: Under the GeM SLA, EPF/ESI claims in bills 'shall be necessarily accompanied with the documentary proof' and 'a requisite portion of the bill/whole of the bill amount will be held up till such proof is furnished'; EPF/ESI (employer and employee share) must be deposited by the 15th of the month; delay in take-home pay or PF/ESI deposit attracts Rs 100/day (first instance), Rs 200/day plus payment hold (second), then cancellation with 10% charges.
findings.source: GeM Manpower Outsourcing Services SLA §5, §8 penalty table

findings.claim: The SLAs buyers actually measure staffing vendors on are submission quality and early attrition — not training quality or curriculum.
findings.detail: NC IFB §6.1 sets: ≥75% qualified candidates submitted; <5% of selected staff who either fail to start or leave within 2 weeks of assignment start; <5% negative attrition at any point in the placement; 95% timesheets on time. Non-conformance in a single quarter triggers a written root-cause analysis within 10 calendar days, a State-approved cure plan implemented within 10 days, monthly monitoring, and removal from the contract for continued failure.
findings.source: North Carolina Statewide IT Procurement Office (IFB ITS-009440), §6.1–6.2

findings.claim: Peer-reviewed meta-analytic evidence shows years of experience barely predicts job performance (ρ = .07), while structured interviews (.42), job-knowledge tests (.40) and work samples (.33) predict strongly.
findings.detail: Sackett, Zhang, Berry & Lievens's revised matrix (Table 3) gives: structured interviews .42, job knowledge tests .40, empirically keyed biodata .38, work sample tests .33, cognitive ability .31, integrity .31, assessment centres .29, unstructured interviews .19, job experience in years .07 (down from .18 in Schmidt & Hunter 1998), years of education .10. This is the strongest available rebuttal to a buyer's '3+ years only' filter — but it only works if the vendor can show structured-interview and work-sample scores.
findings.source: Journal of Applied Psychology (Sackett, Zhang, Berry & Lievens), doi 10.1037/apl0000994
findings.asOf: Published 2022; Table 3 compares against Schmidt & Hunter (1998)

findings.claim: A structured job tryout is the highest-validity selection device in the legacy evidence base (.44), well above reference checks (.26) — which argues for a paid trial as the primary risk-reversal instrument.
findings.detail: In the same comparison table, 'job tryout procedure' is listed at .44 and 'reference checks' at .26 among procedures Sackett et al. excluded from the revised matrix for insufficient information (both figures are Schmidt & Hunter 1998 / Hunter & Hunter 1984 estimates, not revised). Treat the magnitudes as directional, but the ordering — try the person on the work beats asking someone about them — is consistent with how buyers behave.
findings.source: Journal of Applied Psychology (Sackett et al. 2022), Table 3 'excluded for insufficient information'
findings.asOf: Figures originate in Schmidt & Hunter (1998); reproduced 2022
findings.contradicts: These two figures were deliberately NOT re-estimated by Sackett et al. (2022) because of insufficient data, so they are not on the same methodological footing as the .42/.40/.33 figures above.

findings.claim: In B2B, hands-on trial is the single most influential proof asset — far more than vendor-authored content — and vendors systematically under-supply it.
findings.detail: TrustRadius 2024 B2B Buying Disconnect (2,164 verified technology buyers, 243 vendors): 40% of buyers used a free trial and 74% of those called it the most influential resource in their research; demos were used by 54% of buyers (67% at enterprise level) with 71% of users calling them most influential; own prior experience 52% (influential for 71%). Free trials did not appear in vendors' top five marketing tactics.
findings.source: TrustRadius, 2024 B2B Buying Disconnect Report (PDF read directly)

findings.claim: Over half of buyers — 71% at enterprise level — talk to an existing customer before buying, and vendors underestimate this by ~20 points.
findings.detail: TrustRadius 2024: 56% of buyers (71% enterprise) sought out a peer conversation while vendors estimated 34%. The 2025 edition (2,058 buyers, 490 vendors, published 8 Apr 2025) found 54% of buyers engaged in user conversations against a 38% vendor estimate, and 77% consulted user reviews. For Anvi this is the binding constraint: with zero referenceable clients, the most used late-stage validation channel is simply unavailable.
findings.source: TrustRadius 2024 report; TrustRadius 2025 ninth annual report via PR Newswire
