findings.claim: Hiding pricing is a documented buyer grievance, and ROI arithmetic is what enterprise buyers say they most want made easier.
findings.detail: TrustRadius 2024: 51% of buyers said 'I wish all vendors had transparent pricing'; 47% of enterprise buyers said they wished it were easier to calculate ROI; 66% chose the product they bought because it met their needs at the best price. Anvi's site currently publishes neither price bands nor any ROI comparison against direct hiring or incumbent agencies.
findings.source: TrustRadius, 2024 B2B Buying Disconnect Report

findings.claim: Buying third-party analyst validation is a low-yield trust play: analyst-report usage has fallen to a seven-year low of 16%.
findings.detail: TrustRadius 2024 lists as a headline finding that over seven years user-review usage stayed flat while analyst-report usage 'reached a historically low 16% — the lowest it has been in seven years and consistently trending down.' Spend that would go to an analyst listing is better spent on a trial, a published rubric and referenceable pilots.
findings.source: TrustRadius, 2024 B2B Buying Disconnect Report

findings.claim: Relying on referrals is now a weaker strategy in professional services, and firms consistently overrate how well-known they are.
findings.detail: Hinge Research Institute's Inside the Buyer's Brain research (1,900+ buyers and 3,610 sellers of professional services) finds fewer than 60% of buyers now ask for referrals — a 15% decrease — while nearly 60% of buyers rate their vendor highly on reputation but only about 23% consider that vendor well known. Buyers value a reputation for producing results more than sellers assume.
findings.source: Hinge Research Institute / Hinge Marketing
findings.asOf: Inside the Buyer's Brain, third edition research programme (edition dates not stated on the summary page)

findings.claim: CV-validation discrepancies run at 12.80% in the Indian IT sector, which makes an unqualified 'pre-screened bench' claim a liability rather than an asset.
findings.detail: AuthBridge's Workforce Fraud Files for H1 FY26 reports an overall white-collar discrepancy rate of 4.33% (gig 5.61%), with CV-validation discrepancies highest in IT at 12.80%, employment-history discrepancies at 11.15%, address 7.68%, education 4.49% and reference checks 4.17%. A buyer's default assumption is that roughly one submitted profile in eight contains a material inaccuracy.
findings.source: AuthBridge Workforce Fraud Files, reported by The Tribune (India)

findings.claim: Candidate identity fraud is now an explicit procurement risk: Gartner projects one in four candidate profiles worldwide will be fake by 2028.
findings.detail: Gartner's widely reported prediction is that by 2028, 1 in 4 candidate profiles will be fake; a 2Q25 Gartner survey of 3,000 candidates found 6% admitted to interview fraud (posing as someone else or having someone pose for them). Trade analysis of 19,368 live interviews between July 2025 and January 2026 reported 38.5% showing AI-cheating behaviour. A bench vendor that cannot attest identity and proctoring inherits this suspicion.
findings.source: Gartner prediction as reported by Staffing Hub (Gartner's own release not retrieved)
findings.asOf: Gartner prediction for 2028; survey 2Q25; interview analysis Jul 2025–Jan 2026
findings.contradicts: The 38.5% interview-cheating figure comes from a vendor dataset reported in trade press, not from Gartner, and should not be presented as the same source.

findings.claim: The deployment economics of a fresher bench are running against the market: Indian IT fresher intake fell from ~600,000 (FY22) to ~250,000 (FY23) and kept falling, and bench tolerance has collapsed to 30–45 days.
findings.detail: Outlook Business cites Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital, for fresher hiring of 6 lakh in FY21-22 falling to 2.5 lakh in FY22-23 and continuing down; top-five IT firms' net headcount was -70,000 in FY24 and +9,500 in FY25; TCS now requires associates to maintain 225 billable business days in 12 months, with unallocated periods averaging 30–45 days versus a historical 80–90. Buyers will ask who funds Anvi's bench and will doubt that an idle pre-trained bench exists at all.
findings.source: Outlook Business

findings.claim: Stated employer intent to hire freshers for AI roles conflicts sharply with observed entry-level hiring, so Anvi cannot lean on 'employers want freshers' survey data without being contradicted.
findings.detail: TeamLease EdTech's Career Outlook Report put over 74% of Indian employers as planning to hire freshers for AI-related roles in H1 FY25, while a Nomura analysis reported about 55% of Indian IT companies recording lower entry-level hiring versus 14% for senior roles, and the entry-level share of sector hiring falling from 28% (2024) to 15% (2025). Intent surveys and actual requisitions point opposite ways.
findings.source: TeamLease EdTech Career Outlook Report via IBEF; Nomura analysis via Indian trade press
findings.asOf: TeamLease: H1 FY25; Nomura/sector share figures: 2024–2025
findings.contradicts: 74% stated fresher-hiring intent versus 55% of IT firms actually reducing entry-level hiring and entry-level share halving from 28% to 15% — both cannot describe the same market, and neither primary report was retrieved.

findings.claim: The category leader in hire-train-deploy wins without putting client logos on its homepage — it publishes counts, rates, commercial terms and third-party awards instead.
findings.detail: Revature publishes 25,000+ engineers trained, '200+ Leading Enterprises, Government Agencies, and System Integrators', 15+ years, named university partnerships, and 2025 Brandon Hall HCM Excellence (two gold, one silver), Stevie and Great Place to Work validations. Its programme page states zero upfront cost, an FTE conversion path with 'zero-obligation timing', <5% performance-related attrition with mentoring, 70% faster time-to-productivity, 40–55% lower year-one TCO, 3–10 week client-specific training, 200+ hours of free prep, and 0–24 month post-deployment coaching — with one anonymised client case (50% increase in use-case identification, 40% reduction in AI hiring costs).
findings.source: Revature (company website, pages read directly)

findings.claim: Selling into large accounts carries a managed-service tax and not-to-exceed rate caps that must be priced in before any guarantee is offered.
findings.detail: Under NC's ITSS programme, awarded vendors pay a 4.0% IT Supplemental Staffing administrative fee plus a 1.96% MSP vendor fee, both on billable hours, and both are inside the not-to-exceed rates — a $90.00 vendor hourly rate bills to the State at $95.36. A vendor funding free replacement and trial periods out of margin needs to know roughly 6% comes off the top in MSP/VMS-mediated accounts.
findings.source: North Carolina Statewide IT Procurement Office (IFB ITS-009440), §5.5–5.6

findings.claim: Buyers formally require conversion terms to be stated up front in staff-augmentation RFPs, so an undefined contract-to-hire path is a disqualifier rather than a negotiating advantage.
findings.detail: NYSERDA's Staff Augmentation and Payroll Services RFP 3525 reserves the right to convert a candidate to full-time staff and requires the proposer to 'identify conditions, timelines and fees associated with converting a resource.' Anvi markets contract-to-hire but publishes no conversion conditions, timeline or fee basis.
findings.source: NYSERDA, RFP 3525 Staff Augmentation and Payroll Services
findings.asOf: RFP 3525 (document date not confirmed; retrieved Oct 2026 via search index)

findings.claim: India's four labour codes came into force on 21 November 2025, raising both the compliance proof buyers will demand and the true cost of carrying a bench.
findings.detail: The Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Relations Code 2020, Code on Social Security 2020 and OSH Code 2020 commenced 21 Nov 2025: fixed-term employees get the same wages, hours and statutory benefits as permanent staff; gratuity eligibility for fixed-term workers drops from five years to one; full-and-final settlement must be completed within two working days; penalties for non-compliance rise sharply. Central and several State rules were still not notified at commencement, so buyers' questionnaires will probe readiness rather than certificates.
findings.source: Legal 500 India employment update; corroborated by BDO India and HSF Kramer alerts

findings.claim: The addressable comparison set is a ~USD 5.6bn Indian IT flexi-staffing market of ~663,000 workers — the market statistic Anvi should be citing instead of the data-annotation figure.
findings.detail: Indian Staffing Federation data reported in trade press puts Indian IT flexi staffing at USD 4.9bn (about Rs 40,580 crore) employing 597,000 people in FY ending March 2024, rising to about USD 5.6bn and 663,000 workers by FY ending March 2026; the wider flexi workforce is projected to reach 9.16 million by FY27 from 7.2 million in FY25. Citing the AI training-dataset market instead signals to any informed buyer that the vendor has not sized its own market.
findings.source: Indian Staffing Federation data reported by The Week; ISF growth figures via Staffing Industry Analysts
findings.asOf: FY2024 actual, FY2026 projection (report published 14 Nov 2024); FY27 projection

recommendations.action: Replace 'deploy in days, not months' with a published, signable Deployment & Replacement Commitment that mirrors the clauses Indian buyers already sign: named resource on site within N business days of a signed requisition; free replacement within 2 business days of a written removal request for any reason including 'technical or training qualifications, quality of work'; no invoice for the removed resource's final week; and a no-fee exit in the first 30 days.
recommendations.why: Buyers' contractual remedy is removal plus free replacement at no additional cost (NC IFB Attachment G para 5), and the GeM SLA already fixes a 2-day replacement norm with 1%/day penalties — so a vague speed claim with no replacement clause reads as less protection than the buyer's own standard template.

recommendations.action: Publish a Proof Pack page in place of client logos, carrying only numbers Anvi can defend with records: cumulative trained, currently on bench by track, median days from requisition to on-site, 30-day and 90-day stick rate, replacement rate, and negative-attrition rate — each with its definition, the measurement window, and a stated audit path (CA-certified statement, or client-attestable on request). Follow the Revature pattern: counts, rates, commercial terms and third-party validations, no logos.
recommendations.why: Revature leads the HTD category publishing 25,000+ trained, 200+ clients and <5% performance-related attrition without naming clients on its homepage, while NC's SLA shows buyers measure vendors on exactly these metrics (≥75% qualified submission, <5% early loss, <5% negative attrition). Defined metrics are the substitute a logo-less vendor can actually produce.

recommendations.action: Convert the screening claim into a published assessment rubric: structured interview guide, job-knowledge test blueprint, and a scored work-sample task per track, with band definitions and a sample redacted candidate scorecard plus the candidate's work-sample artefact (repo, notebook, runbook). Cite the validity hierarchy explicitly in sales material to reframe the 'minimum 3 years' filter.
recommendations.why: Sackett et al. (2022, Journal of Applied Psychology) puts years of job experience at ρ=.07 against structured interviews .42, job-knowledge tests .40 and work samples .33 — this is the only evidence-based argument that moves a buyer off an experience bar, and it only lands if Anvi can show those instruments exist and are scored.

recommendations.action: Offer a structured 10-working-day paid tryout as the headline commercial instrument: one engineer, a defined scope agreed in advance, priced at or below cost, with a written go/no-go on day 10, no conversion obligation, and a stated fee basis if they continue. Make it the primary CTA alongside the hiring-request form.
recommendations.why: Free trials were the most influential resource for 74% of the buyers who used one (TrustRadius 2024, n=2,164), and job tryout is the highest-validity selection device in the legacy matrix at .44 versus .26 for reference checks. For a vendor with no references, a tryout is the only proof asset that does not depend on past clients.

recommendations.action: Build a downloadable Buyer Due-Diligence Pack: entity and GST/PAN details, insurance, monthly EPF/ESI challan evidence protocol, a labour-codes readiness note (fixed-term parity, one-year gratuity, two-working-day full-and-final), the per-candidate document set (biodata certified by Anvi, police verification, Aadhaar, ID card within 8 days), the named BGV partner, and a false-credential indemnity.
recommendations.why: The GeM SLA makes documentary proof of qualifications a breach-level obligation and withholds bill payment until EPF/ESI proof is furnished, with Rs 100–200/day penalties for delay; the labour codes in force since 21 Nov 2025 raised these exposures. Buyers screen staffing vendors on this pack before they ever assess training quality.

recommendations.action: Add a named identity-and-integrity attestation for every bench candidate — live-proctored assessment, identity match against government ID, recorded work-sample session, and a stated no-outsourced-interview policy — and publish the attestation as a one-page artefact that ships with each submitted profile.
recommendations.why: CV-validation discrepancies run at 12.80% in Indian IT (AuthBridge, H1 FY26) and Gartner projects one in four candidate profiles will be fake by 2028, so 'screened by us' is now read as a risk, not a reassurance; an attestation converts Anvi's screening from a claim into an auditable artefact.

recommendations.action: Publish pricing architecture rather than a price: bill-rate bands per track and seniority, a stated markup basis, a conversion-fee schedule that tapers with hours billed and waives past a defined threshold, and an ROI comparator against direct hire plus agency fee. Model the roughly 6% MSP/administrative drag before setting guarantee economics.
recommendations.why: 51% of buyers say they wish all vendors had transparent pricing and 47% of enterprise buyers want ROI easier to calculate (TrustRadius 2024); NYSERDA's staff-augmentation RFP requires proposers to state conversion conditions, timelines and fees, so an undefined C2H path blocks bids. NC's 4.0% + 1.96% fee stack shows what large accounts cost before margin.

recommendations.action: Reposition the offer inside the buyer's own rate-card schema instead of selling 'freshers': define an explicit 'Junior / 0–18 months, certified' band with published job-knowledge and work-sample score minimums, priced a stated percentage below the market Junior band, plus a defined second-year progression and rate step. Give procurement a category they can raise a task order against.
recommendations.why: Enterprise and public staffing rate cards (NC IFB skill levels) have no zero-experience tier — Junior already means 12–36 months — so a fresher bench is unbuyable until Anvi defines and prices the missing band itself.

recommendations.action: Run three design-partner engagements at cost in Hyderabad or Bengaluru GCCs, with the reference written into the agreement up front: a named reference call, a quotable one-line outcome, and two agreed metrics captured from day one (e.g. days to first merged PR, tickets closed per sprint, defect escape rate). Target completion before any paid demand generation.
recommendations.why: 56% of buyers and 71% of enterprise buyers seek a peer conversation before buying while vendors estimate 34% (TrustRadius 2024) — the channel Anvi most needs is the one it has zero inventory in, and referenceability has to be contracted for rather than hoped for.

recommendations.action: Remove the AI training-dataset market statistic (USD 8.60bn by 2030) from the site and replace it with correctly framed, dated figures: Indian IT flexi staffing at about USD 4.9bn and 597,000 workers in FY24 rising to about USD 5.6bn and 663,000 by FY26 (Indian Staffing Federation), alongside AI talent demand projections — each with publisher and period shown inline.
recommendations.why: Citing the data-annotation market as evidence for a talent-staffing business is a self-inflicted credibility defect that any informed buyer or investor will spot in the first five minutes, and it undermines every other number on the site.

recommendations.action: Prepare an explicit objection-handling sheet for the two hardest buyer questions and publish the answers: 'who pays for your bench and does it really exist?' (bench size by track, refresh cadence, how training is funded) and 'what happens when AI tooling means I need fewer juniors?' (bench reallocation, scope-based ramp). Pair it with a stated bench-ageing policy.
recommendations.why: Indian IT majors cut fresher intake from ~600,000 (FY22) to ~250,000 (FY23) and now hold unallocated time to 30–45 days with TCS requiring 225 billable days a year — buyers read 'pre-trained bench ready in days' against that backdrop and assume the bench is notional.

unverified: Typical commercial terms for contract-to-hire conversion in India and the US (commonly cited as 10–25% of first-year salary, tapering to zero somewhere between 520 and 1,500 hours billed, with C2H periods of 3–6 months) — every source located was a staffing-vendor or recruiter blog. No ISF, NASSCOM, ASA or Staffing Industry Analysts primary document was obtained.

Typical free-replacement guarantee windows in Indian IT recruitment and staffing MSAs (commonly cited as 60–90 days, with 90 days claimed as ~45% of agency guarantee periods) — recruiter blogs only; no industry-body or filing-level source verified.

Alaska RFP 2022-0600-5055's reported staffing SLA of a full-time replacement within 15 business days of a vacancy — appeared in a search result but the document fetched at that URL was a different file (an unrelated branding guide), so the clause is unconfirmed.

Gartner's own publication of the 'one in four candidate profiles will be fake by 2028' prediction and the 2Q25 survey of 3,000 candidates finding 6% admitted interview fraud — only reached via trade press; Gartner's press release for these specific figures was not retrieved.

The claim that named Indian enterprises (Tata, Reliance, HDFC, ICICI, Adani and similar) ask for ISO 27001 by name in staffing-vendor due diligence, and that GeM favours ISO 27001-certified vendors — sourced only to compliance-vendor blogs; no procurement policy document verified. Whether SOC 2 or ISO 27001 is required of a body-shopping staffing supplier (as opposed to a software or data vendor) is therefore unestablished.

'89% of enterprise deals include client reference conversations' and '67% of buyers use review sites to validate partner claims' — widely repeated figures that could not be traced to any primary survey; TrustRadius's verified 54–56% peer-conversation figure is the defensible number.

Whether any hire-train-deploy vendor (Indian or global) publishes an independently audited placement, retention or time-to-productivity figure. Revature's metrics are self-published; no third-party audit or attestation of an HTD vendor's placement data was located.

A credible benchmark for fresher ramp-to-productivity in AI/ML engineering roles — days or weeks to first billable contribution, or to parity with a 2-year engineer. No primary study found; Revature's '70% faster time-to-productivity' is a vendor claim with no stated baseline.

Primary NASSCOM and Indian Staffing Federation reports (Talent Demand & Supply Report: AI & Big Data Analytics; ISF annual flexi-staffing report) are behind knowledge-centre gates and were not retrieved; all ISF and NASSCOM figures cited here come from trade-press reporting of those reports.

Which specific proof asset most improves win rate for a first-time B2B services vendor with no clients — anonymised case study versus paid pilot versus published rubric versus third-party certification. No controlled or survey evidence found; the trial/tryout recommendation rests on adjacent evidence (TrustRadius free-trial influence, job-tryout validity), not on a direct study of logo-less vendors.

Reconciliation of the TeamLease EdTech 74% fresher-AI-hiring-intent figure with Nomura's finding that 55% of Indian IT companies reduced entry-level hiring; neither primary report was obtained, and the entry-level share figures (28% in 2024 falling to 15% in 2025) trace only to secondary aggregation.

Whether Indian GCC and enterprise buyers will accept a vendor-run tryout at all, given co-employment, DPDP-era data-access and security-clearance constraints on letting an unvetted external engineer touch production systems for ten days. No policy or contractual evidence was found either way.

modules.domain: India and Telangana licensing and labour compliance for manpower supply

findings.claim: The legal basis of India's contract staffing industry changed on 21 November 2025: all four Labour Codes were brought into force and the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act 1970 was repealed into the OSH Code 2020.
findings.detail: The Government notified the Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Relations Code 2020, Code on Social Security 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 on 21 November 2025, consolidating 29 central labour laws. CLRA 1970 and its 1971 Central Rules are subsumed and superseded. Any compliance page, client MSA or legal annexure on anviinnovate.com that cites 'CLRA licence' as the governing instrument is now out of date.
findings.source: DLA Piper Global Employment Latest Developments

findings.claim: The contract-labour licensing threshold doubled from 20 to 50 workers, so Anvi needs no contractor licence until it has 50 or more deployed contract workers on any day in the preceding 12 months.
findings.detail: Under the OSH Code the contract-labour chapter applies to establishments engaging 50 or more contract labour, and to every contractor (including a pure manpower-supply contractor) who employed 50 or more contract labour on any day of the preceding 12 months. Below that, no contractor licence is required. For a pre-revenue bench business this is a genuine 12-24 month runway before the licence becomes a gating item — but it also means the moment the 50th deployment happens, an unlicensed supply becomes an offence.
findings.source: Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan

findings.claim: 'Contractor' under the OSH Code now expressly includes a person who supplies manpower as a mere human resource — closing the argument that pure bench-deployment is outside the contract-labour regime.
findings.detail: The OSH Code definition of contractor covers supply of manpower as a mere human resource, which was absent from CLRA 1970. The definition of contract labour was also widened to include workers in supervisory roles earning up to INR 18,000 per month (up from INR 500) and inter-state migrant workers. Anvi's 'deploy from a pre-trained bench' model is squarely a manpower-supply contract, not a services contract, unless deliberately restructured.
findings.source: Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan

findings.claim: Section 57 of the OSH Code prohibits contract labour in a client's core activity, with only three narrow exceptions — this is the single largest legal threat to Anvi's stated model of deploying engineers into client engineering teams.
findings.detail: Core activity means any activity for which the establishment is set up, including any activity essential or necessary to it. The proviso to s.57(1) permits contract labour in core activity only where (a) the activity is ordinarily done through a contractor in the normal functioning of the establishment, (b) the activity does not require full-time workers for the major portion of working hours, or (c) there is a sudden increase in volume of work to be completed in a specified time. Non-core exceptions listed are sanitation, watch and ward, courier, housekeeping, laundry and transport. For a software product or services client, engineering is the core activity — so Anvi's placements must be justified under (a), (b) or (c), or structured as something other than contract labour supply.
findings.source: Simpliance / Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan
findings.asOf: OSH Code s.57, in force 21 November 2025

findings.claim: Relabelling a staffing arrangement as 'managed services' does not defeat s.57 if the deployed engineers remain functionally embedded in the client's team.
findings.detail: Legal commentary on the core-activity boundary states that merely relabelling a manpower supply arrangement as a managed services contract will not reduce risk if vendor personnel remain functionally embedded in the principal employer's core operations; classification turns on functional integration, not contractual designation. The test examines the purpose for which the client establishment was set up and whether the activity is essential to it. Anvi's own copy — 'deploy into client engineering teams' — is an admission of embedding.
findings.source: Mondaq (Indian law firm commentary on outsourcing and the core-activity boundary)
findings.asOf: 2026 commentary on codes in force from 21 November 2025

findings.claim: Software engineers are not outside the labour regime: Indian courts have held that an engineer in a software company doing skilled technical work is a 'workman'.
findings.detail: A labour court held that the job of an engineer in a software company involved skills and technical knowledge and so the engineer was a workman; 'worker' definitions across the ID Act and the Codes cover manual, skilled, unskilled, technical, operational, clerical and supervisory work. The IT sector's long-held assumption that it sits outside industrial labour law has been eroded. Anvi cannot rely on 'these are white-collar AI engineers, not workers' as a compliance position.
findings.source: Kochhar & Co (ksandk) newsletter
findings.asOf: commentary on 2016 labour court ruling and subsequent High Court decisions

findings.claim: The central rules completing the new regime were notified on 8 May 2026 — OSH (Central) Rules 2026 via G.S.R. 345(E) — with Shram Suvidha as the single registration and licensing portal.
findings.detail: On 8 May 2026 the Government notified the Code on Wages (Central) Rules 2026, Social Security (Central) Rules 2026, OSH (Central) Rules 2026 and Industrial Relations (Central) Rules 2026. OSH Rules provide a single registration through the Shram Suvidha Portal with establishments deemed registered within 7 days of a complete application and an auto-generated certificate. Contractors apply for licence electronically; the licence is valid 5 years (replacing annual CLRA licences), specifies the number of contract labour that may be supplied, and a contractor may hold one licence for more than one state or for the whole of India. A 'work specific licence' can be issued for a particular work order.
findings.source: Sansa Legal / KPMG GMS Flash Alert 2026-127

findings.claim: Contractor licensing economics are modest: security deposit of INR 1,000 per contract labour, 5-year validity, renewal 90-30 days before expiry with a 25% late fee.
findings.detail: OSH Rules 2026 set security at INR 1,000 per contract labour, with fixed caps for very large contractors (INR 10 crore for 1-1.5 lakh workers, INR 15 crore for 1.5-2 lakh, INR 20 crore for 2 lakh+). Renewal applications are accepted 90 to 30 days before expiry, delayed applications attract a 25% additional fee, and the licensing authority must renew within 7 days. Contractor licence application is Form XXI on Shram Suvidha; the principal employer annual return is Form XVII (Part III). For a 100-person bench the deposit is roughly INR 1 lakh — not a barrier, so there is no cost excuse for operating unlicensed past 50.
findings.source: TaxGuru analysis of OSH Rules 2026

findings.claim: Telangana has NOT yet finalised its state rules under three of the four Codes — all are still at draft stage as of late 2026 — so Hyderabad-sphere staffing compliance runs on legacy machinery plus the Codes' repeal-and-savings clauses.
findings.detail: Telangana's Labour, Employment, Training and Factories Department published the draft Telangana OSH Rules 2026 on 8 May 2026 (45 days for objections), the draft Code on Social Security (Telangana) Rules 2026 on 24 June 2026, and the draft Industrial Relations (Telangana State) Rules 2026 on 2 February 2026. None were final at the time of research. Under the repeal-and-savings clauses, existing registrations, licences, rules, forms and registers under the repealed state laws continue to apply during transition, with the Code prevailing on any inconsistency. For a staffing firm whose appropriate government is the State (typical for private-sector IT clients), this means a genuinely ambiguous period — and it is why Anvi should take written legal advice rather than rely on a compliance vendor's checklist.
findings.source: TeamLease RegTech updates (Telangana draft rules)

findings.claim: Telangana is already enforcing the Code on Wages: G.O.Ms.No.6 dated 30 May 2026 fixed new minimum wages across all employments effective 1 June 2026, with Zone-I highly-skilled at INR 20,000 per month basic.
findings.detail: Revised Telangana basic minimum wages effective 1 June 2026: unskilled INR 16,000 / 15,000 / 14,000 and semi-skilled INR 17,000 / 16,000 / 15,000 and skilled INR 18,500 / 17,500 / 16,500 and highly skilled INR 20,000 / 19,000 / 18,000 for Zones I / II / III respectively, under four common skill categories defined per the Code on Wages. Hyderabad is Zone-I. Trainees and bench staff who are on Anvi's payroll and not yet deployed must still be paid at least the applicable rate for their classification, plus VDA — which sets a hard floor on bench-carrying cost that Anvi's 'deploy in days from a pre-trained bench' promise has to fund.
findings.source: TeamLease RegTech / Ascent HR, citing Telangana G.O.Ms.No.6

findings.claim: Telangana Shops and Establishments Act 1988 registration is due within 30 days of commencing work, expires on 31 December of the year of issue, and fees scale with headcount from INR 100 to INR 10,000+.
findings.detail: Registration is filed online at labour.telangana.gov.in or via the TS-iPASS portal. Fee slabs: 0 employees INR 100; 1-5 INR 500; 6-10 INR 1,000; 11-20 INR 2,000; 21-50 INR 5,000; 51-100 INR 10,000; 101+ INR 10,000 plus INR 5,000 per additional 50 persons. The certificate runs from issue to 31 December of that year and must be renewed within 30 working days of expiry. Telangana has also exempted establishments employing up to 10 employees from certain provisions of the Act.
findings.source: Keka compliance / Corpbiz
findings.asOf: Telangana Shops and Establishments Act 1988 and Rules 1990, position as at 2026

findings.claim: Telangana's IT/ITeS exemption from working-hours provisions of the Shops and Establishments Act has been extended to 29 May 2028, but it is conditional and does not exempt an employer from the Act itself.
findings.detail: The exemption covers Sections 15, 16, 21, 23 and 31 (opening and closing hours, daily and weekly hours, young persons, special provisions for women, other holidays) and is conditional on a 48-hour week, overtime wages beyond 48 hours, and a weekly day off. It is an exemption from specific sections only — registration, records, leave and wage obligations remain. If Anvi markets flexible or client-timezone shifts for deployed engineers, the 48-hour cap and overtime obligation are the binding constraints.
findings.source: Lexplosion
findings.asOf: exemption extended for 4 years to 29 May 2028

findings.claim: Telangana professional tax: nil up to INR 15,000, INR 150 for INR 15,001-20,000, INR 200 above INR 20,000 per month, with employer PTRC returns and payment due by the 10th of the following month on tgct.gov.in.
findings.detail: Annual maximum for a salaried employee is INR 2,400, within the constitutional cap of INR 2,500. Employers hold a PTRC (deduction) registration and, separately, an enrolment certificate for the entity. Monthly Form V return plus payment is due by the 10th. Because most deployed AI/ML engineers will earn above INR 20,000 per month, Anvi's PT liability is effectively INR 200 per deployed head per month — small, but a recurring monthly filing that creates default risk if unmanaged.
findings.source: CalcGuru (Telangana Professional Tax 2026-27)

findings.claim: EPF applies at 20 or more employees and the wage ceiling was deliberately retained at INR 15,000 per month by a Labour Ministry notification dated 29 May 2026, despite a Supreme Court order of 5 January 2026 asking the Union to consider revision within four months.
findings.detail: Chapter III of the Code on Social Security applies to establishments employing 20 or more employees. The Supreme Court, in an order dated 5 January 2026 in a PIL, observed that the INR 15,000 ceiling unchanged since 2014 warranted active consideration within four months; the notification of 29 May 2026 kept it at INR 15,000. Proposals to raise it to INR 21,000 were not implemented. This caps Anvi's statutory PF exposure at INR 1,800 per employee per month rather than 12% of full salary — but the ceiling is under judicial pressure and could move, so client pricing should not assume it is permanent.
findings.source: Lexplosion / SCC Online

findings.claim: The Employees' Provident Funds Scheme 2026, notified 29 June 2026, caps mandatory PF contribution at INR 1,800 per month and makes everything above it voluntary with no employer obligation to match — a material margin and take-home lever for a staffing firm.
findings.detail: Under the EPF Scheme 2026, mandatory contributions apply only to wages up to the INR 15,000 statutory ceiling (12% = INR 1,800 each from employee and employer). An employee may opt to contribute above the ceiling at the statutory rate or higher; the employer may match but is not required to. Either side can reduce or stop the additional contribution at any time. Legal commentary notes the Scheme took effect in July 2026 with the 1952 Scheme governing until November 2026, that employees must be offered the option to restrict to statutory minimums, that CTC structures may need reallocation, and that s.124 of the Code prohibits reduction of total employment benefits.
findings.source: Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan / Business Today
findings.asOf: Scheme notified 29 June 2026; transition to November 2026
findings.contradicts: Sources differ on the precise effective date: Business Today and other press report the Scheme 'came into effect on June 29, 2026', while LKS describes an effective date in July 2026 with the 1952 Scheme governing until November 2026.

findings.claim: A new joiner whose wages exceed INR 15,000 per month and who was never previously an EPF member can lawfully be treated as an 'excluded employee' — but anyone with a prior UAN must be enrolled regardless of salary.
findings.detail: Employees earning above INR 15,000 per month at the time of joining are excluded employees and are not required to become members, though they may opt in jointly with the employer. The exception matters: if the person was already an EPF member at any previous employer, exclusion is not available irrespective of salary. For Anvi this is genuinely relevant — fresh graduates and first-job trainees above INR 15,000 can be excluded, while career-switchers almost always carry a UAN and must be enrolled. The two cohorts Anvi markets to have different statutory cost structures.
findings.source: Zoho Payroll Academy / greytHR community

findings.claim: ESI registration triggers at 10 or more employees, the wage ceiling is INR 21,000 gross (INR 25,000 for persons with disability), and contribution rates remain employer 3.25% and employee 0.75% unchanged since July 2019.
findings.detail: An establishment with 10 or more workers must register if even one person draws gross wages at or below INR 21,000 per month; the INR 21,000 ceiling has applied since January 2017 and the 4% total split 3.25% / 0.75% has been frozen since the July 2019 revision, with no change in FY 2025-26 or FY 2026-27. Most deployed AI/ML engineers will sit above INR 21,000, so ESI will mainly bite on trainees, bench staff on stipends, and internal support roles — but the 10-employee registration trigger is reached long before Anvi reaches scale.
findings.source: Petpooja (Finance & Compliance) / FactoHR
findings.asOf: rates unchanged since July 2019; ceiling since January 2017; confirmed for FY 2026-27

findings.claim: Gratuity liability for fixed-term staffing now starts at ONE year, not five — the biggest unmodelled cost change for a contract-staffing P&L.
findings.detail: Under the Code on Social Security, fixed-term employees are eligible for gratuity on a pro-rata basis after one year of continuous service, instead of five years, calculated at 15 days' wages per year of service. Termination on expiry of a fixed-term contract is excluded from the definition of retrenchment, so no retrenchment compensation is due. Fixed-term employees are entitled to EPF, ESI and bonus proportionately. For Anvi, a typical 12-18 month client deployment now creates real gratuity accrual from month 12 — roughly 4.8% of wages per year — which must be priced into the bill rate from day one.
findings.source: StudyCafe / Bhatt & Joshi Associates
findings.asOf: Code on Social Security in force 21 November 2025

findings.claim: The Code on Wages 50% rule inflates the base for PF, gratuity and bonus: excluded allowances cannot exceed 50% of total remuneration, and any excess is added back to 'wages'.
findings.detail: Wages under s.2(y) means basic pay plus dearness allowance plus retaining allowance. Excluded components (HRA, conveyance, commission, overtime and similar) cannot together exceed 50% of total remuneration; the excess is added back to the wage base for statutory computation. The Code on Wages came into force 21 November 2025 and the Code on Wages (Central) Rules 2026 were notified 8 May 2026. The standard Indian staffing trick of a thin basic plus large special allowance no longer reduces statutory cost, and gratuity on a higher wage base compounds with the one-year FTE trigger above.
findings.source: Kochhar & Co (ksandk)
findings.asOf: Code in force 21 November 2025; Central Rules notified 8 May 2026

findings.claim: Written appointment letters are now mandatory for every employee including fixed-term and part-time staff, with penalties up to INR 2,00,000 for a first offence and INR 3,00,000 plus INR 2,000 per day for repeat contraventions.
findings.detail: Each employee must receive a written appointment letter stating designation, category, wages and social security details; existing employees who had not received one were to be issued within three months of commencement (reported as by 20 February 2026). The Central Rules notified 8 May 2026 prescribe formats and particulars. For a hire-train-deploy business that moves people from trainee to bench to deployment, each status change needs documentation — and a missing appointment letter is also the first thing a client's vendor audit will find.
findings.source: CalcGuru / KPMG GMS Flash Alert 2026-127
findings.asOf: issued-by date reported as 20 February 2026; Central Rules 8 May 2026

findings.claim: The client, as principal employer, carries statutory back-stop liability for Anvi's PF defaults and unpaid wages — which is why enterprise clients will gate Anvi on compliance evidence before price.
findings.detail: Section 8A of the EPF Act read with paragraph 30 of the EPF Scheme places the primary duty on the principal employer to ensure contractors pay PF contributions and permits recovery from the principal employer in the first instance on contractor default. Under the OSH Rules 2026, if the contractor fails to pay wages within 7 days the principal employer must pay the full wages or unpaid balance to the contract labour within 15 days, and the authority may recover from the contractor's security deposit. A website with no compliance disclosures, no registration numbers and no indemnity position is asking a procurement team to absorb that risk on faith.
findings.source: CGIT/Ministry of Labour appellate orders; TaxGuru analysis of OSH Rules 2026
findings.asOf: EPF Act s.8A and Scheme para 30 (settled law); OSH Rules 2026 notified 8 May 2026

findings.claim: GST at 18% applies to the GROSS invoice including salaries and statutory dues recovered, not just Anvi's markup — so a 10% gross-margin staffing deal carries GST roughly 1.8x the margin itself.
findings.detail: Manpower supply and contract staffing fall under SAC 998513 (contract staffing) and 998514 (temporary staffing) at 18%. The taxable value includes wages, statutory dues recovered such as PF and ESI, and the agency's commission or markup. General manpower supply does not attract reverse charge by default (unlike security services under Notification 13/2017-CT (Rate)), so Anvi must charge and remit. Recipients can claim ITC as staffing is not blocked under s.17(5). The Telangana AAR in Sri Bhavani Developers (TSAAR Order No. 38/2022, 14 July 2022) held manpower/labour supply attracts 18% payable by the supply agency. The working-capital consequence is severe: Anvi funds payroll monthly and remits 18% GST on the full invoice while clients pay on 30-60 day terms.
findings.source: India Briefing; LiveLaw reporting Telangana AAR TSAAR Order No. 38/2022
findings.asOf: AAR dated 14 July 2022; rate position as at 2026

findings.claim: Finance Act 2026 expressly brought supply of manpower within the definition of 'work' for TDS, fixing the rate at 1-2% under the s.194C equivalent from 1 April 2026 — a cash-flow positive clarification for staffing firms.
findings.detail: The amendment inserts supply of manpower into the definition of work at s.402(47) of the Income Tax Act 2025 (corresponding to s.194C of the 1961 Act), effective 1 April 2026, so the 10% professional/technical services rate no longer applies to manpower supply. This codifies CBDT Circular No. 715 of 22 July 1994. Clients deduct 1% or 2% rather than 10% — but note the deduction is on the gross contract value including the wage component, so even 2% of gross is a large fraction of a thin staffing margin and must be modelled as a receivable, not a cost.
findings.source: IncorpX / Terra Insight analysis of Finance Act 2026

findings.claim: A central licensing regime for placement agencies is being drafted and Maharashtra already criminalises unregistered operation with up to three years' imprisonment — a latent licence risk Anvi should track, not discover.
findings.detail: The Directorate General of Employment released the draft Private Placement Agency (Regulation) Bill 2025 for consultation on 14 August 2025, with comments due by 12 September 2025; it would require registration, record-keeping on job seekers and employers, upload of placement details within 60 days via the integrated career service portal, and inspection, with penalties including suspension or cancellation of registration. Maharashtra Act 24 of 2025 already mandates registration for agencies placing candidates in or from the state, with placement reporting within 60 days, published service charges, and up to three years' imprisonment plus fine for unregistered operation; Delhi has required registration since 2014. There is currently no central licence for domestic placement. Telangana has no equivalent statute that this research could identify.
findings.source: L&E Global; Kochhar & Co
findings.asOf: draft Bill released 14 August 2025; Maharashtra Act 24 of 2025

findings.claim: Training bonds are enforceable only up to documented, provable training cost — a round-number bond on Anvi's trainee agreements would be read down as an unenforceable penalty.
findings.detail: Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act voids agreements in restraint of trade, but courts uphold reasonable restrictions tied to genuine, provable training investment during employment. A recovery figure that is arbitrary or punitive is treated as a penalty, not liquidated damages, under ss.73-74; commentary notes courts repeatedly read inflated figures down toward actual loss. In a 2025 Supreme Court decision concerning Vijaya Bank, liquidated damages of INR 2,00,000 were held neither excessive nor punitive given seniority, voluntary execution of the bond and operational disruption. Since Anvi's entire model is funded by training freshers before deployment, bond design is a core commercial document, not boilerplate.
findings.source: JSA Prism Employment Law, May 2025

findings.claim: NAPS reimburses 25% of the prescribed stipend up to INR 1,500 per apprentice per month via DBT — a direct government subsidy for exactly the hire-train-deploy stage Anvi funds out of pocket.
findings.detail: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme, launched August 2016 and continued as NAPS-2 from 2022-23 under MSDE, reimburses 25% of the prescribed stipend capped at INR 1,500 per apprentice per month directly to the establishment. Eligible candidates include graduates, diploma holders, ITI pass-outs and skill-certificate holders; over 500,000 apprentices are engaged across sectors including IT. Apprentices are also not 'workers' for most labour-law purposes, which changes the compliance profile of the pre-deployment phase.
findings.source: IMPRI Impact and Policy Research Institute

findings.claim: POSH obligations attach at 10 or more workers and extend to staffing-agency personnel working at client premises — a gap most early-stage staffing firms carry unknowingly.
findings.detail: An Internal Committee is required where an organisation has 10 or more workers, with at least four members including a senior woman presiding officer and an external member from an NGO working on women's rights. A POSH policy should expressly cover contract workers, consultants and people working through staffing agencies, and risk extends to client meetings, offsites, training events, employer-provided transport, virtual meetings and hybrid work. Where there is no IC, an aggrieved woman may approach the Local Committee constituted by the District Officer. Anvi's residential or cohort-based training programmes and client-site deployments both sit inside this exposure.
findings.source: VinciWorks

findings.claim: The correct market statistic for Anvi's website is the formal flexi-staffing market — approximately INR 2,20,000 crore in FY26 and a workforce heading from 7.2 million in FY25 to 9.16 million by FY27 — not the USD 8.60bn AI training dataset market.
findings.detail: Indian Staffing Federation data: formal flexi-staffing is estimated to reach INR 2,20,000 crore in FY26; the industry grew 9.7% year on year in FY25 adding 1.39 lakh formal flexi workers; the flexi workforce is projected to reach 9.16 million by FY27 from 7.2 million in FY25; ISF members' flexi workforce stood at 1.83 million at end-June 2025. Separately, the Indian IT flexi-staffing market was projected to exceed USD 5.6 billion in 2025-26 with a workforce of 6.63 lakh. Note the counter-signal: flexi-staffing growth slowed to 6.1% in the first quarter reported, described as the weakest since the pandemic. Grand View Research's USD 8.60bn by 2030 figure is the AI training dataset (data annotation) market and has no bearing on demand for AI engineering talent — citing it suggests either carelessness or that no one on the team has sized the actual market.
findings.source: Indian Staffing Federation via DT Next, Staffing Industry Analysts, The Week
findings.asOf: FY25 actuals; FY26 estimate; FY27 projection; Q1 slowdown reported 2025
findings.contradicts: Headline growth projections to 9.16 million by FY27 sit against a reported deceleration to 6.1% flexi-staffing growth in the most recent quarter, the weakest since the pandemic — the market is growing but decelerating, so 'deploy in days' urgency framing should not be built on assumed acceleration.

recommendations.action: Before launch, obtain a written legal opinion on whether deploying engineers into client engineering teams breaches s.57 of the OSH Code, and restructure the top-of-funnel offer accordingly: lead with contract-to-hire and hire-train-deploy (where the client employs the person, typically as a fixed-term employee) and sell pure staff augmentation only against a documented s.57 proviso justification — project-based surge (s.57(1)(c)), part-time or non-full-time activity (s.57(1)(b)), or an activity the client ordinarily contracts out (s.57(1)(a)). Record the justification per engagement in the MSA schedule.
recommendations.why: Section 57 prohibits contract labour in a client's core activity, engineering is core for a software client, and commentary is explicit that relabelling manpower supply as managed services fails if personnel stay functionally embedded. The website currently markets 9 role tracks of embedded core engineering with no structural distinction.

recommendations.action: Re-price every bill rate from a bottom-up statutory cost model before publishing any rate card, with explicit lines for: Telangana Zone-I minimum wage floor (INR 20,000 basic highly-skilled from 1 June 2026), EPF INR 1,800 employer (and the s.124 constraint on reducing benefits), ESI 3.25% where gross is at or below INR 21,000, gratuity accrual from month 12 at 15 days' wages per year on the Code-on-Wages 50%-rule wage base, professional tax INR 200 per head per month, and bench-idle cost. Then overlay 18% GST on gross and 2% TDS on gross as working-capital, not margin, items.
recommendations.why: Gratuity moved from a 5-year to a 1-year trigger for fixed-term staff and the 50% wage rule inflates the base for PF, gratuity and bonus — together roughly 5% of wages that most new staffing entrants omit. GST at 18% is charged on gross including wages, and TDS is withheld on gross, so a thin-margin deal can be cash-negative even when profitable on paper.

recommendations.action: Add a 'Compliance and credentials' page as a second site CTA destination, listing: CIN, GSTIN, PAN/TAN, EPF establishment code, ESIC code, Telangana Shops and Establishments registration number, Telangana PT (PTRC) number, POSH Internal Committee constitution, professional indemnity and employer's liability insurance, and an explicit line on contractor licensing — e.g. 'fewer than 50 deployed contract workers; OSH Code contractor licence not yet triggered, application to be filed on Shram Suvidha (Form XXI) before the 50th deployment.'
recommendations.why: Under EPF Act s.8A and Scheme para 30 the client is recoverable-against for Anvi's PF defaults, and under the OSH Rules 2026 the principal employer must pay unpaid wages within 15 days of the contractor's 7-day failure. Procurement will gate on this before discussing price, and a site with no registration numbers, no founder bios and no case studies gives them nothing to clear.

recommendations.action: Replace the Grand View Research USD 8.60bn AI-training-dataset statistic on the website with Indian Staffing Federation figures — formal flexi-staffing approximately INR 2,20,000 crore in FY26, workforce 7.2 million in FY25 rising to a projected 9.16 million by FY27, IT flexi-staffing projected above USD 5.6 billion in FY26 with a 6.63 lakh workforce — each with publisher and period stated inline.
recommendations.why: The cited figure is the data-annotation market, not the talent market. Any CHRO or procurement lead who checks it will conclude the team has not sized its own market, which destroys the credibility the rest of the page is trying to build.

recommendations.action: Rewrite the trainee service agreement so that the recovery amount equals an itemised, documented training cost (trainer hours, compute and cloud credits, assessment, stipend paid, overhead per head) with the computation annexed, and publish the training-investment-per-candidate figure on the site. Cap recovery with straight-line taper over the commitment period.
recommendations.why: Courts enforce bonds only up to provable loss and read arbitrary round numbers down as penalties under ss.73-74 of the Contract Act; the 2025 Vijaya Bank decision upheld INR 2,00,000 only on evidence of disruption and voluntary execution. Anvi's economics depend on recovering training cost from early exits, and an unenforceable bond means the model leaks.

recommendations.action: Register as a NAPS establishment with MSDE and run the pre-deployment training cohort as an apprenticeship programme wherever candidate qualifications allow, claiming 25% of stipend up to INR 1,500 per apprentice per month via DBT.
recommendations.why: This is a direct subsidy for the exact pre-trained-bench cost that Anvi currently self-funds and that makes 'deploy in days, not months' expensive. At a 50-person cohort it is up to INR 9 lakh a year, and apprentices sit outside most 'worker' obligations during training, simplifying the pre-deployment compliance profile.

recommendations.action: Document and publish a single EPF/CTC policy decision now, covering: who is an excluded employee (new joiners above INR 15,000 with no prior UAN), the default statutory contribution of INR 1,800 under the EPF Scheme 2026, whether Anvi will match voluntary above-ceiling contributions, and how CTC is reallocated without breaching s.124 of the Code on Social Security. Issue compliant appointment letters to every trainee, bench and deployed person at each status change.
recommendations.why: The EPF Scheme 2026 makes above-ceiling contributions voluntary with no employer matching duty, which is a real margin lever, but career-switchers with an existing UAN cannot be excluded while freshers often can — two cohorts Anvi markets to simultaneously. Appointment letters are now mandatory with penalties up to INR 2,00,000 first offence and INR 3,00,000 plus INR 2,000 per day thereafter.

recommendations.action: Complete the Telangana baseline registrations and put a monthly compliance calendar in place: Shops and Establishments registration within 30 days of commencing work at labour.telangana.gov.in or TS-iPASS (renewed before 31 December each year), PT enrolment and PTRC with Form V by the 10th monthly on tgct.gov.in, ESIC at 10 employees, EPF at 20 employees, POSH Internal Committee at 10 workers, and the OSH annual return by 28/29 February.
recommendations.why: These thresholds are crossed well before the 50-worker contractor-licence trigger, and Telangana's own rules under three of the four Codes were still in draft as at late 2026 (OSH draft 8 May 2026, Social Security draft 24 June 2026, IR draft 2 February 2026), so legacy state machinery plus repeal-and-savings governs day-to-day filings in the interim.

recommendations.action: Put a named owner on a watch list with quarterly review for: final Telangana OSH, Social Security and IR Rules; the central Private Placement Agency (Regulation) Bill 2025; any revision of the INR 15,000 EPF ceiling following the Supreme Court order of 5 January 2026; and the Maharashtra Private Placement Agencies (Regulation) Act 2025 — register in Maharashtra before placing any candidate in or from that state.
recommendations.why: Unregistered operation under the Maharashtra Act carries up to three years' imprisonment, the central Bill would create a first-ever domestic placement licence, and the EPF ceiling is under live judicial pressure. Each of these can change Anvi's cost base or legality of operation with little notice, and a staffing firm that discovers a licence requirement after signing a client loses the client.

recommendations.action: Add a statutory-compliance and indemnity schedule to the standard MSA and summarise it on the website: monthly challan evidence for EPF/ESI/PT before invoice, back-to-back indemnity for wage and social-security defaults, replacement and notice SLAs, and a clear statement of who is the employer of record. Expose this as a downloadable one-pager behind the existing hiring request form.
recommendations.why: The client's exposure as principal employer under EPF s.8A and Scheme para 30, plus the OSH Rules 2026 obligation to pay unpaid wages within 15 days, is the first substantive objection an enterprise buyer raises. The site currently has one CTA and no SLAs, so there is nothing for a buyer to evaluate between 'interested' and 'contract'.

unverified: Whether the Telangana OSH, Social Security and Industrial Relations Rules have been finalised and notified after the dates found (drafts dated 8 May 2026, 24 June 2026 and 2 February 2026 respectively) — this must be checked directly on labour.telangana.gov.in before relying on any transition position.

Whether the Andhra Pradesh amendment raising the CLRA threshold from 20 to 50 workers carried over to Telangana after the 2014 bifurcation, and therefore what the legacy state-sphere threshold is during the transition period. The point is largely moot going forward since the OSH Code sets 50 nationally, but it affects liability for any period already elapsed.

The exact contractor licence FEE schedule under the OSH (Central) Rules 2026. Secondary sources report only that no licence is required below 50 contract labour and that security is INR 1,000 per contract labour; the actual rupee fee bands were not located. G.S.R. 345(E) dated 8 May 2026 should be read directly.

Which form number applies to the contractor licence application — sources cite both Form XIII/XIV (application/licence) and Form XXI, and Form XV is variously described as a contractor experience certificate and as an experience certificate issued BY contractors TO workers. The gazette text should settle this.

Whether the final central or Telangana rules impose eligibility criteria on contractors (minimum experience, net worth, turnover) for a licence. Draft-rule commentary hinted at an experience certificate requirement but no confirmed criteria were found.

Reconciliation of the establishment-registration timeline: one source states registration is due within 60 days of applicability under the OSH Code, another that an establishment is deemed registered within 7 days of a complete application on Shram Suvidha. These are probably different obligations (deadline to apply vs time to grant) but this was not confirmed.

Whether any designated authority formally adjudicates 'core activity' disputes under s.57 of the OSH Code, what the appeal route is, and the specific penalty for engaging contract labour in a core activity. No penalty provision or adjudication mechanism for s.57 breach was located.

Whether any Indian authority, court or government circular has addressed whether IT staff augmentation into a client's software engineering function constitutes 'core activity' under s.57. No such determination was found — the s.57 risk to Anvi's model is real but legally untested in the IT staffing context.

Whether the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers (Registration, Social Security and Welfare) Bill 2025 (draft circulated 15 April 2025, proposing a 1-2% per-transaction welfare fund fee on aggregators) has been enacted, and whether its definition of aggregator or primary employer could be read to cover a B2B talent-deployment platform rather than only consumer app-based platforms.

Whether e-invoicing is mandatory for manpower agencies above INR 5 crore aggregate turnover from April 2026 — this rested on a single weak secondary source and should be checked against the GST notification.
Whether all Telangana districts are ESI-implemented areas, which determines whether ESI contribution is payable for staff deployed at client sites outside Hyderabad.

Whether Telangana currently requires any registration or licence for a domestic placement or recruitment agency (as Maharashtra and Delhi do). No Telangana statute or rule to that effect was found, but absence of a search result is not proof of absence.

Anvi Innovate's own current headcount, deployed-worker count, entity type and existing registrations. Every threshold in this review — 10 for ESI and POSH, 20 for EPF, 50 for the contractor licence, and the Shops and Establishments fee slab — depends on numbers this research could not obtain from the public website, which shows no placement numbers, team size or founder details.

modules.domain: GST, contracting and data protection obligations

findings.claim: Contract staffing and manpower supply attract 18% GST with full input tax credit, under the SAC 9985 'support services' family (998511 executive search, 998512 permanent placement, 998513 contract staffing, 998514 temporary staffing, 998515 long-term staffing/payroll).
findings.detail: All of Anvi's sellable motions - contract staffing, contract-to-hire and hire-train-deploy - fall in SAC 9985 at the 18% standard rate, not a concessional slab. The SAC sub-code matters for invoice hygiene and for how clients book the cost: 998513 is the right code when the engineer stays on Anvi's rolls, 998512/998511 when Anvi bills a one-time placement fee. The commonly cited invoicing practice is to show headcount, days/hours and the SAC on the face of the invoice.
findings.source: Busy (GST software vendor reference pages)
findings.asOf: Rates current as at 2026; SAC structure unchanged since 2017

findings.claim: The 22 September 2025 GST rate rationalisation collapsed the slabs to 5% / 18% / 40% but left staffing services at the 18% standard rate.
findings.detail: The 56th GST Council meeting (3 September 2025) recommended the two-rate structure, given effect by Notification No. 15/2025-Central Tax (Rate) and companion notifications amending Notification 11/2017-CTR, effective 22 September 2025. The reductions targeted consumer goods, agri-equipment and household electronics; business support and manpower services stayed at 18%. There is no pending relief for staffing, so Anvi should not price on any assumption of a future rate cut.
findings.source: EY India / CBIC notifications alert; Tally Solutions

findings.claim: GST is payable on the ENTIRE invoice value of a manpower supply - including the deployed engineer's salary and the employer's EPF and ESI contributions. Staffing firms are not 'pure agents'.
findings.detail: The Telangana AAR (Bhagyalakshmi Devamma Vangimallu, TSAAR Order No. 14/2021) and the West Bengal AAR both held that Section 15(2) CGST leaves no room to deduct reimbursed salary, EPF or ESI from taxable value, and that a manpower supplier is not a pure agent under Rule 33. Consequence for Anvi's pricing: an engineer costing INR 1,00,000/month billed at a 30% markup is invoiced at INR 1,30,000 + INR 23,400 GST, not GST on the INR 30,000 margin. Any client who is GST-exempt or has blocked credit (hospitals, education, some BFSI, government bodies) bears that 18% as a real cost, which materially changes Anvi's competitiveness in those segments.
findings.source: GST Council (AAR order, primary) and VJM Global
findings.asOf: TSAAR Order 14/2021; West Bengal AAR line of rulings 2019-2024

findings.claim: There is no reverse charge on general manpower supply. RCM applies only to supply of SECURITY PERSONNEL, and only where the supplier is not a body corporate.
findings.detail: Notification No. 29/2018-Central Tax (Rate) dated 31 December 2018, effective 1 January 2019, put security personnel supply (SAC 998521) under RCM at 18% when supplied to a registered person by any person other than a body corporate. Two implications for Anvi: (a) as a company, Anvi always charges GST under forward charge on its own staffing invoices, including any security-adjacent deployment - a client claiming 'we'll pay under RCM' is wrong; (b) if Anvi sources bench or sub-vendor manpower for security roles from a proprietorship or partnership, Anvi becomes liable to self-assess RCM GST and cannot net it off the sub-vendor invoice.
findings.source: The Hitavada / Legal Mantra summaries of Notification 29/2018-CT(R)

findings.claim: For domestic B2B staffing the place of supply is the client's registered location (Section 12(2) IGST), so a Hyderabad-registered Anvi charges IGST to out-of-state clients and CGST+SGST only to Telangana clients.
findings.detail: The default B2B rule puts the place of supply at the recipient's location, and it is the client's GSTIN on the purchase order - not where the engineer physically sits - that decides CGST+SGST vs IGST. Practical risk: if a Bengaluru client's PO is raised by its Hyderabad branch GSTIN while the engineer works in Bengaluru, Anvi must follow the GSTIN, or face a wrong-tax-head demand with interest and a refund cycle. Anvi's hiring-request form currently captures no GSTIN or billing-state field at all.
findings.source: General Section 12(2)/13(2) IGST position as summarised in export-of-services guides
findings.asOf: IGST Act 2017, Section 12(2); position unchanged as at 2026

findings.claim: Deploying engineers at a client's premises in another state does not by itself create a 'fixed establishment' requiring GST registration in that state - provided contracting, invoicing and control stay with the Hyderabad head office.
findings.detail: The Odisha Appellate AAR (Order No. 02/Odisha-AAAR/Appeal/2025-26, reported February 2026) held that head-office-driven AMC services executed through deputed engineers did not create a place of business or fixed establishment in the state, because the 'sufficient degree of permanence' and the suitable structure of human and technical resources required by Section 2(50) CGST were absent. This is the single biggest cost question in Anvi's model - multi-state registration would mean separate GSTINs, returns and ITC pools. But AAR/AAAR rulings bind only the applicant, and at least one AAR has gone the other way where a site office existed, so this is a planning position to be documented, not a settled entitlement.
findings.source: Taxmann and Taxo.online reporting Odisha AAAR
findings.contradicts: A separate AAR (reported by Taxmann as 'GST Registration Required in Site State for Fixed Establishment') reached the opposite conclusion where the supplier had a durable site presence - so the outcome turns on facts, and a dedicated Anvi-side office or project manager in a client city could flip it.

findings.claim: Finance Act 2026 omitted Section 13(8)(b) of the IGST Act with effect from 30 March 2026, removing the main obstacle to treating offshore staffing and recruitment-facilitation revenue as zero-rated export of services.
findings.detail: The 56th GST Council (3 September 2025) recommended the omission on the ground that deeming the place of supply of 'intermediary services' to be the supplier's location breached the destination principle and was damaging exports. The Finance Act 2026 received Presidential assent on 30 March 2026 and the omission took effect the same day. The place of supply for intermediary services now follows Section 13(2) - the recipient's location. CBIC Circular No. 159/15/2021-GST (20 September 2021) remains the test for who is an intermediary: three parties, two distinct supplies, and the intermediary not supplying the main service on its own account. For Anvi, a US or Gulf client contracting for a deployed engineer is a principal-to-principal supply (not intermediary at all) and, with an LUT and FIRC-backed forex receipt, is zero-rated with ITC refund.
findings.source: Grant Thornton India; Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan; Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas

findings.claim: E-invoicing becomes mandatory for Anvi's B2B invoices once aggregate annual turnover crosses INR 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards.
findings.detail: CBIC Notification No. 10/2023-Central Tax (10 May 2023) cut the threshold from INR 10 crore to INR 5 crore with effect from 1 August 2023; it has not moved since. On a staffing P&L the turnover test is gross billing including pass-through salary, not margin - so a bench of roughly 25-30 engineers billed at INR 1.5-2 lakh/month will breach INR 5 crore within the first full year. An invoice that should have carried an IRN but did not is treated as an invalid document, which lets the client deny ITC and dispute the payment.
findings.source: CAclub / Tax Ninja summarising CBIC Notification 10/2023-Central Tax
findings.asOf: Threshold of INR 5 crore effective 1 August 2023

findings.claim: Where the client is a government department, local authority, PSU or notified entity, 2% GST TDS is withheld under Section 51 CGST on any contract whose taxable value exceeds INR 2.5 lakh.
findings.detail: The deductor pays over the tax by the 10th of the following month and files GSTR-7; the amount shows in Anvi's electronic cash ledger only after that filing. The INR 2.5 lakh test is applied to the contract, not the individual invoice, so almost every government staffing contract is caught. Effect on Anvi: 2% of gross billing is locked up until the client files, and public-sector clients are the slowest filers - this compounds the DSO problem on a model that must pay salaries on the 1st regardless.
findings.source: Masters India; Bihar government GST study material
findings.asOf: Section 51 CGST, in force since 1 October 2018; position current 2026

findings.claim: Clients deduct income-tax TDS from Anvi's staffing invoices, and the rate turns on whether the engagement is characterised as a contract (2%) or as professional/technical services (10% or 2%) - a 5x cash-flow difference.
findings.detail: Under the old numbering, Section 194C applied 1% to individual/HUF contractors and 2% to other residents, with no deduction where a single payment stayed under INR 30,000 and annual aggregate under INR 1,00,000. Section 194J applied 10% to professional fees and 2% to fees for technical services, with a INR 50,000 annual threshold. From 1 April 2026 these are consolidated into Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, with rates and thresholds carried over substantially unchanged. For Anvi the live risk is a client treating an 'Applied AI consultant' deployment as professional services and withholding 10% of gross billing - on a thin staffing margin that is more than the margin itself, recoverable only on assessment a year later.
findings.source: India Briefing; Taxheal; CBDT-aligned TDS summaries
findings.asOf: Section 194C/194J position FY 2025-26; Section 393 effective 1 April 2026

findings.claim: All four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, and the contract-labour licensing threshold rose from 20 to 50 workers, with a single pan-India contractor licence replacing state-by-state licences.
findings.detail: The Code on Wages 2019, Code on Social Security 2020, OSH and Working Conditions Code 2020 and Industrial Relations Code 2020 consolidated 29 central labour laws and were enforced with effect from 21 November 2025. Contract-labour provisions now generally bite where 50 or more contract workers were employed on any day in the preceding 12 months, and a qualifying contractor must hold the licence before deployment - a licence Anvi can now get once for the whole country. This is genuinely favourable to Anvi: below 50 deployed engineers there is no contractor licence obligation, and above it the licence is one filing, not fifteen.
findings.source: JSA (law firm) Labour Codes Snapshot, 22 November 2025

findings.claim: The Supreme Court in Vijaya Bank v. Prashant B. Narnaware (2025 INSC 691, 14 May 2025) upheld a minimum-service clause with INR 2,00,000 liquidated damages - which is the legal foundation Anvi's hire-train-deploy model needs for trainee bonds.
findings.detail: The Court reversed the Karnataka High Court and held that negative covenants operating DURING the term of employment are not a restraint of trade under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act. It stressed that the sum must be reasonable and proportionate and must reflect actual recoverable costs - recruitment, training, disruption from attrition - rather than operate as a penalty. For Anvi this means a trainee service agreement is enforceable if the bond amount is costed from documented training spend per candidate (trainer hours, compute, assessment, stipend) rather than set at a round deterrent figure.
findings.source: S.S. Rana & Co.; LiveLaw; King Stubb & Kasiva

findings.claim: Non-solicitation of employees is enforceable in India; post-employment non-compete against the engineer is not. Anvi's protection has to sit in the client MSA, not in the candidate's contract.
findings.detail: Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act voids any agreement restraining a person from exercising a lawful profession, and the Supreme Court (Superintendence Company of India; the Percept/Zaheer Khan line) has struck down post-service non-competes. But the Delhi High Court in Wipro v. Beckman Coulter held a non-solicitation clause to be a reasonable restriction not hit by Section 27, and courts have repeatedly distinguished restraints on a contracting counterparty from restraints on an individual's livelihood. The operative asset for Anvi is therefore a client-side non-solicit plus a priced conversion fee: an engineer Anvi cannot stop from joining the client directly, Anvi can charge the client for.
findings.source: Casemine; ipleaders; LiveLaw; IIM Ahmedabad working paper on non-compete and non-solicitation
findings.asOf: Section 27 Contract Act 1872; Wipro v. Beckman Coulter (Delhi HC, 2006); IIMA working paper May 2026
findings.contradicts: Commentators disagree on whether employee non-solicit clauses survive Section 27 in all forms - some read non-solicitation as itself a restraint of trade and against public policy. The safer reading is that a liquidated conversion fee between two companies is far more defensible than an injunction against the individual.

findings.claim: The DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified on 13-14 November 2025 and commence in three tranches, with the substantive obligations - notice, consent, security, breach reporting, retention, data principal rights - switching on in May 2027.
findings.detail: Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 (constitution and functioning of the Data Protection Board of India) commenced on notification. Rule 4 (registration and obligations of consent managers) commences at twelve months, i.e. 12 November 2026. Rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 commence at eighteen months - 12 or 13 May 2027 depending on how the notification date is counted. Penalties run to INR 250 crore. Anvi therefore has roughly nineteen months of runway, but the design decisions (what consent text sits on the resume-upload form, where resumes live, how long they are kept) are being made now and are expensive to retrofit after a few thousand candidates are in the database.
findings.source: AZB & Partners; Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan; SCC Online
findings.asOf: Rules notified 13 November 2025; final tranche 12 May 2027
findings.contradicts: AZB states notification on 13 November 2025 and full enforcement 12 May 2027; other trackers (TechPrescient, K&S) state 14 November 2025 and 13 May 2027. Treat mid-May 2027 as the deadline and do not plan to the day.

findings.claim: The DPDP Act's Section 7(i) 'employment purposes' legitimate-use ground does not reliably cover JOB CANDIDATES - so Anvi needs express, specific consent for every resume it collects, screens, verifies and forwards to a client.
findings.detail: Section 7(i) gives a statutory basis for processing employee data for employment purposes, but the position for someone not yet hired is unsettled, and employers should not assume it authorises pre-employment screening - particularly criminal, financial or medical checks unrelated to the role. Submission of a resume is not unrestricted permission. This is structural for Anvi: its entire funnel is candidates who are not yet its employees, and forwarding a CV to a client is a disclosure to a third party that needs its own consent and notice. Under Rule 3 the notice must be standalone and understandable, itemise the data collected, state the purpose, and give the mechanism to withdraw consent and raise grievances - it cannot be buried in a training enrolment form.
findings.source: King Stubb & Kasiva; OnGrid; Avvanz
findings.asOf: Analysis of DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025, as at 2026

findings.claim: DPDP Rule 7 requires Anvi to tell every affected candidate or client contact about a personal data breach 'without delay', intimate the Data Protection Board immediately, and file a detailed report to the Board within 72 hours.
findings.detail: The dual intimation covers the nature and extent of the breach, its likely consequences, mitigation steps taken, and - in the report to the Board - the remedial measures implemented. There is no materiality threshold and no harm test in the Act: a misdirected spreadsheet of candidate CVs is a reportable breach. Rule 6 separately prescribes the minimum safeguards - encryption/tokenisation, access control, logging and monitoring, backup and business continuity - and requires access logs and the relevant personal data to be retained for one year to support breach detection and investigation.
findings.source: Lawrbit; Thales compliance brief; Data Security Council of India (DSCI) guidance on reasonable security safeguards
findings.asOf: DPDP Rules 2025, Rules 6 and 7; in force 12 May 2027

findings.claim: DPDP Rule 8 requires erasure once the purpose is served or consent is withdrawn, with 48 hours' advance notice to the data principal. The fixed three-year retention cap applies only to specified classes (large e-commerce, online gaming, social media) - staffing is not one of them.
findings.detail: So Anvi is not handed a convenient three-year rule; it must define and defend its own retention period for rejected candidates, bench candidates who never deployed, and former deployed engineers, and it must be able to actually delete on request. The practical trap is the shadow copies: resumes in recruiter inboxes, WhatsApp, Google Drive folders and an ATS trial account are all within scope, and a right-to-erasure request that Anvi cannot execute across them is the breach.
findings.source: dpdpa.com rule tracker; BitRaser; Seclore
findings.asOf: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 8; in force 12 May 2027

findings.claim: Under Section 8(2) of the DPDP Act, Anvi can only use a background-verification vendor or any sub-processor under a valid written contract, and Rule 6(1)(f) requires that contract to bind the processor to the prescribed security safeguards.
findings.detail: The required terms are specific: categories of personal data, permitted purposes and uses, confidentiality, security safeguards, restrictions on onward disclosure, rules on engaging sub-processors, assistance with data principal requests, retention and deletion, and breach-response procedures. Anvi sits on both sides of this - data fiduciary for candidate data it collects, and processor (or joint fiduciary) for client data its deployed engineers touch inside the client's systems. That means two paper trails: a downstream DPA with every BGV vendor, assessment platform and ATS, and an upstream data-processing schedule in the client MSA covering what a deployed engineer may access, log and take with them.
findings.source: King Stubb & Kasiva; Tsaaro; AMLEGALS
findings.asOf: DPDP Act 2023 Section 8(2); DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 6(1)(f)
