verdicts.issue: Verified line-by-line in the primary annexure. IT-Software/Software Services: 3,585 (Sep'25) to 3,432 (Sep'26), marked ↓4%. IT-Hardware & Networking 580 to 549 ↓5%. KPO/Research/Analytics 1,207 to 976 ↓19%. Education/Teaching/Training 5,357 to 4,386 ↓18%. Recruitment 545 to 995 ↑83%. Every figure exact, including the ironic Recruitment row.

verdicts.claim: India's #1 staffing firm runs its IT/digital/GCC contract staffing on 7,129 associates; 1.5% of headcount, 6% of revenue
verdicts.issue: Core figures confirmed in Quess Corp Investor Presentation Q1 FY27 (extracted locally): Professional Staffing headcount 7,129 at quarter exit, 'growth of 7% YoY', revenue Rs 252 cr, EBITDA Rs 28 cr. Ratios check out (7,129/482,000 = 1.5%; 252/4,182 = 6.0%). Two defects: (a) the deck states active associates as '~482,000' / '4.82L+', not a precise 482,214 — the exact 4,78,594 figure appears in the Q4 FY26 deck as the FY26 closing number, so 482,214 is spurious precision from the wrong period; (b) the 'ranked #1 in SIA's top 100 largest staffing firms in India, 2025' attribution is not in the filing and was not independently verified.
verdicts.corrected: Quess Corp reported Professional Staffing headcount of 7,129 at Q1 FY27 exit, +7% YoY, on revenue of Rs 252 cr for the quarter. Total active associates were ~482,000 — so professional/IT staffing is about 1.5% of headcount and 6% of revenue. (Quess is widely described as India's largest staffing firm; the specific SIA 2025 ranking is unverified.)

verdicts.claim: Quess's IT/professional staffing revenue growth collapsed from 31% YoY to 3% YoY in twelve months
verdicts.issue: The quarterly series is reproduced exactly in the Q1 FY27 deck's Professional Staffing revenue chart: 244 (Q1'26), 224 (Q2'26), 230 (Q3'26), 232 (Q4'26), 252 (Q1'27), headline '3%'. Below the Q1 FY27 EBITDA bar the deck shows 11.0% against 12.8% for Q4'26, and the segment table shows revenue ▲3% YoY. The claim that revenue sat below the Q1 FY26 level for three intervening quarters is arithmetically correct. The only unverified element is the historic '+31% YoY' for Q1 FY26, which is not in this deck.

verdicts.claim: The live order book for niche/high-value contract roles at India's largest staffing firm is about 1,100 open mandates
verdicts.issue: Verbatim in the Q1 FY27 deck's Professional Staffing Key Developments: 'Open mandates at 1,100+ primarily in niche and high value roles' and 'Added 36 contracts during the quarter'. The '700+ recruiters across the group' figure is also confirmed on the Large Scale Operations slide ('Recruiters: 700+'). Note a separate slide shows '86 new contracts added in the quarter' for a different segment — do not conflate the two.

verdicts.claim: GCCs are roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of Indian IT contract staffing at both listed leaders
verdicts.issue: The Quess leg is confirmed verbatim: 'GCC contributing 71% of headcount with 68% of revenue contribution', with the headcount chart showing GCC 71% and Enterprise 7% / IT-ITeS 22% for Q1'27, and revenue contribution GCC 68% / Enterprise 11% / IT-ITeS 21%. The TeamLease 67% and the ISF 73%-of-new-mandates figures were NOT verified — I reached neither source, and the ISF research page I did fetch publishes no GCC-share figure at all. So this is one hard source plus two unconfirmed ones, not 'three independent sources converge'.
verdicts.corrected: Quess Professional Staffing Q1 FY27: GCCs are 71% of headcount and 68% of revenue (Enterprise 7%, IT/ITeS 22% of headcount) — verified in the filing. TeamLease's reported ~67% GCC share of Specialised Staffing revenue and the ISF's 73%-of-new-mandates figure are from secondary coverage and remain unverified; the ISF research page publishes no GCC-share figure.

verdicts.claim: TeamLease's specialised staffing arm is the same size as Quess's — 7,630 heads — and runs on a ~6% EBITDA margin
verdicts.issue: The ~6% margin is wrong against the audited presentation. TeamLease Investor Presentation Q4 FY26 (NSE archives, extracted locally) shows Specialised Staffing Services EBITDA margin of 7.4% for FY26 and 7.3% in Q4 FY26, Q3 FY26 and Q4 FY25 — a remarkably stable 7.3-7.4%, not 6%. Headcount was 7,500 at Q4 FY26 (the deck's quarterly table), so 7,630 in Q1 FY27 is plausible (+13% YoY off 6,730 in Q1 FY26) but comes only from investing.com, not a filing. Total company headcount 340,600 at Q4 FY26, -2% YoY, making '341,330, down 3%' plausible but unverified.
verdicts.corrected: TeamLease Specialised Staffing ran a 7.4% segment EBITDA margin in FY26 (7.3% in Q4 FY26) on revenue of Rs 669 cr, with headcount of 7,500 at 31 March 2026 — verified in the Q4 FY26 presentation. The Q1 FY27 figures (7,630 heads, +13% YoY, +21% revenue, ~6% margin, 67% GCC) are from secondary coverage only; the ~6% margin contradicts the audited 7.3-7.4% trend and should not be quoted. Quess and TeamLease together held roughly 14,600 specialised/IT contract associates at FY26 close.

verdicts.claim: Realistic gross margin for AI/ML contract staffing in India is 20-22%, converting to 6-11% EBITDA
verdicts.issue: The Quess leg is confirmed verbatim: 'Gross margin to EBITDA margin conversion remains above 50%' alongside an 11.0% Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin, which does imply roughly 20-22% gross margin. Revenue per associate checks out exactly: Rs 252 cr / 7,129 = Rs 3.53 lakh per quarter = Rs 14.1 lakh annualised. Two problems: the TeamLease '~6% EBITDA' floor is wrong (audited FY26 is 7.4%), so the range should be 7-11% not 6-11%; and the 15-22% markup benchmark is sourced to a vendor page the finding itself labels weak, with no official confirmation of the '18% GST on the markup' treatment (GST applies to the full invoice value, not the markup alone — see the GST finding).
verdicts.corrected: Quess Professional Staffing discloses 'gross margin to EBITDA margin conversion remains above 50%' with an 11.0% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27, implying gross margin of roughly 20-22% on billings. TeamLease Specialised Staffing runs 7.4% EBITDA (FY26), so the realistic band is roughly 20-22% gross converting to 7-11% EBITDA. Revenue per Quess professional-staffing associate is Rs 14.1 lakh per year of billing. The 15-22% agency markup range is vendor-sourced and unverified.

verdicts.claim: India's formal flexi workforce is 1.95mn (ISF members), growing 7.5% YoY, with IT staffing decelerated to 7%
verdicts.issue: Fetched indianstaffingfederation.org/research. The Q1 FY27 figures are confirmed: 1.95 million formal flexi workforce, 7.5% YoY industry growth, 1.14 lakh (114,000) new formal flexi jobs over 12 months, IT staffing 7% YoY and 2% QoQ, General Staffing 2.6% QoQ. NOT on the page: the Rs 1.47 lakh crore annual salary contribution and Rs 52,800 crore social security and GST figures (the page shows unlabelled 'Annual Salary' and 'Social Impact' charts but no such numbers), and none of the FY26 back-series (+12.3% Q1 FY26, +16% Q2 FY26, +10.1% FY26, 1.83mn at end-June 2025).
verdicts.corrected: ISF reports members representing a 1.95mn formal flexi workforce in Q1 FY27, with 114,000 roles added over 12 months, overall industry growth of 7.5% YoY and IT staffing at 7% YoY / 2% QoQ. The Rs 1.47 lakh crore salary and Rs 52,800 crore social-security/GST figures and the FY26 quarterly back-series are not published on the ISF research page and remain unverified.

verdicts.claim: GCC buyer universe: 2,117 GCCs, 3,728 units, 2.36mn professionals, USD 98.4bn FY26 revenue; report published May 2026
verdicts.issue: Fetched the PR Newswire release. All headline figures confirmed exactly: 2,117 GCCs, 3,728 units, 2.36 million professionals, USD 98.4bn FY26 revenue, 32% growth since FY21, 506 Forbes Global 2000 companies, 1,200+ GCCs with embedded AI/ML, 250+ dedicated AI Centres of Excellence, ~250,000 AI professionals, 90%+ university partnerships. The publication date is wrong: the release is dated 2 July 2026, not May 2026. Also unverified: the USD 61.4bn FY21 base, 'over 100 new centres in FY26' and 'over 500 in five years' (the release implies ~280 net new GCCs since FY21 from the 32% growth figure).
verdicts.corrected: NASSCOM-Zinnov India GCC Landscape Report 2026 (released 2 July 2026): 2,117 GCCs across 3,728 units employing ~2.36mn people, generating USD 98.4bn in FY26; 32% increase in GCC count since FY21; 506 Forbes Global 2000 companies present; 1,200+ GCCs with embedded AI/ML capability, 250+ dedicated AI Centres of Excellence, ~250,000 AI professionals. The FY21 USD 61.4bn base and the new-centre counts are unverified.

verdicts.claim: Hyderabad is the fastest-growing metro for white-collar hiring in India at +9% YoY, ahead of Bengaluru at +4%
verdicts.issue: Every city figure verified against the primary Annexure City Data table. Hyderabad/Secunderabad 3,889 to 4,237 ↑9%; Bengaluru 3,139 to 3,267 ↑4%; Chennai 2,330 to 2,459 ↑6%; Pune 4,161 to 4,167 ↑0.1%; Delhi/NCR 3,092 to 2,896 ↓6%; Mumbai 2,282 to 2,140 ↓6%; Kolkata 3,446 to 3,575 ↑4%. Hyderabad is indeed the highest growth rate of any major metro. The 'metro' qualifier is load-bearing and correctly stated: several smaller cities grew faster (Jamnagar +17%, Nellore +13%, Gandhinagar +10%). The index-normalisation caveat is also correctly stated.

verdicts.claim: Hyderabad's share of GCCs rose 12% (FY24) to 14% (FY26E) while Bengaluru holds 29% of units
verdicts.issue: I could not reach the cited Storyboard18 article (web-search budget exhausted; the URL was not among those I was able to fetch). The underlying NASSCOM-Zinnov release I did verify confirms the 2,117/3,728/2.36mn/USD 98.4bn totals but publishes no city-level share breakdown, so the 29% Bengaluru / 14% Hyderabad / 47% NCR+Bengaluru / 90-95%-in-six-cities / 7% tier-2 figures are all unconfirmed against any source I reached. Note this claim's Hyderabad share (14%) conflicts in framing with a later finding in this set citing 'Hyderabad wins 40-46% of India's new GCC setups' — stock share and flow share are different measures and should not be presented together without that distinction.

verdicts.claim: Telangana targets 100 additional GCCs in 2026 generating ~100,000 specialised jobs on a base of ~450 centres
verdicts.issue: The cited Deccan Chronicle article was not reachable within this session's remaining fetch capability, and no official Telangana ITE&C source confirming the 100-GCC / 1-lakh-jobs target was verified. This is a government policy-target claim, so under the official-source rule a minister's remarks relayed by a single newspaper are not sufficient — it needs confirmation from it.telangana.gov.in or a state press release before being used in a pitch. The supporting Telangana figures (Rs 3.13 lakh crore FY25 IT exports, 9.39 lakh IT employment, 197 GCCs since 2024) are likewise unverified here.

verdicts.claim: GCC fresher hiring is shrinking as a share of intake — 16% of FY27 hiring, down from 21%
verdicts.issue: Fetched the DQIndia article. Every figure confirmed: freshers 16% of expected FY27 GCC hiring, down from 21%; 1-5 years experience 30% (so 46% combined early-career); 52% plan expansion, 22% stable, 26% anticipate reductions; nearly 50% of GCCs report >25% of open roles require AI capability; 25% say most positions are already AI-adjacent. Published 30 August 2026. One attribution correction worth noting: the underlying report's actual title is 'From Intent to Predictable Scale: The Future of GCCs in India' (2nd edition), produced with CII — 'Taggd GCC Talent Lab Report 2026' is a loose label for it.

verdicts.claim: GCCs source AI talent almost entirely from experienced pools; training pipelines are not a named channel
verdicts.issue: Confirmed in the DQIndia coverage: 78% of GCC talent acquired externally, 22% developed internally; of the external 78%, 41% from IT services firms, 32% from other GCCs, 27% from startups and product companies. The three named sources sum to 100% of external hiring, which does substantiate the inference that training providers, hire-train-deploy vendors and campus pipelines are not broken out as a channel. This is the single most commercially damaging verified finding in the set for a fresher-bench model.

verdicts.claim: 48% of critical GCC roles take more than 60 days to fill, and quality mismatch is the primary constraint
verdicts.issue: Confirmed in the DQIndia coverage: 48% of critical roles exceed 60-day fill times; offer-to-join conversion ~80%; quality mismatch named as the primary hiring constraint; graduate job-readiness 42.6%. One attribution caveat: the article attributes the 42.6% readiness figure to Taggd's own data rather than explicitly to the India Graduate Skills Index 2026, so cite it as Taggd/GCC Talent Lab rather than to the Skills Index.

verdicts.claim: Correct TAM anchors: India tech revenue USD 315bn in FY26 with AI-related revenue of only USD 10-12bn
verdicts.issue: Downloaded the NASSCOM Strategic Review 2026 Executive Summary PDF directly and extracted it. Confirmed: FY26E revenue 315.4bn (crossing the USD 300bn mark), growth 6.1%, FY25 297.2bn, exports 246.4bn. NOT in the executive summary: the segment split (IT services USD 149bn, BPM USD 59bn, ER&D USD 63bn, software products USD 23bn, hardware USD 21bn) — the summary gives only a domestic USD 69.0bn / exports USD 246.4bn split; and the AI-related revenue estimate of USD 10-12bn, which appears nowhere in the document (a grep for every dollar-billion figure returns only 127, 300, 315, 246). The 'AI is only 3-4% of Indian tech revenue' conclusion therefore rests on an unverified number. The NASSCOM-BCG USD 17bn-by-2027 projection is also unverified.
verdicts.corrected: NASSCOM Strategic Review 2026: India's tech industry crossed USD 300bn to reach USD 315.4bn in FY26E, growing 6.1% (FY25: USD 297.2bn), with exports of USD 246.4bn. The per-segment split and the USD 10-12bn AI-revenue estimate are not in the published executive summary and could not be verified — do not use the '3-4% of tech revenue' framing without a primary citation.

verdicts.claim: Standalone 'prompt engineer' and basic annotation roles are shrinking; durable volume is in AI/ML engineer, data engineer, MLOps
verdicts.issue: The cited source (kaam.work blog) aggregates other secondary blogs (recrew.ai, theaicareerlab, dheya) which in turn cite Quess and LinkedIn — a four-deep citation chain with no primary document at the end, and I could not reach it to confirm even what it says. The specific figures (prompt-engineer postings down 30-40% from a 2023 peak, annotation work compressed by more than half, 9.2 lakh AI professionals vs 2.57 lakh in dedicated AI roles from ~3.5 lakh postings) have no verified primary source. The directional recommendation (position the QA track as evaluation engineering, not annotation) is sound product advice independent of the statistics, but the numbers should not be quoted to clients or investors.

verdicts.claim: Contract/flexi arrangements inside GCCs have risen to about 1 in 4 roles
verdicts.issue: Sourced to a single vendor blog (Ceipal) and self-flagged as the weakest number in the set — that self-assessment is correct and I found nothing to upgrade it. I can independently confirm the supporting hard filings the finding leans on (Quess: GCCs 71% of professional-staffing headcount and 68% of revenue), but neither the NASSCOM-Zinnov release nor the ISF research page I fetched publishes any contract-share-of-GCC-roles figure, which corroborates the finding's own warning. The 25%, the 'closer to 1 in 3 by FY27' projection and the '60-75% permanent / 25-40% contract optimal ratio' should be struck from any client-facing material.

verdicts.claim: AI adoption cuts junior employment by 7.7-10% at adopting firms, via slower hiring (Harvard/SSRN 5425555)
verdicts.issue: I was not able to fetch the SSRN working paper within this session's remaining capability, so neither the 7.7-10% range, the ~62 million workers / ~285,000 firms sample, the 'AI integrator' identification strategy, nor the six-quarter window is confirmed. Note this is a US-labour-market working paper (not peer-reviewed), and the finding's own framing as 'the strongest causal evidence' overstates the status of an unreplicated preprint. Its relevance to an Indian staffing business is indirect in any case, since the directly-measured India data in this same set runs the other way.

verdicts.claim: In the most AI-exposed US occupations the entry-level share of postings fell from 29% to 10% while senior share more than doubled
verdicts.issue: Fetched the Indeed Hiring Lab article (23 July 2026). The secondary figures are confirmed exactly: software development 69.3% senior-level and 4.5% entry-level in Q1 2026; entry-level postings -7.5% YoY and senior +14.7% YoY in May 2026. But the headline numbers of the claim — entry-level share in the most AI-exposed occupations falling 29% to 10% and senior share rising 22% to 47% between 2021 and 2026 — are NOT in the article. It states only that 'sectors with high AI exposure and/or more opportunities to work remotely, like tech, tend to have fewer entry-level roles', and gives an overall May 2026 distribution of ~14% senior / 40% mid / 46% entry-level, which is hard to reconcile with the claimed figures.
verdicts.corrected: Indeed Hiring Lab (23 July 2026) found entry-level postings down 7.5% YoY and senior-level postings up 14.7% YoY in May 2026, with software development at 69.3% senior-level and only 4.5% entry-level in Q1 2026. The specific 29%-to-10% entry-level and 22%-to-47% senior shares for AI-exposed occupations are not supported by the cited article and should be dropped.

verdicts.claim: NITI Aayog models a 2 million job contraction in tech services by 2031, naming QA engineers and L1 support as at risk
verdicts.issue: The cited official PDF (niti.gov.in Roadmap for Job Creation in the AI Economy) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on fetch, so I could not confirm the 8mn-to-6mn projection, the 1.8mn customer-experience figure, the naming of QA engineers and L1 support agents, or the 4mn AI-first-jobs upside. This is a government projection and the claim is directly adverse to Anvi's model, so it must be read in the original before being relied on in either direction. The 10 October 2025 release date is consistent with the URL path (2025-10) but is not itself confirmation of content.

verdicts.claim: TCS cut fresher offers ~43% YoY: 25,000 offers for FY27 against 44,000+ freshers hired in FY26
verdicts.issue: The Business Today article was not reachable within remaining capability, and I did not verify the CEO quote, the 25,000 FY27 figure, the 44,000+ FY26 actual, or the nine-months-training claim against TCS's own investor materials. A CEO quote relayed by a single outlet is thin for a number this load-bearing — TCS publishes quarterly fact sheets and earnings-call transcripts, and the figure should be taken from those. Note also that '25,000 offers for FY27' and '44,000 freshers hired in FY26' are different measures (offers vs onboardings), so the 43% arithmetic may not be a like-for-like comparison.

verdicts.claim: TCS shed 23,460 net employees in FY26 against an announced 12,200 cut, while onboarding 44,000 trainees
verdicts.issue: Not verified. The People Matters article was not reachable, and I did not open TCS's Q4 FY26 fact sheet (cited elsewhere in this set) to confirm the 584,519 closing headcount, the 23,460 net decline, the 12,200 announced restructuring, the CHRO quote, or the 593,798 / +9,279 Q1 FY27 recovery. Given that this figure is used to argue the fresher-absorber floor has gone, it should be read off TCS's own published fact sheet rather than trade press.

verdicts.claim: Wipro abandoned fresher hiring targets and its CHRO conceded campus intake has fallen four years running
verdicts.issue: Not verified — neither the People Matters nor the Business Today article was reachable. The 7,500 FY26 freshers, 3,000+ in Q4, the absence of an FY27 target, the two CHRO quotes, the -0.3% dollar revenue and 13.8% Q4 attrition are all unconfirmed. Direct quotes attributed to a named executive are exactly the kind of claim that should be sourced to the earnings-call transcript or the company's own press release before being used in a market narrative.

verdicts.claim: Wipro onboarded zero freshers in Q1 FY27 with headcount flat at ~243,000
verdicts.issue: Unverified, and the finding already flags that it 'appears only in secondary outlets, not in material I could verify against Wipro's own filing' — that self-assessment is correct and I was unable to improve on it. The cited source (indianpaycalculator.in) is a low-authority aggregator with no evident access to Wipro disclosures. A 'zero freshers' claim is unusually strong and absence of onboarding is rarely stated affirmatively in filings, so this should be treated as rumour until confirmed in Wipro's Q1 FY27 press release or call transcript.

verdicts.claim: Indian IT's headcount elasticity has broken: net addition of ~135,000 on a 6 million base in FY26
verdicts.issue: Verified in the NASSCOM Strategic Review 2026 executive summary (downloaded and extracted): 'Direct tech sector employment is projected to reach ~6 mn in FY26E, up 2.3% compared to last year, reflecting net addition of 135,000 employees' — exact. Revenue growth of 6.1% to USD 315.4bn also confirmed. Two defects: the FY25 comparison figure of ~133,000 net additions is not in the summary and is unverified; and the revenue range given as '$283-315bn' is wrong and internally inconsistent — the document states USD 297.2bn for FY25 and USD 315.4bn for FY26E, with no 283 figure anywhere. The 'volume to skill mix' quote was not located in the summary text.
verdicts.corrected: NASSCOM's Strategic Review 2026 projects direct tech sector employment reaching ~6 million in FY26E, up 2.3%, a net addition of about 135,000 — while revenue grew 6.1% to USD 315.4bn (FY25: USD 297.2bn). The FY25 net-addition comparison (~133,000) and the 'volume to skill mix' quote are unverified.

verdicts.claim: Accenture is exiting more than 11,000 staff who cannot be reskilled on AI, on a compressed timeline
verdicts.issue: The CNBC article was not reachable within remaining capability, so the Julie Sweet 'exiting on a compression timeline' quote, the 11,000 figure, the USD 865 million business optimisation programme, the 550,000 reskilled on GenAI fundamentals and the FY2026 headcount-growth statement are all unconfirmed. The quote is from a public earnings call (25-26 September 2025) and should be taken from Accenture's own transcript. Note this is the oldest datapoint in the set and predates everything else by a year, which weakens its relevance to a 2026 go-to-market decision.

verdicts.claim: Cognizant is raising fresher intake ~20% to 24,000-25,000 in 2026 because AI makes juniors billable faster
verdicts.issue: Not verified — the Angel One page was not reachable. The CFO quote, the 20,000 2025 hires, the ~20% increase, and the 16,000-on-projects / 4,000-in-training split are unconfirmed, and Angel One is a brokerage news aggregator rather than a primary source for Cognizant earnings commentary. This claim matters disproportionately because it is the main counterweight in the set to the fresher-collapse narrative, so it deserves a primary citation (Cognizant's own earnings call) rather than the weakest source in the chain.

verdicts.claim: Cognizant's CEO is publicly arguing for a flattened pyramid with more entry-level jobs
verdicts.issue: The Fortune article was not reachable, so the Ravi Kumar S quotes ('a little bit of fearmongering... I think there will be more jobs', the 'ton of jobs in the front... ton of jobs in the back' description), the two new entry-level titles (Frontier Certified Engineer, Frontier Business Operator) and the 'learnability' emphasis are unconfirmed. As with the preceding finding, this is a pro-Anvi datapoint resting on an unverified source — note that a CEO's public advocacy is in any case an opinion about the future, not evidence of current buying behaviour, and it sits against the verified Taggd data showing GCCs cutting fresher share from 21% to 16%.

verdicts.claim: India's fresher hiring data runs opposite to the US: fresher hiring +16% YoY in FY26 and AI/ML roles +45%
verdicts.issue: The Naukri blog post was not reachable. None of the figures are confirmed: FY26 white-collar +8%, fresher (0-3 years) +16%, AI/ML +45%, February 2026 fresher +17%, June 2026 fresher +8%, April-June +9%, July 2026 AI/ML +33%, IT-sector fresher +8% in February 2026. I can note from the primary September 2026 JobSpeak PDF that experience-level trends are published only as an image chart (0-3yrs, 4-7yrs, 8-12yrs, 13-15yrs, 16+yrs) with no extractable values, so even the current-month fresher figure is not machine-verifiable from the primary release. Treat all of these as trade-reported.

verdicts.claim: The channel Anvi sells into grew 10.1% in FY26, and GCCs accounted for 73% of all new staffing mandates
verdicts.issue: The BizzBuzz article was not reachable. Critically, I did fetch the ISF research page itself and it publishes no FY26 IT-staffing growth figure, no 1.91 million workforce figure, no 118,000 additions, no 73%-of-new-mandates figure and no Q4 FY26 QoQ figure — only the Q1 FY27 series (1.95mn, 7.5% YoY, 1.14 lakh added, IT 7% YoY / 2% QoQ). So the FY26 numbers are not on the industry body's own research page and rest entirely on a single secondary outlet's reading of an annual report I could not obtain. The 73% GCC-mandate figure in particular is reused across three findings in this set and is unverified in all of them.

verdicts.claim: GCCs are cutting fresher share from 21% to 16%, and a quarter expect headcount to fall
verdicts.issue: Duplicate of an earlier finding in this set and confirmed on the same fetch of the DQIndia article, published 30 August 2026: freshers 16% of expected FY27 hiring (down from 21%), 1-5 years at 30%, 52% expansion / 22% stable / 26% reductions, nearly half reporting >25% of open roles requiring AI capability, 78% external acquisition with 41% IT services / 32% other GCCs / 27% startups. Note for the write-up that this and the finding above it are the same survey counted twice — do not present them as two independent corroborating sources.

verdicts.claim: The binding constraint is fresher quality not volume: job-readiness 42.6% and 48% of critical roles take over 60 days
verdicts.issue: Confirmed on the same DQIndia fetch: 'quality mismatch' is named as the leading primary hiring constraint, graduate job-readiness is 42.6%, and 48% of critical roles take more than 60 days to fill. This is the strongest verified basis in the entire set for Anvi's screening value proposition. Two cautions: it duplicates an earlier finding (same survey, do not double-count); and the article attributes the 42.6% to Taggd rather than explicitly to the India Graduate Skills Index 2026, so adjust the attribution.

verdicts.claim: India's GenAI supply gap is 53%, only 16% of IT professionals have AI skills, entry GenAI pays 2x+ entry support
verdicts.issue: Verified via the CIOL report on TeamLease Digital's 'Digital Skills & Salary Primer FY2026-27' (published 29 September 2026): 53% GenAI supply gap, 55-60% cloud, 16% of IT professionals AI-skilled, ~20 lakh upskilled against only ~3 lakh with advanced AI, GenAI Developer at 0-2 years Rs 11.2 LPA. Not confirmed on that source: the 25-30% cybersecurity gap, Data Engineer Rs 9.1 LPA, Technical Support Engineer Rs 5.2 LPA, the 37,000-roles sample size, and the '10 lakh GenAI roles by 2026' projection. The 2x pay-ratio conclusion holds against the verified AI-Support band of Rs 4.8-5.4 LPA rather than the unverified Rs 5.2 LPA support figure.

verdicts.claim: Named employers have published AI-stratified fresher pay bands spanning roughly 6x within one cohort
verdicts.issue: The HRKatha article was not reachable, and none of the bands are confirmed: Infosys Systems Engineer Rs 3.6 LPA vs Specialist Programmer / Digital Specialist Engineer Rs 7-21 LPA; TCS Ninja Rs 3.36 LPA / Digital Rs 4.5 LPA / Prime Rs 7-11.5 LPA; HCLTech Elite Engineer Rs 18-22 LPA; Wipro Elite and Turbo Rs 3.5-6.5 LPA. These are company compensation claims assembled from three different outlets across different dates (Infosys December 2025, HCLTech 2026), so the '6x within the same graduating cohort' construction is an aggregation across employers and years rather than a published fact. Verify each band against the employer before using.

verdicts.claim: Infosys held fresher intake flat at 20,000 while total headcount fell 2.5% in a quarter
verdicts.issue: The People Matters article was not reachable and I did not open the Infosys 20-F or 6-K cited alongside it, so the 20,000 FY26 hires, the reaffirmed 20,000 FY27 target, 4,000 in Q1 FY27, 12,000 in H1 FY26, the 328,594 Q4 FY26 headcount, the 337,034 prior quarter, the -2.5% decline, attrition falling from 14.1% to 12.6%, and the HCLTech ~11,000 campus figure are all unconfirmed. Since Infosys files with the SEC, every one of these is available from a primary source and should be taken from there.

verdicts.claim: GCCs employ 2.36mn, prioritise redeployment over headcount growth, and 90%+ already partner with universities
verdicts.issue: Verified on the PR Newswire release: 2,117 GCCs, 3,728 units, 2.36 million professionals, USD 98.4bn FY26 revenue, 32% growth since FY2021, 250,000 AI professionals, 1,200+ GCCs with embedded AI/ML, over 90% of leading GCCs running university talent-pipeline partnerships, and the characterisation that organisations are 'prioritising redeployment and AI-led productivity over linear headcount growth'. Release date 2 July 2026, which matches this finding's stated date (and shows the 'published May 2026' in the earlier duplicate to be the error). The 'resilient and at moderate pace' hiring phrasing was not individually confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Specialised IT staffing outgrew general staffing ~6x at TeamLease, but revenue guidance missed badly
verdicts.issue: Verified in the TeamLease Q4 FY26 investor presentation (NSE archives, extracted locally) — and the apparent conflict with the other TeamLease finding in this set resolves cleanly. FY26 operating revenue was Rs 11,791 cr vs Rs 11,156 cr, exactly +5.69%, which is the Rs 117.90bn figure; total revenue was Rs 11,859 cr (+6%). Consolidated EBITDA Rs 158 cr, +14%. Q4 FY26 Specialised Staffing Rs 177 cr vs Rs 158 cr (the Rs 1,766m figure, ~+12%) against General Staffing Rs 2,671 cr vs Rs 2,623 cr (+1.8%, the Rs 26,714m figure). Unverified: the CFO's 20-22% growth guidance, the 28 new specialised customers, and the ~27,000-associate NBFC insourcing.

verdicts.claim: The pay-after-placement hire-train-deploy model is demonstrably cash-fragile in a hiring freeze
verdicts.issue: The Inc42 article was not reachable, so Masai School's revenue decline from Rs 36.84 Cr (FY23) to Rs 33.06 Cr (FY24), the 11.43% fall, the 69% loss reduction to Rs 13.2 Cr in FY25, the approach to a Rs 100 Cr topline, and the TeamLease EdTech benchmark that only 16.67% of Indian institutions place more than 75% of students within six months are all unconfirmed. Note the analytical tension: the same source is used to argue the model is fragile and that it recovered strongly, so even if verified it cuts both ways. The structural point about pay-after-placement working capital is sound reasoning rather than a sourced finding.

verdicts.claim: Anvi's home market is one of the fastest-growing GCC hubs in India (Telangana exports Rs 3.13 lakh crore, 197 GCCs)
verdicts.issue: The Deccan Herald article was not reachable, so Telangana IT exports of Rs 3.13 lakh crore in 2024-25 (+16.6%), IT employment of 9.39 lakh, the 197 GCCs attracted since December 2023, the 70+/84/43 annual breakdown, and the '~20% of India's GCCs across 350-450 active centres' are unconfirmed. I can independently confirm from the primary JobSpeak annexure that Hyderabad is the fastest-growing major metro for white-collar hiring (+9% YoY), which supports the location thesis through a different and fully verified route — use that instead until the state figures are sourced officially.

verdicts.claim: Engineering employability is high but slipping; CS/IT graduates are the most employable cohort in India
verdicts.issue: The Careers360 article was not reachable, so the India Skills Report 2026 figures — overall employability 56.35% (up from ~54.8%), BE/BTech 70.15% (down from 71.5%), computer science 80%, IT 78%, and '90%+ of employees report using GenAI tools' — are unconfirmed. Note the internal tension with a verified figure elsewhere in this set: the Taggd/GCC survey puts graduate job-readiness at 42.6%, roughly half the 80% CS employability claimed here. Those two numbers measure different things, and presenting either without the other would be misleading.

verdicts.claim: FDM Group, the listed pure-play hire-train-deploy firm, shrank sharply — revenue -31%, consultants -22%
verdicts.issue: Verified against the RNS annual results on the FCA's National Storage Mechanism. Every figure exact: FY2025 revenue GBP 177.7m vs GBP 257.7m (-31%); profit before tax GBP 7.6m vs GBP 28.1m (-73%); consultants assigned to clients at year end 2,003 vs 2,578 (-22%); consultants coached 828 vs 877. Announcement date 18 March 2026, for the year ended 31 December 2025. The company also reported GBP 35.3m cash and no debt, which is relevant context the finding omits — FDM shrank but remained profitable and solvent. The separate H1 2026 figure (-19% to GBP 78.6m) is from Staffing Industry Analyst and unverified.

verdicts.claim: Revature has abandoned the fresher bench and now sells experienced AI-native Forward Deployed Engineers
verdicts.issue: Fetched the live Revature page; the strategic thesis is confirmed and is the most important competitive signal in the set — the page sells experienced AI-native engineers, explicitly contrasting Forward Deployed Engineers against Full Stack Developers, with no pricing or guarantees published. Confirmed figures: 1-2 weeks to first contribution, 40-55% lower TCO in year one, 85-90% reduction in PoC-to-production failure, ~80% lower attrition, Palantir USD 1.14m revenue per employee, 1,165% FDE demand surge in 2025. Two figures understate the page: delivery compression is advertised as 4-10x velocity, not '3x+', and project ramp is 'just days', not '~1 week'. The page also claims a 70-80% SDLC handoff latency cut and that 85% of AI/ML projects fail beyond PoC. The 1,343 headcount (Tracxn, May 2026) and the 2 April 2026 FDE Accelerator launch date are unverified.
verdicts.corrected: Revature's current hire-train-deploy page sells experienced AI-native engineers 'built for the AI era', claiming first contribution in 1-2 weeks, a ramp of 'just days', 4-10x delivery velocity, a 70-80% cut in SDLC handoff latency, 40-55% lower TCO in year one, 85-90% reduction in PoC-to-production failure and ~80% lower attrition. It cites Palantir's USD 1.14m revenue per employee and a 1,165% FDE demand surge in 2025. No pricing or guarantees are published. Headcount (~1,343) and the launch date are unverified.

verdicts.claim: Andela occupies almost exactly Anvi's intended position globally and publishes the proof Anvi lacks
verdicts.issue: Verified on andela.com. Tagline 'The Human Layer Powering Production AI' exact; 17,000 certified AI-native engineers; 200,000+ technologists trained since 2014; 98% enterprise client satisfaction; G2 4.7 stars from 329 reviews; Builders / Integrators / Scalers team roles; Training-as-a-Service covering LLM engineering, agentic AI systems, AI in production (LLMOps) and AI strategy; no pricing and no time-to-deploy SLA published. Named logos confirmed include Goldman Sachs, GitHub, Capital One, SoFi, Johnson & Johnson and Indeed, plus Lattice, Coursera, WPP, Gopuff, The Weather Company and Resy. Unverified: the USD 381m total funding (Wikipedia) and 'quarterly AI engineer cohort releases'.

verdicts.claim: Quess Corp sells the identical hire-train-deploy product at 478,594-person scale
verdicts.issue: The financial scale is verified exactly in the Quess Q4 FY26 investor presentation: FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 15,305 cr (+2% YoY), consolidated EBITDA Rs 312 cr (+19%), headcount 4,78,594 (+4%), PAT Rs 222 cr. The deck also confirms the segment structure consistent with the post-demerger perimeter (General, Professional and Overseas staffing only). Unverified because I did not fetch the product page: the 6-8 week upskilling window, the virtual-labs and on-site/virtual/hybrid delivery detail, the 'project-ready from day one' phrasing, and the absence of published pricing/SLA/placement numbers. The 1 April 2025 demerger effective date and the Digitide/Bluspring/Foundit allocation are also unverified.

verdicts.claim: Indian specialised staffing earns roughly 7% EBITDA, capping a pure body-shop model
verdicts.issue: Verified exactly in the TeamLease Q4 FY26 investor presentation consolidated segment results. Specialised Staffing Services FY26 revenue Rs 669 cr (FY25 Rs 592 cr, +13%), FY26 EBITDA Rs 49.8 cr (+15%), FY26 segment EBITDA margin 7.4% and Q4 FY26 7.3%, against General Staffing and Allied Services at 1.1% in every quarter shown and for both full years. FY26 consolidated PAT Rs 147 cr, +33%. The one figure not matching is the consolidated revenue: the deck shows Rs 11,859 cr total / Rs 11,791 cr operating, not Rs 11,859 cr described as 'revenue' alone — immaterial here. Management's stated 8-9% four-to-five-quarter objective was not located in the deck and is unverified.

verdicts.claim: Indian IT staffing is growing and GCCs, not IT services firms, are the buyer (ISF data)
verdicts.issue: Fetched the ISF research page. Only the Q1 FY27 figures are supported: 1.95m formal flexi workers, 7.5% YoY industry growth, IT staffing 7% YoY. Everything else in the claim is absent from the page: the FY26 1.18 lakh formal jobs added (+8%), the IT segment at 10.1% YoY, the ~73% of new IT staffing mandates from GCCs, and the market sizing (USD 4.9bn / 5.97 lakh workers FY24 rising to ~USD 5.6bn / 6.63 lakh by FY26). Note also that the claim's own framing is misleading: ISF's Q1 FY27 data shows IT staffing growing more slowly than the overall industry (7% vs 7.5% YoY, 2% vs 2.6% QoQ), so 'Indian IT staffing is growing' is true but it is lagging, not leading.
verdicts.corrected: ISF reports members representing 1.95m formal flexi workers in Q1 FY27, with industry growth of 7.5% YoY and IT staffing at 7% YoY — i.e. IT staffing is growing but trailing the overall market. The FY26 figures (1.18 lakh jobs added, IT at 10.1%), the 73%-of-new-mandates GCC share, and the USD 4.9bn/USD 5.6bn market sizing are not published on the ISF research page and are unverified.

verdicts.claim: The specific gap Anvi targets is real and quantified by a competitor (Quess GCC tech talent shortfall)
verdicts.issue: The February 2026 leg is verified via the Storyboard18 article (published 26 February 2026): 43% shortfall in AI/ML operations and data analytics, 38% in platform engineering, an 18-43% range across high-demand domains, and 1,850-1,900 active GCCs — all exact. The article also gives Q3 FY26 QoQ hiring growth of 4-6% and notes tier-2 cities at 9-10% share. The Q1 FY27 leg is NOT verified: the 36-40% AI/data/analytics gap, the 16.7% share of hiring demand, ~10% QoQ growth against 5-6% overall, the three-to-six-month external hiring time and the ~1.7x salary premium all come from a CRN India report I did not reach, and the 15 July 2026 release date is unconfirmed.
verdicts.corrected: Quess Corp's India GCC Tech Talent Landscape report of 26 February 2026 puts role-level shortfalls at 43% for AI/ML operations and data analytics and 38% for platform engineering, an 18-43% range across high-demand domains, across 1,850-1,900 active GCCs, with Q3 FY26 GCC hiring up 4-6% QoQ. The Q1 FY27 figures (36-40% gap, 16.7% of hiring demand, ~10% QoQ, 3-6 month fill times, ~1.7x premium) are unverified.

verdicts.claim: Hyderabad is the fastest-growing GCC market in India (Zinnov-NASSCOM), validating Anvi's location
verdicts.issue: The national totals are confirmed via the NASSCOM-Zinnov PR Newswire release: 2,117 GCCs, 3,728 units, USD 98.4bn, 2.36m professionals, 32% growth since FY2021, 506 Forbes Global 2000 companies. But '506k+ AI/ML talent' is almost certainly a misreading of that same 506 Forbes Global 2000 figure — the release puts AI talent in the GCC ecosystem at ~250,000, not 506,000, so the claim doubles the real number. Also unverified (the Zinnov page was not reached): Hyderabad's 515+ GCC units, ~14% share, 75+ added in the past year, the 40-46% share of new GCC setups, the BFSI/pharma/semiconductor strength, and Xpheno's ~180,000 FY26 hires projection. Note the 14%-of-stock and 40-46%-of-new-setups figures are different measures and must not be presented as one.
verdicts.corrected: The Zinnov-NASSCOM India GCC Landscape Report 2026 counts 2,117 GCCs across 3,728 units, USD 98.4bn revenue and 2.36m professionals, up 32% since FY2021, with 506 Forbes Global 2000 companies operating GCCs in India and ~250,000 AI professionals in the ecosystem (not 506k AI/ML talent). Hyderabad's unit count, ~14% stock share and reported 40-46% share of new setups are unverified and measure different things.

verdicts.claim: GCC buyers are choosing to reskill their own people rather than buy external AI talent
verdicts.issue: None of the three legs was verified: the PwC India-FICCI figures (72% of GCCs needing to reskill >40% of workforce, 62% citing absence of domain-plus-technology professionals, 27% leadership AI literacy, 8.69 months to full productivity), the EY GCC Pulse figures (81% upskilling internal teams on GenAI, 71% saying reskilling shapes core talent strategy), and the July 2026 Quess study. I could not reach the CRN Asia page. This is the single most strategically adverse claim in the set for Anvi's thesis, and it is also corroborated in direction by the one survey I did verify (Taggd: 22% of GCC talent developed internally, 78% external — which actually cuts against the 'reskill rather than buy' framing). Worth resolving properly before it shapes positioning.

verdicts.claim: The entry-level AI-exposed job market is contracting (Stanford, 19% below less-exposed peers)
verdicts.issue: Verified on the Stanford Digital Economy Lab publication page. Title 'Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence', authors Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen, ADP administrative payroll data through June 2026, employment for 22-25 year olds in the most AI-exposed occupations '19% below where it would be had it kept pace with that of their less-exposed peers', and the decline operating 'primarily through reduced hiring of young workers rather than increased separations'. Revision dates confirmed: 12 August 2026 and a 9 February 2026 update. One element unverified: that the gap 'widened from 13% in the August 2025 release' — the page does not state the original figure. US data, so applicability to India is indirect.

verdicts.claim: India's traditional fresher absorber shrank in FY26 (TCS headcount -23,460)
verdicts.issue: I did not open the cited TCS Q4 FY26 fact sheet, so the 584,519 closing headcount, the 23,460 FY26 decline, the 11,151 single-quarter net fall in the December 2025 quarter, the 2,356 net addition in Q4 FY26, 13.7% Q4 attrition and the 114,000+ employees with higher-order AI skills are unconfirmed; so are the Wipro 7,500-8,000 revised guidance and Infosys ~20,000. This is the third finding in the set resting on the same unverified TCS FY26 headcount story. Since the fact sheet is a primary document on tcs.com, there is no reason to rely on IANS or Business Today for it — read it before using the number.

verdicts.claim: Headcount growth across India's tech sector is only ~2%, so Anvi competes for a thin increment
verdicts.issue: Verified in the NASSCOM Strategic Review 2026 executive summary: USD 315.4bn FY26E, +6.1% (FY25 USD 297.2bn), direct employment ~6m in FY26E, +2.3%, net addition 135,000, exports USD 246.4bn (+5.6%) led by ER&D (7.7%) and BPM (7%) with IT services at 4.1%. The FY25 +5.9% growth figure, the segment split (IT services USD 149bn, BPM USD 59bn, ER&D USD 63bn, software products USD 23bn, hardware USD 21bn) and the USD 10-12bn AI revenue estimate are NOT in the executive summary — I grepped every dollar-billion figure in the document and the segment values do not appear. The headline conclusion is sound; the supporting breakdown is not sourced.
verdicts.corrected: NASSCOM Strategic Review 2026 projects the Indian technology sector at USD 315.4bn in FY26E, +6.1%, with exports of USD 246.4bn (+5.6%), led by ER&D (7.7%) and BPM (7%) against IT services at 4.1%. Direct employment reaches ~6m in FY26E, up 2.3%, a net addition of 135,000. The per-segment revenue split and the USD 10-12bn AI revenue estimate are not in the published executive summary and are unverified.

verdicts.claim: The freelance-marketplace substitute is being eaten by AI itself (Upwork Q2 2026)
verdicts.issue: The Next Web article was not reachable, so Upwork's Q2 2026 revenue of USD 191.7m (-2% YoY), the FY2026 guidance cut from USD 760-790m to USD 730-750m, the Q3 guide of USD 176-184m against ~USD 194m consensus, the CEO's 'faster pace of AI-related automation' attribution, GSV of USD 966.4m (-4%), active clients of 763,000 (-4%), the ~USD 330m annualised AI-related segment (+22%), AI consulting +50% and FY2025 revenue of USD 787.8m are all unconfirmed. Upwork is a US-listed issuer, so all of this is in a 10-Q and press release — use those. Note the claim is also internally mixed: the same company reports its AI-related work growing 22-50%, which undercuts the 'AI eats human hours' reading.

verdicts.claim: Mercor has built a multi-billion-dollar business out of AI-evaluation and expert-data work
verdicts.issue: The Sacra page was not reachable. None of the figures are confirmed: ~USD 2bn annualised gross revenue by June 2026, USD 760m at end-2025, USD 614m gross revenue in H1 2026, the 60-70% contractor take-rate and implied USD 180-250m net revenue, the USD 350m Series C at a USD 10bn valuation in October 2025, USD 485.6m total funding, and ~USD 20bn talks in July 2026. These are private-company figures from a subscription research aggregator with no issuer disclosure behind them, and gross-vs-net revenue for a marketplace is exactly where such estimates go wrong — the finding's own 60-70% pass-through adjustment shows the headline number is not comparable to Anvi's revenue in any case.

verdicts.claim: micro1 shows how fast a vetted-AI-talent entrant can scale and how much capital the category attracts
verdicts.issue: The TechCrunch article was not reachable, so the growth from ~USD 7m annualised in early 2025 to more than USD 500m, the USD 35m Series A at a USD 500m valuation in September 2025, and the reported ~USD 4bn valuation on a USD 100m+ raise are unconfirmed. Private-company revenue multiples of this magnitude (70x in eighteen months) reported through secondary aggregators warrant particular scepticism. The strategic point — that well-capitalised competitors make the same 'pre-screened, deploy fast' promise — is independently supported by the Andela and Revature pages I did verify, so the argument does not depend on these numbers.

verdicts.claim: India's annotation/AI-data industry — the market Anvi cites on its homepage — is owned by specialists
verdicts.issue: The premise is confirmed: I fetched anviinnovate.com and the Grand View 'USD 8.60 billion by 2030, 21.9% CAGR (2025-2030)' citation is indeed on the site, and it is the AI training dataset market. But the claim overstates it as the market Anvi cites, singular — the site carries four other statistics, all talent/skills-demand ones. And the annotation-industry figures themselves are unverified (the Substack market map was not reachable): ~200,000 Indian annotators, ~half the global workforce, USD 209m domestic market in 2023 at 29-35% CAGR, NASSCOM's USD 7bn-by-2030 and million-jobs projection, iMerit's ~7,000 employees, and Scale AI's USD 870m 2024 revenue with ~1,200 employees.
verdicts.corrected: Anvi's homepage does cite the AI training dataset market (USD 8.60bn by 2030, 21.9% CAGR 2025-2030, Grand View Research) — confirmed on the live site — and that is an annotation/AI-data market served by firms like iMerit and Scale AI rather than a talent market. It is, however, one of five statistics on the page, the other four being talent-demand stats. The India annotation market figures (200,000 annotators, USD 209m in 2023, USD 7bn by 2030) are unverified.

verdicts.claim: 'Deploy in days' is already a commodity claim made by dozens of small firms
verdicts.issue: I did not reach the KORE1 page or the various India bench-vendor pages, so the specific claims (KORE1's 17-day average time-to-hire for GenAI engineers and five-business-day placement, gNxt's 1-2 weeks, the 48-72 hour profile delivery, 5-day minimums, the 9-day average across 60 AI bench placements) are unconfirmed. I can partially corroborate the thesis from sources I did verify: Revature advertises first contribution in 1-2 weeks and a ramp of 'just days', and neither Revature nor Andela nor Quess publishes a time-to-deploy SLA. So 'speed claims are common and unevidenced' is supportable; the specific competitor numbers are not.

verdicts.claim: Buying an AI coding agent is now cheap enough to be a genuine alternative to a junior engineer
verdicts.issue: The cited source is a secondary pricing aggregator (usagepricing.com) summarising Cognition's pricing rather than Cognition's own page, and I did not reach it. None of the tiers, the ~USD 2.25 per Agent Compute Unit, the ~USD 9 per agent-hour derivation, or the 'six to seven figures annually' enterprise range is confirmed. The '30-50% reduction in need for junior developers' is attributed only to unnamed 'reports'. The LeadDev finding that 54% of engineering leaders plan to hire fewer juniors is from a 2025 survey via CIO.com and also unverified. SaaS pricing changes frequently, so a July-2026 third-party snapshot is weak evidence for a 2026 go-to-market decision.

verdicts.claim: GCC-as-a-service (ANSR/Accenture) is the structural substitute for buying staffing
verdicts.issue: The HFS Research page was not reachable, so ANSR's 125+ GCCs set up over 18+ years, USD 2bn+ enabled capital investment, 125,000+ professionals hired, 2m+ sq ft managed, the subscription-plus-services model, Accenture's USD 170m July 2024 investment, the joint GCC services launch and the board seat are all unconfirmed. Note that the strategic inference — 'a buyer that engages ANSR/Accenture does not separately buy a trained AI bench' — is an assertion rather than something the source could establish; GCC-builders routinely use contract staffing vendors during ramp-up, so this may overstate the substitution effect even if the ANSR figures are accurate.

verdicts.claim: Outcome-priced AI services are the other substitute, and Fractal Analytics just IPO'd in India
verdicts.issue: The IndiaIPO page was not reachable, so Fractal's FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 32,997m against Rs 27,654m in FY25, the 16 February 2026 NSE/BSE listing, the ~Rs 2,834 crore IPO subscribed 2.66x, and the Rs 100 crore+ PAT in Q3 FY26 are unconfirmed. Fractal is now a listed Indian issuer, so these figures are available from its own filings and from NSE/BSE archives and should be taken from there rather than from an IPO-news site. The competitive inference (buyers can purchase a delivered outcome instead of staffing a team) is reasonable but is a positioning argument, not a finding the source establishes.

verdicts.claim: Buyers are repricing labour-based delivery downward, compressing the per-seat staffing model
verdicts.issue: The Futurum Group press release was not reachable, so the 1H 2026 buyer-survey findings (43% preferring consumption-based pricing, 27% outcome-based) are unconfirmed, as are the trade-press claims of clients demanding 25-30% lower prices, ~80% of TCS's finance/HR/business-services contracts priced on outcomes, and TCS's 10-15% AI productivity savings passed to clients. The replacement-warranty benchmarks (30-90 days standard, 7-business-day SLA with pro-rata exit at 14 days) are sourced only to unnamed 'vendor comparison pages'. Note that the SBI RFP I did verify shows the opposite structure for Indian enterprise IT staffing: per-hour rate cards with reverse-auction price discovery, not outcome pricing.

verdicts.claim: Telangana's free AI skilling programmes are a substitute for Anvi's training and show training without deployment fails
verdicts.issue: I did not reach it.telangana.gov.in or the NASSCOM Community article, so TASK's 2.3 lakh students trained with ~11,000 placements (the sub-5% conversion that carries the argument), the 2,000+ basic AI/ML and 5,000+ deep-tech trainees, the five-lakh-professionals-by-2027 commitment, T-AIM, and the Pearson MoU and Aikam entity are all unconfirmed. These are state-government programme claims, so under the official-source rule they need the Telangana IT department's own publication. The sub-5% placement conversion is the load-bearing number and is also the most likely to be a denominator artefact (cumulative trainees against a single period's placements), so verify the basis before using it.

verdicts.claim: India's edtech-staffing hybrids already sell HTD with larger claimed talent pools and enterprise relationships
verdicts.issue: I did not reach the upGrad Rekrut page or the other vendor sites, so none of the specifics is confirmed: the January 2021 Rekrut acquisition, the claimed 10m upskilled talent pool, upGrad Enterprise's ~six-week role-specific programmes, NIIT StackRoute NewHire, Alp Consulting's 30 years and end-to-end HTD offer, or NLB Services' founding year, Noida location, 5,001-10,000 headcount and Data & AI practice. The competitive conclusion is plausible and is partly corroborated by the Quess, Revature and Andela pages I did verify, but a claim that competitors have '10m upskilled talent' should be checked before it is used to argue Anvi is outgunned — such vendor-marketing pool figures are rarely meaningful.

verdicts.claim: Quess bills roughly Rs 1.10 lakh per deployed head per month in professional/IT staffing
verdicts.issue: Verified against the Quess Q4 FY26 investor presentation, which states on its segment-overview slide: Professional Staffing headcount 7,066 (1.5%), revenue Rs 930 Cr (6%), operational EBITDA Rs 111 Cr (30%). The arithmetic is exact: Rs 930 cr / 7,066 = Rs 13.16 lakh per head per year = Rs 1,09,700 per head per month. The deck also confirms GCC at 71% of Professional Staffing headcount and 67% of revenue in Q4 FY26, matching the claim's parenthetical. The inference that an entry-level bench prices well below a mixed-seniority average is sound reasoning and is independently supported by the verified TeamLease AI-Support band of Rs 4.8-5.4 LPA.

verdicts.claim: Segment operating profit is only about Rs 13,100 per deployed head per month, 11.9% of billing
verdicts.issue: Verified and the arithmetic is exact. Quess Q4 FY26 presentation: Professional Staffing FY26 operational EBITDA Rs 111 Cr on Rs 930 Cr revenue = 11.94%, and Rs 111 cr / 7,066 heads / 12 months = Rs 13,090 per head per month. The Q4 FY26 quarterly margin is shown as 12.7% on the segment chart (note the Q1 FY27 deck restates the same quarter as 12.8% — a trivial restatement, but quote one deck consistently). The caveat that this is segment operational EBITDA before corporate/IDC allocation is correct and material: group consolidated EBITDA margin was 2.0% in FY26. Management's 11-12% medium-term guidance was not located in the deck and is unverified.

verdicts.claim: TeamLease runs the same business at roughly half: Rs 67,900 revenue and Rs 4,633 EBITDA per head per month
verdicts.issue: Verified against the TeamLease Q4 FY24 investor presentation and the arithmetic is exact to the rupee. FY24 Specialised Staffing Services revenue Rs 589 cr (FY23 Rs 566 cr), FY24 EBITDA Rs 40.2 cr, FY24 margin 6.8%, FY23 margin 7.7%, and FY-24 Q4 Specialised Staffing headcount 7,230. Rs 589 cr / 7,230 / 12 = Rs 67,890 and Rs 40.2 cr / 7,230 / 12 = Rs 4,633. The resulting 7-12% operating-margin band and Rs 4,600-13,100 per-head contribution range is a fair synthesis — though note FY24 is now two years stale and TeamLease's FY26 specialised margin had recovered to 7.4%, so the low end of the band has moved up slightly.

verdicts.claim: Quess management's own cross-check puts India IT-staffing gross margin per head at ~17.5x general staffing, ~Rs 12,000/month
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in the Quess Q4FY23 & FY23 earnings call transcript (18 May 2023). Lohit Bhatia: 'For every one resource gross margin added in the American business ... it compares to about 20 people's gross margin added in the India IT staffing business and close to 350 people's gross margin added in general staffing in India.' And separately in the prepared remarks: 'The per associate per month gross margin profile, which is also known as PAPM, stayed stable and in a range of about 670 to 700.' The derivation (350/20 = 17.5x; 17.5 x Rs 670-700 = Rs 11,725-12,250) is arithmetically sound and lands within 10% of the Rs 13,090 independently derived from the FY26 segment accounts — a genuinely useful triangulation.

verdicts.claim: General staffing yields only Rs 670-700 gross margin per associate per month, forcing a sub-scale firm into IT staffing
verdicts.issue: The PAPM range is verified verbatim in the Quess Q4FY23 call transcript as quoted above. The segment-margin contrast is confirmed from the filings I extracted: Quess General Staffing FY26 operational EBITDA of Rs 189 cr on Rs 13,176 cr revenue = 1.43% (the claim's 1.4-1.5% range is right), and the TeamLease Q4 FY26 presentation shows General Staffing and Allied Services at a 1.1% EBITDA margin in every quarter of FY25 and FY26 with consolidated EBITDA margin of 1.34% in FY26 — consistent with the claim's 1.2-1.3% FY25 figure and its explanation that general staffing dominates the mix. The cited ICRA rationale was not separately opened for this point.

verdicts.claim: Indian IT staffing runs on 'pay-and-collect'; general staffing's cash-positive 'collect-and-pay' is unavailable in this segment
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in the Frost & Sullivan 'Assessment of Staffing Solutions Market in India' prepared for FirstMeridian (downloaded and extracted). The report states collect-and-pay 'is predominantly used in General Staffing only', and 'Pay-and-collect: After billing the end users, staffing companies pay the salaries of the temporary staff first and then collect the revenues from clients. This is the prevalent model in IT Staffing and Professional Staffing.' The Quess contrast is also confirmed: the Q4 FY26 deck shows Collect & Pay at 76% of general staffing with Average AR DSO of 15 days, and the Q1 FY27 deck shows 'GS DSO days at 28'. The consolidated 24-day DSO figure was not found in either deck and is unverified. This is the single most important working-capital finding in the set.

verdicts.claim: Rate-card billing is the convention in Indian IT staffing, but fixed mark-ups are a documented margin trap
verdicts.issue: Both legs verified. Frost & Sullivan lists exactly three billing models: Fixed Fee ('more prevalent in the General Staffing Solutions segment'), Rate Card ('based on a rate card or bill rates per hour that varies across skill set and experience... This is the common method in IT Staffing and Professional Staffing segments') and Percentage of Salary ('charged a certain percentage on the total cost of the temporary staff'). And the ICRA rating rationale on TeamLease Digital (19 November 2024, extracted locally) states margins are 'expected to improve over the medium term, supported by gradual changes in contracts to variable mark-up, especially with' new clients — confirming the fixed-markup-erosion mechanism. The January 2026 ICRA rationale was not separately opened.

verdicts.claim: Indian IT staffing is extremely fragmented with low entry barriers; the top seven held just 16.6% share
verdicts.issue: Verified exactly in the Frost & Sullivan report. 'The IT Staffing Solutions Segment market is estimated to be INR 260 billion in FY 2022... From FY 2022 - FY2026 the IT Staffing Solutions segment market is forecast to grow at a CAGR of 20.4% to reach INR 546.0 billion.' Market share FY2022 chart: Quess 4.6%, Genius Consultants 4.0%, ManpowerGroup 2.1%, TeamLease 1.7%, Randstad 1.7%, Adecco 1.5%, FirstMeridian 0.9%, Others 83.4% — every figure matches, and the named players sum to 16.5-16.6%. The attribution is also verbatim: 'High growth witnessed by the segment in the last decade and low entry barriers have resulted in a large base of small to medium companies.' Note the report is from January 2023, so FY2026 is a forecast, not an actual.

verdicts.claim: IT flexi staffing is the fastest-growing staffing segment (+12.3% YoY) even as the overall market slowed
verdicts.issue: The Outlook Business article was not reachable, so the Q1 FY26 figures (total flexi +6.1% YoY / +1.5% QoQ, IT staffing +12.3% YoY / +5.5% QoQ, general staffing +5.8% YoY, 1.83 million formal contract workforce at June 2025, 91,500 net new positions, FY25 +9.7% with 1.39 lakh additions on a 1.8 million base) are unconfirmed, and none of them appears on the ISF research page I did fetch. Note the important temporal caveat: this is Q1 FY26 (June 2025) data, and the current ISF position I verified for Q1 FY27 shows IT staffing at 7% YoY and 2% QoQ — i.e. decelerated and now trailing general staffing. The 'fastest-growing segment' framing is a year out of date.

verdicts.claim: The entry-level AI band a freshly-trained graduate maps to is Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh, not Rs 11-13 lakh
verdicts.issue: Verified via CIOL's report on TeamLease Digital's 'Digital Skills & Salary Primer FY2026-27' (29 September 2026). Confirmed: the AI-Core / AI-Adjacent / AI-Support categorisation; entry-level AI-Core in GCCs Rs 13.2 lakh; GenAI Developer at 0-2 years Rs 11.2 lakh; entry-level AI-Support Rs 4.8-5.4 lakh. This is the most commercially consequential verified pricing finding in the set. One flag: the concluding step — 'which implies a bill rate of roughly Rs 55,000-70,000 per month, not Rs 1.2 lakh+' — is the analyst's own derivation, not a figure in the source, and it also assumes the bench maps to AI-Support rather than AI-Core. Present it as an inference, not a published benchmark.

verdicts.claim: TeamLease can fill only ~30% of client openings, failing on salary expectations, location and skills
verdicts.issue: The Reuters-via-Yahoo article was not reachable, so the 30% fill rate and the attribution to salary-expectation, location and skills mismatches are unconfirmed. The supporting figures are partially verified from elsewhere: the 53% GenAI supply gap and 55-60% cloud gap are confirmed via CIOL's report on TeamLease Digital's FY2026-27 primer, but the 'roughly one qualified engineer per ten open GenAI roles' ratio is not. The reconciliation argument in the detail field — that clients are short of proven mid-level people at an acceptable price, which does not convert into willingness to pay for unproven juniors — is sound analysis and is independently supported by the verified Taggd external-sourcing split (41% IT services, 32% other GCCs, 27% startups).

verdicts.claim: Skilled/IT staffing needs ~1 internal employee per 22 deployed contractors, 16x general staffing's overhead ratio
verdicts.issue: Verified exactly in the TeamLease Q4 FY24 investor presentation, which publishes both tables. Core-count breakdown Q4FY24: Staffing and DA 839, Specialised Staffing 320, EdTech 382, HRTech 391, Regtech 170, Support functions 102, total 2,204. FTE Productivity table FY-24 Q4: headcount 311,800, core employees 829, productivity 371. So Specialised Staffing is 320 core for 7,230 associates = 1:22.6, against 371:1 for Staffing and DA — a 16.4x ratio, exactly as claimed. The Quess comparison is also confirmed: the Q4 FY26 deck's Associate:Core FTE (GS) chart shows 270 for Q4'26 (349, 307, 286, 279, 270 across the five quarters). Minor: the deck shows both 829 and 839 for Staffing and DA core count in different tables.

verdicts.claim: A well-capitalised incumbent entering IT staffing in a new market burned Rs 11 crore in a year, targeting 'a few hundred deployed resources'
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in the Quess Q4FY23 & FY23 earnings call transcript (18 May 2023). Prepared remarks: 'In North America, we made an investment of about INR 11 crore in FY23. We expect the business to breakeven by H1 FY24.' In Q&A, CFO Kamal Pal Hoda confirms 'It is on a full year basis, its INR 11 crore' and, asked about the quarter, 'It will be close to INR 3 crore this quarter.' And Lohit Bhatia: 'Our medium-term goal is to steadily go beyond a few hundred deployed resources.' The finding is also careful about scope — this is the North America build-out, not India — which is the right framing, and the inference that breakeven in IT staffing is a tens-to-low-hundreds-of-heads problem is a reasonable read of the disclosure.

verdicts.claim: GST of 18% applies to the entire invoice value of contract staffing, payable on invoice date not collection
verdicts.issue: Two problems. First, the official-source rule: this is a tax-rate and tax-base claim sourced only to ClearTax, a commercial practice guide. No CBIC notification, GST Council decision or official rate schedule was verified, and the September 2025 GST rate rationalisation makes a stale secondary page a real risk — so the 18% rate and SAC 998513 classification must be re-confirmed against CBIC before use. ClearTax does support 18% on SAC 998513 'Contract Staffing' and that service charges, EPF and ESI deductions are included in the value of supply ('All such charges should be included in the value of supply'), which backs the full-invoice-value point. Second, a substantive error: the claim's reverse-charge sentence is wrong. ClearTax says RCM applies where the supplying agency is UNREGISTERED. The body-corporate / non-body-corporate forward-vs-reverse distinction is the rule for security services (SAC 998521), not manpower supply generally.
verdicts.corrected: Contract staffing / manpower supply is generally treated as SAC 998513 at 18% GST, with the taxable value including the service charge, mark-up on salaries, administrative fees and reimbursable costs forming part of consideration — so for a firm billing Rs 1 lakh per head of which ~Rs 87,000 is pass-through salary, GST is on the full Rs 1 lakh, creating a float of ~18% of gross billing between invoice and collection. Verify the rate and SAC against the current CBIC rate schedule before relying on it; no official source was confirmed here, and the 2025 rate rationalisation may have changed the position. Delete the body-corporate/reverse-charge sentence: reverse charge on manpower supply turns on the supplier being unregistered, not on its constitution — the body-corporate test applies to security services (SAC 998521).

verdicts.claim: The four Labour Codes in force from 21 November 2025 raise cost-to-company: FTE gratuity after one year, and the 50% wage rule
verdicts.issue: Verified in the Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas guide (downloaded and extracted), which records the operative government act: 'On November 21, 2025, by notifications issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment' the Codes came into force. On fixed-term employment, verbatim: FTEs are entitled to 'parity in wages, working hours, allowances and other benefits similar to those extended to permanent workers'; 'all statutory benefits... proportionate to their period of employment'; and 'gratuity benefits if they render service for at least 1 year under the contract'. The cost quote is also verbatim: 'Employers will have to assess the cost impact consequent to engagement of fixed term employees.' The 50% rule is confirmed: 'if the aggregate amount of exclusions exceeds 50% of the total remuneration, the amount in excess of 50%, will be deemed as remuneration and be added to wages.' Two caveats: the guide's impact list names social security benefits, retrenchment compensation, gratuity, notice pay and leave encashment — not bonus; and the base statutory load percentages (EPF ~13%, ESIC 3.25% to Rs 21,000, gratuity 4.81%, bonus 8.33%) are standard but were not verified against any official source.

verdicts.claim: The OSH Code introduces a core-activity prohibition on contract labour plus contractor licensing, with a specific carve-out
verdicts.issue: Verified in detail in the CAM guide, and this is the most operationally useful legal finding in the set. Confirmed: 'a single unified threshold of 50 or more contract labour for applicability'; 'The OSH Code also allows contractors, who supply manpower to obtain a work-specific license for project-based work orders and a national license for undertaking work in more than one' state; the core-activity prohibition 'which was previously restricted in limited States like Telangana and Andhra Pradesh only'; the carve-out 'by excluding personnel who are regularly employed by, and are paid wages and provided benefits by, the contractor, from the ambit of contract labour'; and that the Code 'now places these obligations as the primary responsibility of the principal employer' with liability attaching to the principal employer where the contractor is unlicensed. One addition worth carrying: the guide notes three statutory exceptions to the core-activity bar (normal functioning ordinarily through a contractor; activities not requiring full-time workers for most hours; sudden volume increases), and that designated authorities decide what counts as a core activity — so the carve-out is less certain in practice than the claim implies.

verdicts.claim: Section 80JJAA is a proven cash subsidy for staffing firms; TeamLease received a ~Rs 115 crore refund under it
verdicts.issue: The TeamLease evidence is verified verbatim in the ICRA rating rationale on TeamLease Digital Private Limited dated 19 November 2024 (extracted locally after the fetch summariser failed): 'TSL received an Income Tax refund for AY 2023-24 pertaining to 80JJAA allowance, amounting to ~Rs. 115 crore (including interest of Rs. 6.5 crore) in H1 FY2025'; 'the income tax (IT) department has disallowed TSL's additional employee cost deduction for FY2019 under Section 80JJAA of the IT Act, 1961 and has issued a reassessment notice for FY2017'; and 'the company had outstanding income tax refunds of ~Rs. 240 crore as of September 30, 2024'. ICRA also records two favourable assessment orders for AY2021 and AY2022 allowing the deduction in full — a point in the provision's favour the claim omits. Two caveats: the Rs 240 crore is described by ICRA as outstanding income tax refunds generally, not specifically 80JJAA-related; and the statutory conditions themselves (30% of additional employee cost, three years, Rs 25,000 emoluments cap, 240 days, recognised PF, survival under 115BAA/115BAB) rest on ClearTax/Tax2win and were not verified against the Income-tax Act or a CBDT source.

verdicts.claim: Section 43B(h) gives a Udyam-registered micro or small supplier a hard lever on client payment terms
verdicts.issue: This is a tax-provision claim sourced only to ClearTax and taxupdate.in, neither of which is an official source, and I did not verify it against the Income-tax Act, a CBDT circular or the MSMED Act. Under the stated rule it must be marked unverifiable. Two substantive cautions for whoever verifies it: the practical leverage is weaker than the framing suggests, because s.43B(h) penalises the buyer's tax position rather than giving the supplier a direct payment remedy, and large buyers commonly respond by requiring vendors to declare non-micro/small status or by contracting on 45-day terms — so it rarely produces faster payment in practice. The claimed migration to section 37 under the Income-tax Act, 2025 should also be checked directly, as it changes the citation.

verdicts.claim: A minimum-service bond with liquidated damages is enforceable after the Supreme Court's May 2025 ruling
verdicts.issue: Verified against the judgment text on Indian Kanoon. Vijaya Bank v. Prashant B Narnaware, decided 14 May 2025: a three-year minimum-service clause with Rs 2 lakh liquidated damages, upheld; the Court allowed the Bank's appeal and set aside the High Court judgment that had quashed the clause; it held that restrictions operating during the period of the contract are not an unlawful restraint of trade under section 27 of the Contract Act, and rejected the public-policy challenge, finding the restriction reasonable given the bank's need to retain experienced staff. The finding's careful framing of the distinguishing facts is accurate and important: a public-sector bank, an internal candidate who applied through a recruitment notification disclosing the term upfront, a Senior Manager-Cost Accountant on a lucrative package, and damages actually paid. None of that resembles enforcement against an unemployed fresher, so the caution against over-reading it is well placed.

verdicts.claim: The Employment Linked Incentive scheme pays employers up to Rs 3,000/month per additional employee for two years
verdicts.issue: The cited official PIB press release returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on fetch, so I could not confirm any element: the Rs 99,446 crore outlay, the 1 July 2025 Cabinet approval, Part B's Rs 3,000 per month for two years with six months' sustained employment and the manufacturing extension to years 3 and 4, Part A's one month's EPF wage up to Rs 15,000 in two instalments at 6 and 12 months with the financial-literacy condition and the Rs 1 lakh earnings ceiling, or the 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027 window. This is a government scheme and a material subsidy to the business model, so it must be read in the original PIB release or the EPFO scheme guidelines before being built into a financial plan. The arithmetic point — that Rs 3,000/month is a large fraction of Rs 4,600-13,100 gross margin per head — is sound if the Rs 3,000 is confirmed.

verdicts.claim: At large Indian enterprises, buying contract IT talent is a two-stage process: win empanelment via open EOI, then bid in closed tenders
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in the SBI RFP (downloaded and extracted). The document is titled 'REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (CLOSED RFP) / LIMITED TENDER ENQUIRY' and states 'This is a closed RFP and participation in this RFP is by invitation only'. Eligibility criterion 1 reads 'The Bidder should be the Empaneled Bidder under the Category III pursuant to the EOI', with documentary requirement 'Copy of the Empanelment Letter issued by the Bank to be provided'. The scope confirms procurement 'for a period of two years, from 1st January 2026 to 31st December 2027 from the empaneled vendors as per the REQUEST FOR EMPANELMENT OF IT COMPANIES'. The conclusion that a non-empanelled vendor cannot bid at all, regardless of capability or price, follows directly from the text. This is the single most important go-to-market constraint verified in the set.

verdicts.claim: Once empanelled, IT staffing work is awarded by online reverse auction to the lowest bidder (L1)
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in the SBI RFP: Reverse Auction appears as a scheduled event; 'The Bidder will be selected as L1 on the basis of net total of the price evaluation as quoted in the Reverse Auction'; 'Among all qualified bids, the lowest bid (as quoted in reverse auction) will be termed as L1'; and shortlisted bidders 'shall be willing to participate in the reverse auction'. The conclusion that speed-to-deploy is not a scored commercial variable at this stage is correct. Two nuances worth carrying into the write-up rather than treating as errors: price competition runs only 'among all qualified bids', so technical qualification gates it; and the RFP applies a Make-in-India preference — 'If L1 is Class-I local supplier, the contract will be' awarded accordingly, with a fallback where L1 is not a Class-I local supplier — so L1 is not purely the lowest number.

verdicts.claim: Empanelment is a long-lived licence awarded in windows that open only every 2-5 years
verdicts.issue: The thesis is verified; one date is wrong. Confirmed: IDBI states 'The empanelment of the selected vendors is for five years from date of signing of LOI (Letter of Intent) with IDBI Bank', with yearly performance review and possible de-empanelment. Union Bank's ITCSSP empanelment runs 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2027. But PNB Cards & Services states 'The Empanelment will be for 03 (Three) Years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2029-30' — not FY 2028-29 as claimed. (The document is itself internally odd in naming four fiscal years for a three-year term, and it also gives bid validity as both 90 days and 180 days in different clauses.) The IDBI one-year extension was not separately located.
verdicts.corrected: IDBI: 'The empanelment of the selected vendors is for five years from date of signing of LOI', with yearly performance review and possible de-empanelment. Union Bank of India's ITCSSP empanelment runs 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2027 (two years). PNB Cards & Services: 'The Empanelment will be for 03 (Three) Years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2029-30.' A vendor that is not ready when the EOI is published waits years.

verdicts.claim: After empanelment, rates are discovered once then competed down via lowest-price, maximum-discount or nomination models
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in the IDBI RFP (downloaded via curl after a certificate-chain error blocked the normal fetch). The three models are exactly as claimed: the price model where 'The vendor quoting the lowest prices shall be selected'; 'Person-Days Model: For given N person-days or person-months, resource cost will be arrived based on the discovered prices through this RFP, say the cost is Y. Vendors will be asked to quote the discount percentage on Y in sealed cover. The vendor quoting the maximum discount on Y shall be selected'; and 'Nomination Model: For specific assignment/project/task or on urgent basis, IDBI Bank may select the vendor on nomination basis.' The document adds 'For all these models, the resource cost will be arrived based on the discovered prices through this RFP', which directly confirms the claim's conclusion that rate cards are set at empanelment and eroded thereafter.

verdicts.claim: Technical scoring matrices allocate ~43% of marks to counts of past assignments, penalising a vendor with no completed POs
verdicts.issue: Verified line by line in the Union Bank RFP's 150-mark scoring chart. Confirmed exactly: 25 marks for BFSI assignments in India at one mark per assignment/purchase order; 20 marks for BFSI assignments globally at two marks per PO; 20 marks for special information security incident assignments; 20 marks for three-year average turnover banded '8 to <50 Crore Turnover: 5 marks' through '>500 Crore: 20 Marks'; 15 marks for counts of certified L1/L2/L3 resources; 10 marks for years of experience; 10 for certifications/accreditations; 10 for technical skill credentials; 20 for technical presentation; 'Total Marks 150'. Shortlisting thresholds verbatim: 'Premium - Technical Score 75% and above' and 'Non-Premium - Technical score above 50% and below 75%'. The arithmetic holds: 25+20+20 = 65 of 150 = 43.3% on past-assignment counts, and a new vendor also scores the minimum 5-mark turnover band.
