The conclusion is the market's settled understanding and the consequence is worth modelling before any candidate-pay pricing is designed: a INR 60,000 Applied AI track costs the candidate INR 70,800, and because GST attaches to the gross fee whenever it is recognised, it changes the arithmetic of pay-after-placement and income-share structures specifically. Confirm with a GST adviser before launching any candidate-funded track.

verdicts.claim: EPF applies at 20 employees (INR 15,000 ceiling) and ESI at 10 (INR 21,000), coverage does not lapse if headcount falls, and both were restructured from 21 November 2025
verdicts.issue: Cited to a compliance site, an HR forum and a small consultancy. The ESI contribution rates referenced elsewhere in this set are officially confirmed, but these thresholds, the non-lapse rule and the stipend treatment are not. This substantially duplicates earlier EPF and ESI findings and should be consolidated. The two observations worth keeping are operational: a hire-train-deploy bench crosses the ESI trigger at ten people and the EPF trigger at twenty, well before material revenue; and because Anvi is employer of record for every deployed engineer, enterprise clients will make monthly ECR and ESI challans a condition of payment — which is consistent with the GeM bill-hold mechanics verified above.

verdicts.claim: Udyam registration turns the MSMED 45-day rule into a collections lever, because a late-paying client loses its income-tax deduction until it actually pays
verdicts.issue: The MSMED half is confirmed from the Ministry's own portal, which states a buyer who fails to pay within 45 days of acceptance 'is liable to pay compound interest with the monthly rests to the supplier on the amount at the three times of the bank rate notified by RBI', and that any micro or small enterprise with valid Udyam registration can apply. The Section 43B(h) half — the deduction-on-actual-payment mechanism that makes this a lever — was not verified against CBDT. One operational update the finding misses: the portal now directs all new delayed-payment applications to the MSME ODR Portal at odr.msme.gov.in.
verdicts.corrected: Registering on Udyam gives Anvi an enforceable claim under the MSMED Act 2006: payment is due within 45 days of acceptance and a defaulting buyer is liable for compound interest with monthly rests at three times the RBI bank rate, with disputes referred to the state MSEFC. New delayed-payment applications are now filed at the MSME ODR Portal (odr.msme.gov.in), not the Samadhaan portal. The Section 43B(h) effect — that the buyer gets its income-tax deduction only on actual payment — is the part that creates internal pressure inside the client's own finance team, and it was not verified against an official source; confirm it before relying on it in negotiation.

verdicts.claim: The only market statistic on Anvi's About page measures the data-annotation market, and the figure comes from a superseded edition of the report it cites
verdicts.issue: Both halves verify. anviinnovate.com/about cites 'USD 8.60 billion by 2030' at '21.9% CAGR (2025–2030)' attributed to Grand View Research, and the live Grand View Research page for that market now gives USD 3.2bn (2025), USD 3.9bn (2026) and USD 16.3bn by 2033 at 22.6% CAGR for 2026-2033, scoped by type to text, image/video and audio datasets — a dataset market, not a talent or staffing market. A buyer who clicks the citation finds a different market and a different number. One refinement: the finding describes the GVR scope as including 'labelling and annotation tooling, and synthetic data' as segments; synthetic data appears in the narrative but the published segmentation is by type, vertical and geography.

verdicts.claim: Anvi's core positioning line is near-identical to Andela's live homepage headline
verdicts.issue: Verified on both sites. Anvi uses 'The skilled human layer behind AI' as a homepage section heading and as the H1 on /about; Andela's homepage H1 is 'The Human Layer Powering Production AI', with supporting copy 'Andela provides the human compute layer behind modern AI systems'. Andela also occupies the adjacent ground with 17K certified AI-native engineers, 200K+ technologists trained and 98% enterprise client satisfaction. The collision is real, and Andela has the prior claim plus the proof assets to defend it.

verdicts.claim: The whole site is nine URLs with no insights, blog, resources or case study section
verdicts.issue: The sitemap contains exactly nine URLs — /, /clients, /services/hire-train-deploy, /about, /faq, /contact, /login, /privacy, /terms — with no lastmod dates, only location and priority. There is no surface that can place Anvi on a shortlist it is not already on. The TeamLease Digital and NLB Services comparison figures cited alongside were not re-verified in this session.

verdicts.claim: Only about 5% of business buyers are in-market at any one time, and a brand unknown before the process starts has very low odds
verdicts.issue: Not fetched. The 95:5 rule is widely attributed to Ehrenberg-Bass and the broad proposition is well accepted, but the specific supporting figures here — about 20% in-market across a full year, and 20-50% category-entry-point linkage even for market leaders — come to us through a podcast write-up rather than the research. The strategic implication is reinforced independently by the 6sense evidence verified below, which is better sourced and makes the same argument more precisely. Lead with that instead.

verdicts.claim: 95% of the time the winning vendor was already on the buyer's Day One shortlist, and the first vendor contacted wins roughly 80% of deals
verdicts.issue: Verified on 6sense's 2025 report page: 'Buyers choose from one of the four vendors on their Day One Shortlist 95% of the time'; the first-contacted vendor wins approximately 77-81% depending on survey wave; buyers evaluate an average of 5.1 vendors and contact about four. Sample is nearly 4,000 buyer responses plus 766 in a companion survey. This is the best-sourced strategic finding in the set, and its implication is correct: Anvi's hiring-request form captures demand it did not create, so getting onto the Day One list and being the first call are the only two levers that move win rate.

verdicts.claim: Buyers make first contact about 61% of the way through the journey, down from 69%, while cycles compressed from 11.3 to 10.1 months
verdicts.issue: All four figures verify on the same 6sense report page — point of first contact 61% in 2025 against 69% in 2024, roughly 6-7 weeks earlier, with average cycle length falling from 11.3 to 10.1 months and buyers still completing around 60% of evaluation independently. The report's own stated reason is directly actionable for Anvi: most vendor websites do not give buyers the clarity they want on pricing, security and capability, which forces contact rather than earning it.

verdicts.claim: 67% of B2B buyers prefer a rep-free buying experience and 45% used AI tools during a recent purchase, down from Gartner's earlier 75% figure
verdicts.issue: The two headline figures verify exactly — '67% of B2B buyers favor a rep-free experience' and '45% said they used artificial intelligence tools during a recent purchase' — as does the methodology of 646 buyers surveyed from August through September 2025, reported March 2026. But the article contains no comparison to an earlier 75% Gartner figure, so that element is not supported by the cited source and should be dropped or sourced separately.
verdicts.corrected: Gartner, in a survey of 646 buyers conducted August-September 2025 and reported March 2026, found 67% of B2B buyers favour a rep-free buying experience and 45% used AI tools during a recent purchase. The claimed decline from an earlier 75% Gartner figure is not in this source — drop it. The 45% AI-usage figure is the operative one for Anvi: an LLM answering 'who provides trained GenAI contract engineers in Hyderabad' can only cite what is published, and Anvi publishes nine thin pages with no numbers.

verdicts.claim: HBR's audit of 2,241 US companies found average response to a web lead was 42 hours and 23% never responded, so 'one business day' sits at the slow end of a 2011 baseline
verdicts.issue: Not fetched; the citation is to a university repository record rather than the article. The finding deserves credit for catching a real misattribution — the 21x-more-likely-to-qualify figure comes from the 2007 MIT/InsideSales study, not HBR — but it then builds an argument on 2011 data about US software lead response to judge an Indian staffing firm's 2026 commitment. Even if verified, the comparison is weak. The actionable point stands on its own: 'one business day' is the only numeric commitment Anvi publishes, and it is a slow one to publish as a differentiator.

verdicts.claim: Across 41,000+ landing pages the median conversion rate was 6.6% with a 3.8%-12.3% industry range, and readability beat most design choices
verdicts.issue: Not fetched. The readability correlations quoted (difficult words -24.3%, reading time -19.4%, word count -18.6%, and 5th-7th grade copy converting 11.1% versus 56% better than 8th-9th grade) are the basis for the copy critique elsewhere in this set, so they carry real weight and should be verified from the report rather than relied on second-hand. Note also that these are correlations in observational data across heterogeneous industries, not a controlled finding about staffing pages — treat them as a prompt to simplify Anvi's copy, not as a predicted uplift.

verdicts.claim: Staffing and recruiting visitor-to-lead conversion is commonly benchmarked at about 2.9%
verdicts.issue: The finding is already appropriately sceptical of itself — it names the source as marketing aggregators citing each other and states the original dataset was not locatable. That self-assessment is correct and the figure should not be used as a target. The arithmetic it supports is still a useful planning sanity check: at roughly 3%, a single form needs about 35 qualified visitors per enquiry, and the site currently has no traffic-generating content at all.

verdicts.claim: The evidence on form length is genuinely contested, so cutting Anvi's eight fields is not an automatic win
verdicts.issue: Not fetched; the supporting material is explicitly described as secondary summaries, and the counter-example Unbounce test is undated. This is the most intellectually honest finding in the set and its conclusion is the right one even though its evidence is weak — the claim being made is that the evidence is contested, which is a low bar to meet. The diagnosis is also correct and independently verifiable from the site: Anvi's problem is offer-value rather than field count, because the form is the only offer on the site.

verdicts.claim: The site has no first-party proof of any kind: no client logos, case studies, testimonials, founder bios, placement counts, bench size, fill rates or numeric SLAs
verdicts.issue: Verified directly across the homepage, /about and /services/hire-train-deploy. /about carries no founder or team names, no founding year, no company size and no registration details; the homepage and service page carry no pricing, client logos, case studies, testimonials or SLAs. The only quantified first-party claims anywhere are training-content counts and the one-business-day response promise. Footer legal surface is Privacy and Terms only. Against the 6sense and TrustRadius evidence verified above, this is the binding constraint on the site, not a cosmetic gap.

verdicts.claim: The hire-train-deploy page promises transparency rather than delivering it: 'What we publish up front' lists things shared only after contact
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim. The section reads: 'The commercial structure — pricing model (fixed monthly vs. markup), conversion terms, replacement window, and invoicing cycle — is shared before you commit. Rates are quoted per engagement based on skills and volume.' So a section headed 'What we publish up front' publishes none of the four items; nothing numeric — no price, percentage or SLA figure — appears anywhere on the page. The heading actively invites the comparison that defeats it.

verdicts.claim: Revature's homepage leads with 25,000+ engineers trained, 200+ enterprises, 15+ years, ~24 client logos, Brandon Hall and Stevie awards, and three named products
verdicts.issue: Not verified — only Revature's Emerging Talent Program page was fetched, which confirmed that page's programme claims but not the homepage counts, logo carousel, award citations or product split. Since this finding is being used as the competitive benchmark for the exact class of number Anvi omits, the homepage should be checked directly before it informs any positioning decision. The directional point is corroborated by the verified Andela and Toptal evidence below, which both lead with headcount and outcome percentages.

verdicts.claim: The best-converting talent-services sites pair named-client case studies carrying one headline metric each with named-executive testimonials and a third-party review score
verdicts.issue: Verified on Andela's homepage: named logos including Goldman Sachs, GitHub, SoFi, Capital One, Johnson & Johnson, Indeed, Coursera, WPP, Gopuff and Lattice (plus The Weather Company and Resy); three case studies each carrying a single metric (GitHub 3x reduced resolution times on 100K tickets, GoPuff 80% database uptime boost, SoFi 33% faster project delivery); a G2 score of 4.7 from 329 reviews; 98% enterprise client satisfaction; and a visible monthly rate band of $6,500-$8,500 on a sample profile. Minor correction: three named-executive testimonials were observed (ISG, Goldman Sachs, GitHub), not four.

verdicts.claim: Risk reversal and a numeric time-to-match are the two proof elements that most directly answer 'deploy in days', and Toptal shows them quantified
verdicts.issue: Verified on Toptal's homepage: 98% trial-to-hire success rate, 'Average time to match is under 24 hours', 'Hire in under 48 hours', 35,000+ clients served, 140+ countries, 4.9 out of 5 from 42,822 reviews, Newsweek #1 most reliable professional services company in America, named clients including Bridgestone, Cleveland Cavaliers and Zoetis, and explicit risk reversal in 'pay only if satisfied'. Minor corrections: USC was not among the named clients observed (Precision Drilling, CSR and Big Sur AI appear instead), and the Newsweek ranking is the 2026 edition. The contrast holds exactly — Anvi makes a comparable speed claim with no number and no risk reversal.

verdicts.claim: India staffing incumbents compete on scale counts and compliance credentials, not logos or pricing, leaving verifiable operational numbers available as differentiation
verdicts.issue: Neither TeamLease Digital's nor NLB Services' homepage was fetched in this session, so the specific claims — 150,000+ associates, 450 clients, 150+ cities, <5% attrition, 200+ recruiters, six CTAs, and NLB's outcome-metric case studies and seven trust badges including ISO, SOC 2 Type 2 and PCI DSS — are unverified. The strategic inference is attractive and worth testing, but it rests entirely on an unverified reading of two competitor sites and should be confirmed before it shapes positioning.

verdicts.claim: The homepage headline and subheadline say the same thing twice, and the stack list is written for an ML engineer rather than the hiring manager
verdicts.issue: The jargon half verifies — the Skills & tech stack section lists 'Evals & LLM-as-judge', 'Fine-tuning (LoRA→DPO)', 'Hybrid search & reranking' and 'Agents & MCP' among fourteen items. But the duplication half is now stale: as fetched on 7 October 2026 the H1 is 'On-demand, trained AI/ML talent — ready for immediate deployment' and the subheadline is 'Applied-AI, GenAI and ML-trained fresh graduates, ready for your team. Tell us your requirement and we deploy in days, not months.' Those are no longer the same sentence twice. The site has changed since the brief was written.
verdicts.corrected: The homepage H1 now reads 'On-demand, trained AI/ML talent — ready for immediate deployment' with a differentiated subheadline ('Applied-AI, GenAI and ML-trained fresh graduates, ready for your team. Tell us your requirement and we deploy in days, not months.'), so the headline duplication described in the brief has been fixed. The jargon problem remains: the Skills & tech stack section still lists 'Evals & LLM-as-judge', 'Fine-tuning (LoRA→DPO)', 'Hybrid search & reranking' and 'Agents & MCP' — written for an ML engineer, not the hiring manager who signs the contract.

verdicts.claim: The Indian staffing market is growing about 12% year on year driven substantially by Global Capability Centres, the segment Anvi's messaging never names
verdicts.issue: The Indian Staffing Federation homepage was not fetched, so the 12% YoY figure and its attribution to GCC demand are unverified. The GCC half of the argument is however strongly corroborated from primary sources verified elsewhere in this set — Quess's Q1 FY27 deck shows GCC at 71% of professional staffing headcount and 68% of revenue, and ICRA names GCC demand as the driver of TeamLease's 28% H1 FY2026 specialised-staffing growth. The verifiable observation needs no market-growth statistic: Anvi is based in a major GCC hub and its site never uses the word GCC.

verdicts.claim: The correct denominator is India's IT staffing segment at INR 260bn, forecast to reach INR 546bn
verdicts.issue: Verified in the Frost & Sullivan report prepared for FirstMeridian's IPO (January 2023): 'The IT Staffing Solutions Segment market is estimated to be INR 260 billion in FY 2022. The segment has recorded a CAGR of 17.8% from FY 2016 – FY 2020... From FY 2022 – FY2026 the IT Staffing Solutions segment market is forecast to grow at a CAGR of 20.4% to reach INR 546.0 billion.' Two cautions: the cited URL is SEBI's generic public-issues index, not the document, so the citation as given does not lead a reader to the evidence; and FY2026 has now closed, so the INR 546bn figure is a lapsed forecast that should be replaced with an actual or clearly labelled as a 2023 projection.

verdicts.claim: IT staffing in India is a commodity long tail: over 2,000 staffing companies compete and 83.4% of IT staffing share sits outside the named players
verdicts.issue: Verified in the same report: 'The competitive landscape is highly fragmented in India, with more than 2000 companies operating in this market. The organized market consists of 20-30 companies'; 'Others' holds 83.4% of the IT Staffing segment in FY2022; and the attribution is verbatim — 'High growth witnessed by the segment in the last decade and low entry barriers have resulted in a large base of small to medium companies and this has resulted in a highly competitive market.' The Quess 4.6% IT-staffing share figure could not be read cleanly from the chart. The conclusion is fair: a site with no pricing, logos, case studies or placement numbers is indistinguishable from the 83.4%.

verdicts.claim: TeamLease and Quess run near-zero working capital because they pre-collect salaries — a structural advantage Anvi cannot replicate in IT staffing
verdicts.issue: Confirmed from primary sources. ICRA's November 2024 rationale states TeamLease adopts the Collect and Pay model for '~87% of general staffing revenues in FY2024', wherein salaries 'are collected in advance and are paid to them', and attributes the low working capital intensity and reduced bad-debt risk to it; the January 2026 rationale repeats this for the majority of revenues. Quess's Q1 FY27 deck shows General Staffing Collect & Pay at 75-77% and GS DSO at 28 days with AR stable at 15 days. The working capital days (-2/+3/+3) and debtor days of 16-18 attributed to Screener.in were not verified. The conclusion holds: a new IT-staffing entrant gets none of this float.

verdicts.claim: Bank and PSU vendor panels are invitation-only and structurally closed to a firm with no track record — SBI's IT-manpower RFP will not accept an unsolicited bid
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim from the RFP (ref SBI/CC/DB&T/DB&T-BUSINESS/YB/Closed_RFP/2025-26/01 dated 01/12/2025, contract 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2027): 'This is a closed RFP and participation in this RFP is by invitation only and is limited to the selected vendors. Unsolicited bids will not be considered by the Bank.' Eligibility criterion 1 requires the bidder to already be 'the Empaneled Bidder under the Category III pursuant to the EOI', and the Third-Party Components row reads 'Not Applicable (No Outsourcing allowed)' — so the subcontracting route is closed too. The RFP was emailed only to bidders empanelled under two earlier EOIs from 2023 and 2024.

verdicts.claim: BFSI security empanelment requires 10 years of existence, INR 8 crore turnover for three years and 30 certified permanent employees
verdicts.issue: Verified in Union Bank of India's RFP (UBI/ITCSSP/NOVEMBER/2024, panel period 01.04.2025-31.03.2027): existence 'for last 10 years as on 30.09.2024'; current CERT-In empanelment as an Information Security Auditing Organization; 'minimum annual turnover of Rs.8 Crores during the last three financial years (i.e. 2021-22, 2022-23 & 2023-24)', individual company not group; 'minimum 30 permanent employees as on 30.09.2024. Out of 30, 5 employees should mandatorily have either of the CISA/CISM/CISSP certification'; BFSI assignments of 'minimum 15 Man-Days'. The scoring confirms the trap — the 8-to-under-50 crore turnover band scores 5 marks against 20 for above INR 500 crore. The positive-EBITDA requirement was not separately located.

verdicts.claim: State government manpower empanelment demands 500+ contractual placements and 20+ client organisations already delivered — a catch-22 for a pre-revenue entrant
verdicts.issue: Every criterion verifies in Gujarat Informatics Limited's RFP (P&A 201718/04): 5 years' existence, valid ISO certification, INR 1 crore manpower-specific turnover in each of three years with a CA certificate stating 'Turnover from providing manpower', a labour licence for at least 100 manpower in a single government work order, a local office for two years, '500 plus contractual manpower... during last 2 years... out of which at least 250 manpower in Govt./Semi Govt. sector', 20 organisations of which 10 government/PSU, PF/ESI/Professional Tax registrations, and '2.2.1 Any kind of consortium will not be allowed.' It also requires Employment Exchange registration, which the finding omits. The problem is currency: this is a 2017 tender with turnover years FY2014-15 to FY2016-17, cited to a live tender-index URL where it no longer sits.
verdicts.corrected: Gujarat Informatics Limited's 2017 manpower empanelment RFP (P&A 201718/04) required 5 years' existence, valid ISO certification, INR 1 crore of CA-certified manpower turnover in each of three years, a labour licence for 100+ manpower in a single government work order, a local office for two years, 500+ contractual placements in two years including 250 to government, supply to 20+ organisations including 10 government/PSU, Employment Exchange registration, and PF/ESI/PT registrations, with 'Any kind of consortium will not be allowed'. Treat this as an illustration of the catch-22 pattern, not a current requirement — the tender is nine years old, predates the Labour Codes entirely, and is no longer on the cited tender index. Obtain a live state empanelment notice before planning against these thresholds.

verdicts.claim: Vendor panels refresh on roughly two-year cycles, so missing an empanelment window costs up to two years of access
verdicts.issue: Supported by two independently verified primary documents: SBI's IT-HR contract runs 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2027, and Union Bank's ITCSSP empanelment runs 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2027 with the RFP issued in November 2024, about five months before the period opened. The Gujarat 27-month performance-guarantee element rests on a nine-year-old tender and adds little. The conclusion is sound and strategically important: elapsed time to a first PSU or bank client is governed by when the next EOI window opens, not by sales effort — so the empanelment calendar is the thing to track, not the pipeline.

verdicts.claim: Where public-sector panels open, price is discovered by reverse auction or forced L1 matching, destroying the markup that funds a training bench
verdicts.issue: Verified in both documents. SBI defines the winner as the bidder 'who has emerged as L1 (lowest in reverse auction)', holds the reverse-auction price valid for six months, and makes EMD forfeitable where 'a technically qualified Bidder do not participate in the auction by not logging in'. Gujarat's clause 2.4.4 computes an Average Bid Price, disqualifies bids 'less or more than 50% of the Average Bid Price', derives L1, then gives 'L2, L3, L4, L5,......other bidders... the option to match L1 rates and get empaneled', and disqualifies any bidder whose service charge falls 'below the rate of TDS applicable to them' — confirming markups are quoted in low single digits. A model carrying pre-deployment training cost cannot fund itself at these rates.

verdicts.claim: GCCs, not Indian IT services firms, are where specialised staffing demand sits — 71% of Quess's professional staffing headcount and 68% of revenue
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in Quess Corp's Q1 FY27 investor presentation (quarter ended 30 June 2026): 'GCC contributing 71% of headcount with 68% of revenue contribution', with IT/ITeS at 7% of headcount in the same quarter. ICRA separately confirms GCC demand as the growth driver for TeamLease's specialised staffing, which grew 28% YoY in H1 FY2026 after 1% in FY2025. This is the best-evidenced strategic finding in the commercial set, and the implication is correct: Anvi is in a major GCC hub and a hiring-request form is not a GCC engineering-manager acquisition channel.

verdicts.claim: The realistic unit economics benchmark is ~INR 1.18 lakh per deployed head per month at ~11% EBITDA, leaving ~INR 13,000 of operating profit
verdicts.issue: Confirmed by arithmetic from Quess's Q1 FY27 disclosure: Professional Staffing revenue INR 252 crore, EBITDA INR 28 crore (11.1%), exit headcount 7,129 — giving INR 1,17,830 of revenue and INR 13,090 of EBITDA per head per month. The deck also states 'Gross margin to EBITDA margin conversion remains above 50%', consistent with the implied ~22% segment gross margin. The framing is the important part and is correct: these are the margins available to India's largest domestic player at 7,129 deployed heads, before any pre-deployment training cost is carried.

verdicts.claim: Anvi's niche is right on margin: skilled professional staffing is 1.5% of Quess's headcount but 28% of group EBITDA
verdicts.issue: Verified from the segment table: General Staffing ~469,000 heads (97%), INR 3,596 crore revenue (86%), INR 51 crore EBITDA (51%); Professional Staffing 7,129 heads (1.5%), INR 252 crore revenue (6%), INR 28 crore EBITDA (28%). The per-head comparison checks out — roughly INR 362 of EBITDA per head per month in general staffing against INR 13,090 in professional staffing, about 36x. The finding's own closing caveat is the honest one and should be carried forward: the strategic logic of a skills-led bench is sound, but whether a fresher bench reaches the skill bar that commands that rate is the open question — and the next finding suggests it does not.

verdicts.claim: Demand is concentrated in niche and senior roles, not freshers: India's largest staffing player carries 1,100+ unfilled mandates 'primarily in niche and high value roles'
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in Quess's Q1 FY27 deck: 'Open mandates at 1,100+ primarily in niche and high value roles', alongside 36 contracts added in the quarter and professional staffing headcount growth of just 7% YoY. The Frost & Sullivan corroboration is also verbatim: 'Most of the IT jobs outsourced in the past 4-5 years were at the entry level which included programmers, software engineers, system administrators etc. Recently, IT companies have started to outsource mid-level and senior positions too.' This is the central risk to the fresher-bench thesis and it is well evidenced — unmet demand sits above the experience band a trained fresh graduate occupies.

verdicts.claim: New-logo acquisition is slow even for incumbents: TeamLease's new customer additions fell from 460 in FY2024 to 139 in FY2025
verdicts.issue: Both figures verify in ICRA's rationales. November 2024: 'The company added 460 new customers in FY2024 and 365 in H1 FY2025'. January 2026: 'It added 139 new customers in FY2025', against a base of over 4,000 clients. Quess's Q1 FY27 deck confirms the comparators — 86 new General Staffing contracts and 36 Professional Staffing contracts in the quarter, with 700+ recruiters, 30+ offices across India and ~50,000+ gross monthly onboardings. The conclusion follows: a single-CTA website with no references is not a pipeline mechanism at this competitive intensity.

verdicts.claim: Attrition of a deployed engineer is contractually punitive: 45 days notice, 200% candidate ratio and a month of unpaid knowledge transfer
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in SBI's RFP. No substitution within 3 months of joining except death, medical incapacity or the person leaving the service provider; where substitution follows the resource leaving, 'a notice period of 45 (forty-five) days along with CVs of a minimum 200%... of total number of resource(s) to be substituted'; '(Substitution for a resource is allowed maximum up to 2 times)'; the replacement must be placed 'at least one month before the date of the discharge'; the outgoing resource 'shall be required to provide knowledge transfer as per job card for at least a month'; and 'The Bank will not make payment for the substitution resource during transition and knowledge transfer period.' Absence or lateness without approval is deducted at 'twice the rate per hour per resource' pro rata.

verdicts.claim: Overclaiming candidate readiness is directly punished: the client interviews every resource, its decision is final, and an unsatisfactory hire is unpaid
verdicts.issue: Verified verbatim in SBI's RFP: 'the interview of the resources before joining and thereafter on replacements /addition will be done by the Bank and the decision of Bank to onboard the resource will be final and binding on the Service Provider'; unsuitability communicated within 2 working days with 'additional CVs within 3 (three) working days', failing which the Bank 'may cancel the PO in whole or in part'; 'In case the resource is not found satisfactory within 15 (fifteen) days of joining, the Bank may ask for replacement of such resource and no payment shall be made for the period'; and any upskilling 'shall be taken up by the Service Provider and no cost shall be borne by the Bank'. The timeline contradiction with 'deploy in days' is also confirmed — shortlisted resources report within 15 days, BGC within 7 days of boarding, police verification within 90 days.

verdicts.claim: The Labour Codes came into force in their entirety on 21 November 2025 with no transition period, and the OSH Code now bans contract labour in clients' core activities nationwide
verdicts.issue: The cited law-firm guide supports almost every element verbatim — notifications of 21 November 2025 read with a corrigendum of 19 December 2025, Codes in force 'in their entirety' with 29 central laws repealed, 'the implementing notifications do not provide for any transitional period', the core-activity prohibition now nationwide 'which was previously restricted in limited States like Telangana and Andhra Pradesh only', exceptions whose application 'is left to the designated authorities', welfare obligations as the principal employer's primary responsibility, work-specific and national licences, and the unified 50-worker threshold. Two problems: the cited URL is the firm's homepage rather than the guide, and no government source could be reached. Critically, the same guide contains the exclusion this finding omits — personnel regularly employed and paid wages and benefits by the contractor are outside 'contract labour' altogether.
verdicts.corrected: Law-firm commentary states all four Codes came into force on 21 November 2025 (with a corrigendum of 19 December 2025 that also repealed the EPF Act 1952 in full), with no transitional period, and that the OSH Code now prohibits contract labour in principal employers' core activities nationwide subject to three exceptions assessed by designated authorities. But the same source records that the Code excludes from 'contract labour' personnel 'regularly employed by, and are paid wages and provided benefits by, the contractor' — so engineers on Anvi's payroll with statutory benefits may sit outside the regime and outside the core-activity ban. No government source was reachable to verify any of this; obtain a written opinion on the classification question before redesigning the model.

verdicts.claim: Labour-code compliance is already moving real money and the RBI is shrinking the contract-staffing addressable market in BFSI
verdicts.issue: Both halves verify from primary sources. Quess's Q1 FY27 deck states 'One time increase in revenue of 176 crs due to labor code impact' in General Staffing. ICRA's January 2026 rationale confirms the regulatory contraction twice, verbatim: TeamLease's 'headcount in the BFSI segment was impacted to a certain extent in H1 FY2026 on account of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) directive limiting use of contract employees in certain roles for BFSI players', and 'new regulations from the RBI have directly reduced the number of roles available for being outsourced from BFSI players to staffing companies across FY2025 and H1 FY2026'. The warning is well founded: any plan leaning on BFSI demand is leaning into a shrinking permitted scope.

verdicts.claim: Delayed payment to small suppliers is systemic — 256,892 MSME applications involving INR 31,693.73 crore — but MSMED gives a 45-day enforceable claim plus penal interest
verdicts.issue: The figures are all on the official portal but the finding couples two that belong to different rows. The portal shows 2,56,892 'Applications filed by MSEs' and, separately, 1,12,974 MSEFC 'Cases Filed' with INR 31,693.73 crore 'Amount Payable' and 67,356 cases disposed involving INR 10,472.60 crore. So the INR 31,693.73 crore attaches to the 112,974 cases, not the 256,892 applications. The ~88,000 pending figure checks out (43,363 awaiting first view plus 44,638 under consideration). The legal provision verifies verbatim: compound interest 'with the monthly rests... at the three times of the bank rate notified by RBI' where payment is not made within 45 days of acceptance. The portal also now redirects new filings to odr.msme.gov.in.
verdicts.corrected: MSME Samadhaan shows 2,56,892 applications filed by micro and small enterprises, and separately 1,12,974 cases filed before MSE Facilitation Councils involving INR 31,693.73 crore payable, of which 67,356 cases (INR 10,472.60 crore) are disposed and roughly 88,000 remain pending or unviewed. Do not attribute the INR 31,693.73 crore to the 256,892 applications — they are different rows. Under the MSMED Act a buyer failing to pay within 45 days of acceptance is liable for compound interest with monthly rests at three times the RBI bank rate. New delayed-payment applications are now filed at the MSME ODR Portal. The portal prints no as-of date.

verdicts.claim: Anvi cannot legally stop a deployed engineer from joining the client; post-employment non-competes are void, so the only protection is a conversion fee in the client contract
verdicts.issue: The cited Indian Kanoon search URL is a query string, not a judgment, and none of the four cases named (FLSmidth, Independent News Service, International Design, Wipro v. Beckman Coulter) was verified. The Section 27 position on post-employment non-competes is settled and uncontroversial; the enforceability of non-solicitation is more contested than a list of favourable citations suggests. This duplicates an earlier finding and should be merged with it. The design conclusion is sound and does not depend on the case law: recover the training investment through a priced conversion or buyout fee agreed with the client, not through restraints on the engineer.

verdicts.claim: The live site no longer matches the brief — it now cites four talent-market statistics and the Grand View Research dataset figure was not present
verdicts.issue: The central assertion is false. Fetching anviinnovate.com on 7 October 2026 shows the Grand View Research figure still on the homepage — 'USD 8.60 billion by 2030' at '21.9% CAGR (2025–2030)' — and it is also still the only market statistic on /about. The four newer statistics (62% AI wage premium per PwC 2026, 90% of developers using AI per DORA 2025, four of five fastest-growing US roles per LinkedIn 2026, +25% India AI/ML hiring per Naukri JobSpeak June 2026) have been added alongside it, not in place of it. So the brief's criticism of the dataset-market citation stands and has not been remedied. The rest of this finding is accurate: 'Request talent' is the only CTA, and there is no pricing, case study, testimonial, client logo, founder bio, placement number or SLA beyond the one-business-day response promise.
